News.title: Dad-of-two, 48, ‘died with wife in Spanish villa hot tub after suction pump fault’ before kids found parents in water
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

HOT TUB TRAGEDY Dad-of-two, 48, ‘died with wife in Spanish villa hot tub after suction pump fault’ before kids found parents in water

A DAD who died alongside his wife after getting trapped inside a hot tub on a Spanish holiday with their family has been pictured.

Patrick Tobin, 48, and Thomasina Tobin, 51, were found by their teenage children after reportedly being killed more than 12 hours earlier.



The family were enjoying a trip abroad inside a large hilltop property in Cullera near the east coast Spanish city of Valencia.

The children, aged 14 and 16, were sleeping in their top-floor bedrooms unaware of the tragedy that had occurred in the ground-floor Jacuzzi.



Police are continuing to investigate the “chain accident” tragedy involving New Zealand-born Patrick and Irish quantity surveyor Thomasina.

Initial investigations point towards the couple dying after being caught in the water due to “suction entrapment”.



The rare phenomenon occurs when a powerful vacuum is created from a hot tub drain or swimming pool and traps a person’s body, hair, or clothing underwater.

Investigators believe Patrick tried to save his wife as she struggled in the water.



Officers are focusing on the theory the supposed technical fault then led to the couple being electrocuted, local paper Las Provincias reports.

Post-mortem examinations found marks and scratches on both bodies as well as blood in the cloudy water of the hot tub.

Foul play has been ruled out as there were no signs of forced entry and nearby CCTV cameras didn’t show any suspicious signs.



The family arrived at the luxury £2,000-a-week Villa Luna on August 22 for a two-week holiday.

They are tragically believed to have died just two days into the trip before being found on Tuesday, August 25.

Thomasina was a chartered surveyor from Co Monaghan, Ireland but had been living in London for around 20 years.

Her father is well-known playwright, actor and producer Tommy McArdle, who spent many years directing Irish drama Glenroe.

News.title: Hospital patient charged after ‘exposing himself & sexually assaulting staff’
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

PATIENT PROBE Hospital patient charged after ‘exposing himself & sexually assaulting staff’

A HOSPITAL patient allegedly exposed himself and sexually assaulted a staff member.

Police were called to Queen’s Medical Centre in Nottinghamshire on August 25 following reports a man had exposed himself.

On arrival, officers were also informed the same person had inappropriately touched a staff member.

Colin Worley, 58, has been charged with one count of sexual assault and two counts of exposure.





He appeared at Nottingham Magistrates’ Court last Saturday (August 29) and was remanded in custody.

He is due to appear at Nottingham Crown Court on September 26.

PC Joseph Jacks, of Nottinghamshire Police, said: “We will always take any report of sexual assault, or violence against women and girls, extremely seriously.

“In this case, officers arrived within minutes of receiving the report and, within two days, secured an arrest, charge and court appearance.

“We would like to thank the victim for her bravery and reassure the public that we are here to listen.

“We will investigate every report we receive and do everything in our power to secure justice for victims.”

News.title: Man, 27, arrested after ‘indecent act’ in parked van outside train station in broad daylight
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

'INDECENT ACT' Man, 27, arrested after ‘indecent act’ in parked van outside train station in broad daylight

A MAN has been arrested after an alleged indecent act while sitting in a parked van outside a train station.

The incident, in a Transit van, took place near the entrance to Ashford International in Kent at around 4.10pm on August 24.

A 27-year-old man was arrested and has since been released on bail pending further enquiries.

Investigators are urging any witnesses to come forward.





Kent Police said: “Officers are appealing for witnesses to come forward following an arrest for indecent behaviour in Ashford.

“It was reported that at around 4.10pm on Monday 24 August 2026, a man carried out an indecent act while sat in a parked white Transit van at

the junction of Newtown Road and the entrance to the Ashford International car park.

“Detectives arrested a 27 year old man from Ashford in connection with the incident.

“He has since been released on bail pending further enquiries.”



Anyone who witnessed the incident or has information regarding it, should contact Kent Police on 01843 222289 quoting 46/140371/26.

News.title: Coke dealer who thinks he’s doppelganger of James Bond star was snared by cops after posting on Strava
News.content:
LAST LAP Coke dealer who thinks he’s doppelganger of James Bond star was snared by cops after posting on Strava

A COKE dealer who claimed he looked like James Bond was snared by cops after revealing his location by posting a jog on Strava.

Andrew Doran, 42, was part of an audacious plot to smuggle a whopping 172kg of cocaine into the country hidden in gas canisters.



He thought he bore a resemblance to the iconic 007 secret agent when sharing his supposed doppelganger on social media.

But Doran turned out to be no James Bond, and was caught by police hiding out in Spain after he posted a jogging route on the fitness app Strava under an alias.



The details of the route in Estepona, Spain helped the National Crime Agency track the apparent wannabe secret agent down to his Iberian hideout.

He was arrested in Spain and then extradited to the UK in October last year.

Doran, from Kirkby in Merseyside, admitted to drugs importation charges at Newcastle Crown Court in December.

Last week he was sentenced to 18 years in prison.



Doran had pleadeed guilty to his part in smuggling the huge quantities of coke from the Netherlands to the UK.

The court heard that the drugs were packed into gas canisters.

Twelve of the canisters were collected from locations in Chatham, Kent, Corby and Northampton and Peterborough between October 2019 and April 2020.

Each bottle was packed with up to 16 kilos of coke, with 172kg seized in total.

Doran commanded international criminals in the Netherlands and Kevin Taylor, 44, from Newcastle upon Tyne, to orchestrate the plot.



He also gave orders to Taylor to shift huge amounts of cash from drug sales from the North East to the South and abroad.

Taylor was sentenced to 27 years behind bars in September last year.

Another foiled plot of Doran’s saw him arrange the importation of 42 kilos of cocaine from the Netherlands between March and June 2020.

The combined street value of both schemes was estimated at £18million.

NCA branch commander Gavin Heckles sent a warning to other Brits on the run abroad that they are “not beyond our reach”.



He said: “Andrew Doran had a central role in this plot, telling criminal associates at home and overseas how the drugs should be transported and distributed once in the UK.

“His extradition shows that criminals living in Spain are not beyond our reach, and we will never relent in securing justice.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Class A drugs like cocaine cause huge amounts of harm to communities across the UK, and create violence and exploitation at every level.

“We will continue to work with partners at home and abroad to pursue the criminal networks behind this trade and protect the public.”

News.title: Three dead & 6 injured including 3 cops after shooter opened fire as FBI deployed to deadly rampage in Minneapolis
News.content:
AT LEAST three people are dead with six others injured after a lone gunman opened fire at an apartment block in Minneapolis.

The suspected shooter is among those killed during the deadly rampage with three police officers being rushed to hospital after the shootout.



Cops rushed to control the active shooter situation on Wednesday just after 4.30pm after a 911 call reported multiple gunshots.

Within two minutes, officers had managed to breach a block of flats and quickly found multiple people with serious injuries, Interim Police Chief Bill Peterson said.



One of the victims was pronounced dead at the scene from a gunshot wound as another died after arriving at hospital.

Hero cops reportedly located the suspected shooter inside an upper-floor flat near 15 East Grant Street where gunfire continued to ring out.

Read More in World News KILLER'S RAMPAGE Moment fast food staff scramble for cover as mass shooter fires into store

One Minneapolis police officer was shot in the leg and another was hit twice in the abdomen.

A third also suffered unknown injuries, according to police Sgt. Garrett Parten.



All three injured officers are expected to make a full recovery.

Another three people were found injured at the scene and taken away for treatment.

The unidentified shooter was also found dead.

It is unknown if he was killed during the firefight or if he took his own life.

Police Chief Peterson said: “I’m truly sickened by this level of violence.



“That feeling is tempered only by the courageous actions of the Minneapolis police officers, who responded without hesitation, confronted an extraordinarily dangerous situation and worked to end the violence and restore safety.”

FBI director Kash Patel offered his full support to Minneapolis during the first reports of the shooting.

He said: “The FBI is aware of the shooting in Minneapolis involving law enforcement and our personnel are responding — we will offer any and all resources necessary to assist local authorities.”



Two men were shot and killed at the same apartment building last year.

Building resident Umecua Agnew told the Star Tribune the shooting was “terrifying”.

She was in the lift when the shooting began, and said: “It was three adults and one child in the elevator, we were all together and when we got to the first floor it was when we heard the massive shooting.”

Umecua ran and hid in the bathroom before another resident helped her flee.

She said: “I just thank God for being alive because that could have been me or he could have killed another girl or her mom or anybody that could have got shot right there.”



Minnesota Governor Tim Walz said state officials remain on the ground at the scene of the shooting.

He added: “Grateful to law enforcement actively working to ensure the safety of our neighbors in Downtown Minneapolis this afternoon.

“Minnesota is praying for our first responders.”

People have been asked to avoid the area from 12th Street to Franklin Avenue and Hennepin Avenue to Third Avenue South, with the Hyatt Regency hotel on lockdown.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Minnesota House Speaker Lisa Demuth said she is “praying for the victims of this heinous crime”.



She wrote on social media: “I’m incredibly thankful for the massive response of our brave law enforcement officers.”

News.title: Burnham’s 70s-style Socialism and big-state agenda are a toxic mix designed to deliver only economic ruin
News.content:
Road to ruin

Andy Burnham is so wedded to 1970s-style Socialism that he appears to have no clue how economic growth actually works.

Despite all the evidence from history, our Bus Conductor-in-Chief remains determined to let the dead hand of the State throttle all aspects of our lives.



It is a terrifying misunderstanding of how modern economies work.

Governments DON’T create growth, they can only summon up the best conditions for it. That should mean the State getting out of the way and freeing individuals and businesses to invest.



But yet again the PM and his deputy Louise Haigh told MPs they would deliver the very opposite: public control of energy, housing and water, plus a costly programme of devolution.

The problem for them and Chancellor John Healey is that for a second day running, the markets simply weren’t buying it.



They sent the cost of Government borrowing to the highest level in 28 years, blowing a £14billion hole in the nation’s finances.

Burnham still insists that tackling the cost of living is his top priority.

But how does he square that with the fact that Labour’s addiction to welfare and spending is guaranteeing interest rate spikes, food price surges and tax rises that clobber working families?

As for creating the best platform for growth, Net Zero has saddled Britain with the highest electricity costs in the world, making the PM’s plans for “reindustrialisation” a pipe dream.



National Insurance and business rates have crippled businesses and left a million young people jobless.

That’s a toxic left-wing mix designed to deliver only economic ruin.

Firing blanks

Yesterday Andy Burnham told MPs he would commit to spending 3 per cent of GDP on defence — only for Downing Street to later insist it wasn’t confirmed.

While he dithered, Kemi Badenoch’s Tories have a sensible alternative plan: re-introducing the two-child benefit cap to cut the welfare bill and ditching the Chagos Islands giveaway.

As Kemi rightly says, a country that spends more on benefits than bullets is guaranteeing its own surrender.



Deal is sunk

Whether or not the hopeless “one in, one out” migrant deal with France is scrapped, it will make no meaningful difference to stopping the boats.

Britain remains a magnet for young men from countries who don’t share our culture or values but want to exploit a system offering free housing, welfare, health and other benefits.

Small deals with the French are no substitute for what we really need: a Rwanda-style return scheme.

News.title: King Charles and Macron share a joke as they view the Bayeux Tapestry together at the British Museum
News.content:
King Charles and Emmanuel Macron try to show there is no needle between Britain and France as they view the Bayeux Tapestry together.

His Majesty and the French president enjoyed a joke while walking the artwork’s 230ft length at the British Museum yesterday.



The 950-year-old masterpiece, which depicts the 1066 Battle of Hastings and Norman Conquest, is in the UK temporarily in an act of diplomacy agreed after Mr Macron’s State Visit to Windsor Castle last year.

The King hailed it as an “unprecedented loan”.



Charles, Camilla, Mr Macron and his wife Brigitte viewed the work along with PM Andy Burnham and his wife Marie-France van Heel.

They paused at key points along the 11th century artwork to hear from curators about the historic moments depicted.

They included King Harold’s death after supposedly being shot in the eye at Hastings.

Charles, speaking later in both French and English at the London museum, said the tapestry is a reminder “that our two nations have been bound together for almost a millennium”.



He said that although the artwork depicts a conflict, “here it is today, nearly a thousand years later, as a precious symbol of trust, at a time when trust seems sadly to be in short supply between nations”.

He added those involved in it would be “pleased our two great nations have prospered together across the tides of history”.

The tapestry is on display from September 10 to next July, and tickets until December 31 — costing up to £33 — are already sold out.

Britain is sending the treasures of Sutton Hoo to France in return.

News.title: Woman fighting for life after being shot with air rifle as man, 28, and woman, 26, arrested for ‘attempted murder’
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

STREET SHOOTING Woman fighting for life after being shot with air rifle as man, 28, and woman, 26, arrested for ‘attempted murder’

COPS have arrested three people after a woman was left fighting for her life after reportedly being shot with an air rifle.

The victim was rushed to hospital with serious injuries following the alleged horror attack yesterday evening.

Police were called to Windsor Street in Thurnscoe, near Barnsley, at around 9.50pm yesterday after reports of a person with a suspected firearm.

It was reported that a woman had been shot with an air rifle.





Officers and ambulance crews raced to the scene and the woman was taken to hospital for treatment.

She suffered serious injuries and remains in hospital in a stable but life-threatening condition.

Cops recovered an air rifle from the scene before launching a search for the suspect.

A 26-year-old woman was arrested at the scene on suspicion of attempted murder.



She remains in custody.

Then today, cops arrested two more people as the investigation continued.

A 28-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of attempted murder.

A 37-year-old man was also arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender.



Both men remain in police custody.

A police scene remains in place on Windsor Street as detectives continue their investigation.

DI Claire Moss, from the Armed Crime Team, said: “The thoughts of all those involved in this investigation remain with the victim and her family in the wake of such a vicious attack.

“I am thankful for the work of the first officers at the scene and emergency services staff who attended the scene and provided essential and immediate medical care to the victim.

“We are carrying out detailed inquiries to get a better understanding of the circumstances which resulted in the victim being seriously injured.



“If you saw what happened yesterday evening, or have any information which may assist our enquiries, please get in touch online or by calling 101, quoting incident number 1076 of 1 September 2026.”

News.title: Boy, 17, has hand cut off in horror car park knife attack as another teen charged
News.content:
Boy, 17, has hand cut off in horror car park knife attack as another teen charged

The victim and his severed hand were rushed to hospital, where the boy is understood to have remained overnight in a stable condition. Doctors are still yet to confirm if they were able to save his detached hand

View 2 Images A New South Wales Police vehicle patrols the main street in the suburb of Merrylands, Sydney (file image) (Image: Getty Images)

A teenage boy has fronted court hours after the “near-complete amputation” of the hand of another teenager during an alleged assault on Wednesday (September 2).

According to police in Sydney, Australia, the 15-year-old allegedly attacked the 17-year-old boy at around 6pm local time on Wednesday, in a car park in the inner city suburb of Redfern.

Shortly afterward, emergency crews were called t o an oval on Redfern Street amid calls regarding a concern for welfare. It was there that NSW Police confirmed its officers found a teenage boy, 17, and his severed hand on the grass oval. Paramedics from NSW Ambulance were able to stabilise the teen at the scene, before transporting him to hospital in a stable condition.

As of Thursday morning, the 17-year-old is understood to have remained in a stable condition in hospital overnight. It is not yet clear whether or not doctors were able to reattach his hand, however.

View 2 Images A 17-year-old boy had his hand chopped off in an alleged car park assault (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

After a brief police investigation, NSW Police stopped a vehicle in the Redfern area just after midnight that was travelling west on Redfern Street. Police confirmed that shortly thereafter, officers arrested a 15-year-old boy nearby.

The teen was taken to Mascot Police Station in Sydney's south where he was charged with wound person with intent to cause grievous bodily harm, and breach of bail. He was refused bail to appear before a children’s court on Thursday.

The teen was silent on Thursday morning when he faced Surry Hills Children’s Court in relation to the alleged incident from the night prior.

Article continues below

“It’s a serious children’s offence,” Judge Keisha Hopgood told him.

No application for bail was made, and the 15-year-old was remanded in custody until October 6, the date of his next court appearance.

News.title: Binman shares 'secret' that 'most councils' follow to get extra wheelie bin
News.content:
Binman shares 'secret' that 'most councils' follow to get extra wheelie bin

A binman has shared a simple tip for households struggling with overflowing recycling that could lead to extra capacity

View 3 Images An overflowing, green coloured business recycling bin (Image: Getty Images)

Running out of room in your recycling bin can leave households wondering what they are supposed to do with the rest of their bottles, cans and cardboard. But one binman has revealed a little-known option that could give some people more space without forcing them to resort to putting recyclable items in their general waste.

‌



The No1 Binman, who has more than 200,000 followers and nearly four million likes on TikTok, regularly answers questions about what happens behind the scenes on bin rounds. In a recent video, he suggested that households whose recycling bins are repeatedly full should contact their local council and explain the problem.

‌



According to the council worker-turned-influencer, councils may be willing to provide another recycling bin where residents are regularly producing large amounts of recyclable waste. However, he stressed that this is not a guarantee, saying the approach applies to "most councils, not all councils".

‌



View 3 Images Do you need extra recycling waste capacity? (Image: Getty Images)

The binman suggested residents tell their council that their recycling bin keeps becoming full and ask what they should do with the additional recycling. He said some authorities may respond by providing another bin, particularly when the household is correctly separating recyclable material from its general rubbish.

His advice was based on the idea that councils want households to recycle as much as possible rather than putting recyclable material into residual waste. He also suggested taking excess recycling to a household recycling centre as another option if an additional bin is not available.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

There is no nationwide entitlement to an extra wheelie bin, however. GOV.UK directs residents to contact their local council when they need a recycling bin, meaning arrangements are decided locally.

Some councils do allow households to request additional recycling capacity. Southwark Council, for example, says residents can order an extra recycling wheelie bin if they cannot fit all their recycling into the one provided regularly.

‌



View 3 Images A line-up of waste bins outside a property (Image: Getty Images)

Salford City Council also allows residents to request extra recycling bins free of charge. Meanwhile, Coventry Council says additional recycling bins can be provided free where the authority is satisfied that residents are making reasonable efforts to recycle and compost.

Other authorities have different rules, including charges or assessments before an additional container is approved. Cheshire East, for instance, currently offers additional recycling bins for a charge, while Ashford Borough Council says extra bins are only considered in specific circumstances.

Article continues below

So if your recycling bin is constantly overflowing, it could be worth contacting your council rather than squeezing recyclable items into your general waste. Just don't assume you'll automatically receive a second bin - check your local authority's rules first.

News.title: Schoolboy rushed to hospital after hand turns blue from petting 'worm' in park
News.content:
Schoolboy rushed to hospital after hand turns blue from petting 'worm' in park

A six-year-old animal-lover got a very nasty surprise when the creature he believed to be a 'slow worm' during a trip to the park ended up giving him a very nasty bite

View 4 Images Kenzie got a nasty surprise when he picked up what he thought was a slow-worm

An animal-loving schoolboy was rushed to hospital after his attempt to pet what he believed was a "worm" ended with his hand swelling.

‌



Kenzie Macrae was with his friends when they came across a 'baby' reptile in a park on August 10. Kenzie initially took the creature to be a slow-worm until it suddenly sank its fangs into his finger.

‌



Shocked, the six-year-old rushed to his grandma's house, who lives across the road from the park, when his finger began swelling and turning white within minutes of the attack.

‌



Kenzie was rushed to hospital for anti-venom treatment where his whole hand and wrist became inflamed, causing him to temporarily lose function of his fingers.

Horrified mum Andrea Denoon rushed to A&E from work when little Kenzie's finger began turning blue and the venom continued to spread up his arm.

View 4 Images The creature was in fact an adder

‌



Doctors administered another bout of anti-venom to control Kenzie's symptoms, but grew concerned he may have gone into anaphylaxis when his heart rate and breathing levels began to drop.

Kenzie made a full recovery, but had to return to hospital 11 days later when he began experiencing a reaction known as 'serum sickness'.

Andrea, a 38-year-old infrastructure technician, is sharing Kenzie's story to raise awareness of the dangers of snake bites.

‌



Andrea, from Helmsdale, Sutherland, Scotland, said: "Mum picked the kids up and they wanted to go out to the play park.

"Mum was in the house and my daughter ran in the house to say Kenzie had been bitten by a snake. There was an older lad who had picked up the snake thinking it was a slow worm. He had it in his hands and because Kenzie has no fear, he thought 'I'm going to pet this'.

"He went in front of the snake towards the boy that was holding it and it obviously lashed out and bit him. He said it was very painful, initially he was in shock and kind of disorientated."

‌



View 4 Images Kenzie's hand swelled alarmingly

Kenzie was taken to Raigmore Hospital in Inverness to treat his snake bite with anti-venom medication, where mum-of-two Andrea met the family from work.

Andrea said: "Where he had been bitten, from the tip of the finger to the knuckle, had gone completely white.

‌



"Above the knuckle it had started swelling, that was within minutes. We were told he would be kept in overnight.

"Once I arrived at the hospital, his whole hand and just above his wrist had swollen up.

"He was struggling to bend his fingers, his whole hand was inflamed, it was massive.

‌



"A lot of nurses and doctors had never seen it before, especially on children.

"One of the kids got a picture of the snake, which was very handy. It was about 25cm long, it was tiny."

View 4 Images Kenzie required a second hospital visit

‌



Doctors quickly remedied Kenzie’s immediate problem, although he later had to return to hospital after suffering an after-effect known as “serum sickness."

Andrea said: "It was just a delayed aftermath of the anti-venom. He's absolutely fine now, we're just keeping an eye on him.

"It was very scary [when we thought his organs were shutting down], I didn't sleep for two days.

‌



"It was just a constant hand-on-chest listening to his breathing and watching him the whole time.

"I was massively shocked by the effect of the bite. It could've been a lot worse, it's a scary situation to be in.

"You don't know how each person is going to react to it.

Article continues below

"I'm not going to stop him playing with his friends. He has no fear of snakes even now."

News.title: 'Our boy suddenly lost his sight before we spent 6 months in hospital'
News.content:
'Our boy suddenly lost his sight before we spent 6 months in hospital'

Little Noah bumped his head and at first his mum thought he was fine

View 4 Images Noah spent 181 days in hospital (Image: PA Real Life)

A little boy lost his sight at the start of an ordeal that saw him spend 181 days in hospital.

‌



The parents of Noah Butterfield, who lost his sight before he was diagnosed with a rare brain tumour aged three, said it was the “best feeling” to receive the all-clear within six months of treatment – though his sight has not returned. When Noah, now four, bumped his head on Boxing Day 2024, his mother Amy Dickenson, 32, from Bradford and who works in HR, said she administered first aid and he seemed “fine” afterwards.

‌



But within two days Amy said Noah kept being sick and he “wasn’t himself” so she took him to hospital and doctors believed he had a viral infection, so she was advised to keep an eye on her son. By January 14, 2025, Noah’s father James, 29, a drainage engineer, needed to pick his son up from nursery early, with staff reporting he was “lying with his head in his hands”.

‌



A second trip to the hospital that same day had doctors believing Noah had flu, before he was sent home. His condition worsened to lethargy, a constant headache and more vomiting on January 18, as Noah began to complain that he couldn’t see.

Two days later, a CT scan revealed a brain tumour that was pressing on his optic nerve and he was blue-lighted to Leeds Children’s Hospital. After a biopsy, doctors confirmed Noah’s non-Hodgkin lymphoma diagnosis on January 24, and he started emergency chemotherapy the same day.

View 4 Images Amy and James are thankful to Leeds Children’s Hospital staff (Image: PA Real Life)

‌



Amy said Noah had six months of “horrendous” cancer treatment, but he was told in July that he was in remission and he rang a bell to signify the end of treatment.

James said: “Noah spent 181 days in a hospital bed, so for him to ring the bell, it was the best feeling."

Amy added: “I think I just cried. When his consultant came in and she said there’s no sign of disease, you just wait to hear that.

‌



“But I found it quite bittersweet too because I just thought: ‘Well, that’s good, but he’s still blind’.”

The parents believe Noah being an “excited toddler” and bumping his head on December 26, 2024, was a “blessing in disguise” because it forced them to seek medical advice earlier. Even though Amy said he seemed “fine” immediately after the accident when they gave him a cold compress, Noah’s condition worsened within two days.

But on two separate visits to the same hospital A&E department – on December 28 and January 14 – Noah was misdiagnosed with a viral infection and flu, respectively. After twice being sent home and told to “keep an eye” on Noah and give him Calpol if he needed it, Amy said her son’s condition started to deteriorate. Keeping Noah home from nursery, Amy said she noticed her son was “not himself”.

‌



Amy said: “He was really lethargic and didn’t want to do anything, which is really different because he’s very active.”

Then, on Saturday, January 18, Amy brought out paints and a paintbrush for Noah to use and placed them directly in front of him. But she said Noah lifted up his glasses and said, “I can’t see it – where is it?”

That same night, Amy said Noah was “up pretty much every hour” from bed complaining of pain in the front of his head. They gave him cold compresses, Calpol and made sure he was drinking water, but Amy and James decided to take him to another hospital’s A&E department on Sunday morning, where he was admitted.

‌



Amy said: “He went to give the doctor a high five and he completely missed. Then he walked into a door. He’d gone into hospital feeling poorly, and within 24 hours, his sight was gone.”

View 4 Images Noah rang the end-of-treatment cancer bell in July 2025 (Image: PA Real Life)

Noah had a CT scan on Monday, January 20, which confirmed a brain tumour pressing on his optic nerves.

‌



“You go really numb,” James said, of the moment he first heard the words “brain tumour”.

Amy added: “I screamed, cried and shouted.”

The parents did not want to scare Noah, so they did not tell him about his diagnosis, instead telling him that he is “poorly” and that was the reason why he could no longer see. The family was transferred to Leeds Children’s Hospital and Noah had a biopsy on January 22 that confirmed two days later that Noah had non-Hodgkin lymphoma.

‌



According to Cancer Research UK, it is a type of blood cancer that affects white blood cells and is more common among older people. Lymphomas of the brain are very rare and symptoms can include headaches, difficulty thinking, mobility issues, changes in personality, changes to speech and seizures.

The same day the biopsy confirmed Noah’s diagnosis, he started a round of emergency chemotherapy. Noah had six rounds of this treatment over as many months and Amy said he experienced many side effects, including mucositis – causing ulcers throughout his mouth and throat – black lips, a “massive” rash, blisters all over his body, vomiting, hair loss, swelling and losing his ability to walk.

“It was just horrendous,” Amy said. “You’re just watching your little person completely deteriorate in front of your eyes and you can’t do anything about it.”

‌



By July 2025, scans revealed there was no cancer detected in Noah’s body.

“How do you thank somebody for taking away cancer?” Amy said, of the staff at Leeds Children’s Hospital. “There are never any words.”

James said Noah has taken “everything in his stride”, including adjusting to now being registered blind by learning braille: “He’s very clever and he’s not let it stop him in the slightest.”

‌



The family has been supported by Cancer Research UK, including helping to organise a visit from Leeds United captain Ethan Ampadu, while in hospital, who James said “showered him” with gifts. Then, after Noah finished his treatment, he was invited to walk out during a Leeds United match as the club’s mascot in October 2025.

View 4 Images Leeds United captain Ethan Ampadu with Noah (Image: PA Real Life)

Amy said: “From the sidelines, we saw Noah walking across this pitch in front of thousands of people, and we couldn’t believe that a few months earlier, our little boy wouldn’t even put his feet on the floor. It was incredible."

Article continues below

Life for Noah has carried on since he received the all-clear over a year ago, including going back to nursery and continuing to enjoy football.

“He loves it,” James said. “We take him to games now, and despite not being able to see what’s going on, it’s about the atmosphere for him. A lot of people say blind people don’t like noise, but he’s in the middle of it all.”

Noah and his family are supporting Cancer Research UK this September for Childhood Cancer Awareness Month. Find out more about how the charity is driving progress for children and young people with cancer at http://cruk.org/children-and-young-people

News.title: UK weather maps show 3C chill as Brits face shock cold snap in weeks
News.content:
UK weather maps show 3C chill as Brits face shock cold snap in weeks

Weather maps show temperatures will plummet to 3C in the next few weeks as the nation braces for a cool temperatures following the hottest summer on record

View 3 Images The UK is braced for a cold spell (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The UK can brace for cool temperatures as the nation will feel extreme lows in the coming weeks.

‌



UK weather maps from WXCharts using Met Desk data show that certain areas will drop to a mere 3C in just over two weeks time.

‌



The chill will strike the nation on Sunday, September 13.

‌



View 3 Images Temperatures will drop as low as 3C (Image: WXCharts )

The conditions will feel especially cool following the UK's hottest summer on record.

The morning will start with areas further north sitting at 3C, including Northumberland and large parts of Scotland.

‌



Areas surrounding Yorkshire are also forecast to be around 4C in the morning, with counties in the south unsurprisingly slightly warmer.

The maps show London to be around 9C at 6am, with Greater Manchester and nearby Cheshire likely to be around 6C.

Much of the Midlands is forecast to drop to as low as 7C at the start of the day.

‌



Parts of Wales, including Montgomeryshire and Radnorshire will be some of the chilliest areas, also forecast a harsh 3C.

The weather maps show that these cool temperatures are likely to stay throughout the day, with little increase by midday.

The warmest area in the UK is forecast to be Norfolk, at 12C, still a sharp decline from the current conditions.

‌



Elsewhere at 12pm, highs of 10C will be felt.

View 3 Images The coolest temperatures will be felt in Wales and the north according to the maps (Image: WXCharts)

However large parts of Wales and Scotland will remain at the frosty 3C.

‌



In England the coldest areas are expected to be 4C, in the North West.

Cumberland and Westmorland will see icy temperatures of 4C and 3C. Slightly further south in Lancashire the forecaster predicts a cool 8C.

Much of the South West is also likely to experience 8C temperatures throughout the day. Despite these cooler conditions the Met Office has not ruled out any further "very warm spells" in September.

Article continues below

The long range forecast for September 7 to 16 says: "Overall, a fairly unsettled period is likely, with many places seeing showers or longer spells of rain at times, interspersed by drier periods.

"Rain will likely be most frequent across northern and western areas, while the south and east are more likely to see longer drier interludes. There is also the potential for some strong and gusty winds, particularly in the northwest.

"Temperatures are likely to be near average, although brief warm or very warm spells are possible, especially in the south."

News.title: 'Innocent' electrician shot dead with bullet to the head in drive-by shooting
News.content:
'Innocent' electrician shot dead with bullet to the head in drive-by shooting

Not one but two men have died in two separate cases of mistaken identity that appear linked to the city's seedy underbelly - with neither known to police

View 4 Images Joshua MacDonald, 40, was gunned down outside a Merrylands home on Wednesday

An innocent man has been gunned down in what police believe was a tragic case of mistaken identity, less than 24-hours after another man was killed in a similar case.

‌



Joshua MacDonald, aged 40, was walking down a western Sydney street on Wednesday (September 2). He was minding his own business, walking along Bruce Street in the Sydney suburb of Merrylands West, when gunmen in a stolen Audi screeched up alongside him, shooting the tradesman in the head. He was killed instantly.

‌



Mr MacDonald, who was an electrician by trade, is now understood to have been visiting an address with occupants that are allegedly 'well known to police for organised crime activity'. Officers from New South Wales Police have already confirmed that Mr MacDonald had no links to organised crime.

‌



View 4 Images The 40-year-old was killed instantly when gunmen opened fire from inside a stolen Audi sedan (pictured)

NSW Police Detective Superintendent Simon Glasser said: "The victim arrived at the property with a resident from the property and two young children.

"People associated with this address have links to organised crime. It is a possibility that the wrong person has been shot by these offenders."

‌



Security footage of Mr MacDonald's gruesome death was shared online.

In the footage, a gunman can be seen leaning out of the rear window of the stolen grey sedan before opening fire on Mr MacDonald as the Audi zipped past the western Sydney home.

Those responsible for the Merrylands shooting remain at large.

‌



Mr MacDonald's grim end came mere hours after another fatal shooting in Sydney, in Glen Alpine in the city's south-west at around 4am on Tuesday (September 1).

View 4 Images Marco Tapia (pictured) had a bright future ahead of him before he was killed on Tuesday

University student Marco Tapia, 23, was asleep in his bed in the early hours of Tuesday morning. He awoke to three masked men storming his home and was shot dead moments later, still in his bed.

‌



NSW Police confirmed that the 23-year-old engineering student was not known to police and had only a traffic offence on his record, which has led detectives to believe the shooting may also have been another hit served with a side of mistaken identity.

The Coconut Cartel and notorious crime syndicate the Alameddine network have been embroiled in a violent turf war in Sydney in recent months, with the gangland sides understood to be at war with each other over the rights to the city's illegal drug and tobacco trade.

On Thursday afternoon, NSW Police Minister Yasmin Catley hit back at claims police do not have the situation under control in the wake of the latest killings of innocent civilians.

‌



"We will not be surrendering our streets to organised criminals. Not now, not ever. Police are working around the clock to address these issues," she said.

"The model that we are seeing on our streets of these organised crime gangs, and utilising and using young men to do their dirty work for them, is insidious."

View 4 Images NSW Minister for Police and Counter-terrorism Yasmin Catley

‌



NSW Police Commissioner Mal Lanyon added that there may be more shootings on the horizon for Sydney, due to the flagrant disregard for human life stemming from the warring parties.

"What we are seeing at the moment is not the act of a genuine human," he said.

"That disregard for human life - to shoot at people that are innocent or they're not even certain (of) - shows that they don't care about that.

Article continues below

"There are many people who know of those that are committing this. I ask those people to provide us with information because... there is a chance that your loved one may be a victim one day, because that is the nature of organised crime."

News.title: Russian teachers made to spy on 'disloyal' students in patriotism lessons
News.content:
Russian teachers made to spy on 'disloyal' students in patriotism lessons

Students who teachers report as being unreceptive during the weekly 'patriot' lessons taught each Monday in Russian schools could find themselves in serious trouble with the police . . . or worse

View 4 Images A teacher with her students on the first day of school - known as Knowledge Day in Russia - at the newly opened Moya Shkola educational facility in Streletskoye (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Teachers in Russia are being made to spy on their own students, with official documents directing educators to file reports and keep tabs on school children deemed 'disloyal' to Moscow.

‌



As per a 2026/27 class outline for the mandatory 'Conversations about Important Matters' classes, now being taught in schools across Russia, pupils of all ages will to partake in ‘patriotism’ lessons throughout the academic year.

‌



The hour-long lessons, held each Monday, are designed to teach students "to form a value worldview in students based on the priority of spiritual and moral values, historical memory, generational continuity, active civic position, and readiness for creative labour for the good of the Motherland".

‌



The classes are 'patriot lessons' designed to push a pro-Russia doctrine amongst its youth, with the classes originally cropping up on school curriculums back in 2022, following the Kremlin invasion of neighbouring Ukraine.

View 4 Images Russian classrooms have been weaponised into insidious propaganda machines, says Amnesty International (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

As per the Moscow Times, homeroom teachers must record any incidents regarding pupils who disagree with the lesson's "value orientations", while educators themselves must also file a self-reflection section with each report on how they handled any rebellious students.

‌



While official documents from the Russian education department says that these post-lesson reviews are designed to help teachers evaluate the impact of the lessons and to help improve the course in years to come, human rights organisation Amnesty International has taken a rather different view.

A spokesperson for Amnesty International said in an online statement that the 'Conversations about Important Matters' lessons are simply state “indoctrination” at a classroom level.

"Since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Russian authorities have used the education system as a tool for political indoctrination," the statement reads.

‌



"Authorities are also using schools to identify and silence potential dissenters. Children are taught to avoid independent media and other sources of alternative information and opinion. School staff are instructed to monitor students’ behaviour and record their opinions on political and other issues."

View 4 Images Teachers will monitor kids of all ages during the 'patriot classes', including primary schoolers like this boy in Belgorod, Russia (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

The statement added: "If a student is disloyal, teachers must report them to the police and security services, resulting in reprisals against them and their families."

‌



These 'Conversations about Important Matters' classes, held each Monday in classrooms across the former Soviet nation, became a compulsory part of the school curriculum in 2023 on the basis of building patriotism amongst Russia's young people.

Lessons are also understood to have regularly featured Russian soldiers and mercenaries as guest speakers, invited into playgrounds to talk to small children about themes such as making "sacrifices for the nation".

Tuesday, September 1, was Knowledge Day in Russia which is essentially just day one of the new school year. It was on Tuesday - mere days ago - that students attended a school assembly in Siberia with a well-known Russian machine gunner appearing as guest speaker. According to Novaya Gazeta, he loosely quoted late nationalist politician Vladimir Zhirinovsky when speaking to the kids by telling them to study the workings of the Kalashnikov rifle if they “want the whole world [to speak] Russian”.

Article continues below

View 4 Images The classes will now be taught to kindergarteners as of September 2026. Pictured: Singing school students in Russia at a Knowledge Day ceremony on Tuesday

He is understood to have made gestures synonymous with now-defunct mercenary militia the Wagner Group; who were a group of soldiers of fortune who acted as a shadow army for the Kremlin until 2023. He also wished the children a good first day back at school, before adding that "victory will be ours" in Russia's conflict with Ukraine.

News.title: Chaos in Kyiv as two Ukrainian intelligence agencies 'shoot at each other' with three injured
News.content:
Chaos in Kyiv as two Ukrainian intelligence agencies 'shoot at each other' with three injured

The President has slammed the leaders of both agencies, but has not clarified what triggered the incident that left three people hurt and several 'detained'

View 2 Images The moment violence broke out between the SBU and HUR (Image: X/AseyevStanislav)

Three people have been injured after two top Ukrainian intelligence agencies shot at each other on the streets of Kyiv, officials have confirmed.

‌



Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has hit out at the leaders of Ukraine ’s security service (SBU) and its military intelligence unit (HUR) after the incident, according to the president’s chief communication adviser Dmytro Lytvyn, per the FT. Three people were wounded in the Wednesday (September 2) morning melee.

‌



The President's office has not clarified what caused the clashes, but the SBU has issued a statement claiming its personnel were attacked when trying to search a property for a ‘pre-trial investigation into the terrorist act organised by the FSB of the Russian Federation’.

‌



View 2 Images Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy (Image: PRESIDENT OF UKRAINE/APAImages/Shutterstock)

An SBU spokesperson said: “During a search at one of the addresses, a group of individuals carried out an armed attack on the SBU operational-investigative group. They tried to hinder the investigation and blocked the passage of law enforcement officers with their cars.

“To stop the attack and ensure the safety of the participants in the procedural actions, a special unit of the Special Operations Center "Alpha" of the SBU was involved. During the cessation of armed resistance, law enforcement officers used weapons.”

‌



They then claimed the SBU ‘detained’ members of the Ukrainian defence forces. The spokesperson added: “As a result of the incident, there are injured people among the people who resisted. The attackers have been detained.

During the initial investigative actions, it was established that the detainees belong to one of the units of the Defense Forces of Ukraine. Weapons and documents were seized from them.”

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



The HUR has not commented on the incident.

Footage from the incident circulated on social media early on Thursday morning (September 3). It shows a large group of men in military uniform shouting at one another, before several shots are fired.

The incident took place as Russian drones targeted Kyiv for the sixth day in a row. Russia has expanded its use of drone warfare in recent months in an effort to cripple Ukraine’s economy.

News.title: Watch: Drop in small boats crossings forces smugglers to adapt
News.content:
A BBC investigation has found smuggling gangs are running low on small boats, forcing rival gangs to have to work together to meet demand for crossings.

With crossings at a six-year low, it includes loading more migrants on larger vessels, as the 'mega-dinghies' that were first seen last month.

The gangs claim more are being prepared.

News.title: UN warns of 'supersized' El Niño as countries prepare for impact
News.content:
The world has entered a "danger zone of extreme weather" as the impacts of El NiÃ±o start to be felt globally, UN head AntÃ³nio Guterres has warned.

The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) has released the latest data on the natural weather phenomenon showing it could be the strongest for more than 70 years and last until at least February 2027.

El NiÃ±o changes weather patterns around the world, pushing some regions into drought whilst others experience stronger typhoons and flooding.

Forecasters also say El NiÃ±o will boost temperatures in some places, coming on top of rising heat globally from human-induced climate change.

"El NiÃ±o is being supersized before our eyes. The science leaves no room for doubt: the planet is in uncharted waters, and those waters are heating up," Guterres said.

The BBC spoke with governments and scientists about the measures being taken globally to reduce the risk of deaths, displacement and environmental damage. Early warning systems have been strengthened and deployment of pre-emptive medical assistance, but the strength of this particular event has raised serious concerns particularly for vulnerable groups.

The WMO - a UN agency - said it has undertaken a "major mobilisation" to try to circulate its forecasts of potential extreme weather events, linked to El NiÃ±o, to as many communities as possible.

WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo warned: "El NiÃ±o has the potential to deliver a massive blow to communities and economies across the world."

El NiÃ±o is a natural weather phenomenon that develops in the Pacific Ocean and is linked to a change in wind patterns. It allows warm water to spread eastwards and releases heat into the atmosphere.

Sea temperatures in the central and eastern tropical Pacific have risen sharply in recent months - a clear sign of a strengthening El NiÃ±o.

In the Pacific's key monitoring region, surface temperatures have been well over 2C above average in recent weeks, putting it on track to be declared a "very strong" event.

But it is expected to surpass even that marker. Monthly sea surface temperatures could get close to 4C above average, forecasts suggest.

This would make it the strongest El NiÃ±o since at least 1950, by potentially a large margin.

News.title: King hails 'unprecedented' Bayeux Tapestry exhibition in London
News.content:
The King and Queen, Macron and his wife Brigitte, and Burnham and his wife Marie-France van Heel were given the chance to see the historic embroidery in the atmospheric darkness of the British Museum.

It's displayed in a long glass illuminated cabinet, with the figures remarkably vivid for something almost a 1,000 years old, and visitors file along, following the story of the Norman invasion.

The royal visitors had a close look at key scenes in the tapestry, including the Coronation of King Harold and his death in battle.

It's filled with details of medieval life and the King commented on Normans pulling a cart with "an enormous amount of wine".

Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy said the final scene, showing King Harold with an arrow in his eye, was what she found the most dramatic.

"We've just been talking to all the schoolchildren, and that's the bit that they really liked and really registered with them," she said.

"And it's amazing actually that a tapestry that is 1,000 years old can still inspire people to feel such emotion and capture such drama after all this time."

Nandy said she was inspired by the way this epic depiction of conflict had "come to symbolise probably the biggest act of friendship on behalf of the French nation".

Sending the tapestry to the British Museum was announced by Macron during a state visit to the UK in July 2025, as an emblem of the strong partnership between the countries.

There had been fears that moving the fragile tapestry could risk causing damage, but French government sources said display conditions at the British Museum were "ideal".

The French authorities welcomed the way that visitors in London would see the tapestry lying flat, rather than upright, with this believed to be better for the conservation of the fibres.

It also allows viewers to get a clearer view of all the animals, plants and often bawdy images sewn around the margins of the main narrative.

It is believed the final scenes of the tapestry have been lost or destroyed, as it has not always had such careful owners. In the 18th Century, during the French Revolution, it was rescued from being cut up to make covers for soldiers' carts.

News.title: Uber launches UK's first robotaxis with a driver - here's what it's like to ride in one
News.content:
Londoners are able to hail the UK's first robotaxis - as Uber today becomes the first company to launch a self-driving minicab.

Initially, it only has 15 autonomous vehicles with a licence to operate in the city, and each one must have a human safety driver behind the wheel ready to take control if anything goes wrong.

Uber said it surveyed London-based customers via the app and more than 100,000 said they would choose a self-driving taxi if one was available, despite incidents of driverless rides malfunctioning in US cities where they already operate.

As I found out when I became the first UK journalist to hail one, it was mostly smooth but the safety driver did intervene on one occasion.

At the moment the UK fare for a robotaxi ride will be the same fare as a standard UberX, Uber Electric, or Uber Comfort journey, with upfront fares shown in the app.

Taking a self-driving ride will only appear as an option in the app after the journey has been booked, and if one of its cars is available nearby.

Uber's global head of autonomous mobility and delivery Sarfraz Maredia said the plan was to phase them in over a period of several years.

"We always want consumers to be able to request a human ride or an autonomous vehicle, and because the market's growing, we expect that there will be human drivers on Uber London for a long time to come," he said.

The Ford Mustang electric vehicles which make up Uber's current small fleet are fitted with the UK tech firm Wayve's driverless car technology, which uses AI to analyse data about what is going on around it in real time, gathered by sensors in a bar on the roof of the vehicle and elsewhere.

The vehicles are not pre-programmed - their actions are determined on the spot depending on what is going on.

Google's autonomous car company Waymo and the Chinese tech giant Baidu are also vying to launch services in the UK, and the competition is fierce.

Wayve chief executive Alex Kendall described developing the technology as "the space race for our generation" but added there were some "really hard problems to solve" along the way.

"What we've done over time is pioneer a completely new approach to autonomous driving, making it possible to bring this to a busy and complex city like London and scale it globally," he said.

News.title: The overlooked factor driving the childhood obesity crisis
News.content:
"I loved school. I loved to learn."

Ibbie, 16, always struggled with her weight, but it was during the Covid-19 lockdowns that she started eating even more. She was bullied by classmates over her size, and in her first year of secondary school she stopped attending completely.

Away from the routine of the school day, her weight problems worsened.

"When you are at home 24/7 it is very easy to go into the kitchen to get a snack. It's not the same if you are at school," says Ibbie, from Doncaster.

By the age of 12 she weighed nearly 22 stone (140kg) and was diagnosed with liver damage. "I was told that I might need to have a liver transplant if I didn't lose weight. That was scary to hear."

Ibbie's experience is one of the more extreme examples of children living with obesity in the UK â but her story is not unique. She is one of more than 6,000 children who have been treated at a pioneering weight-loss service for the most obese children in the country. These Complications from Excess Weight (CEW) clinics are a network of 39 specialist NHS hubs across England designed to treat severe obesity in children.

News.title: US sailors go shopping and bar-hopping in Thailand after 250-day voyage
News.content:
Far from hitting the bars and fleshpots of the Thai beach resort of Pattaya, in their first hours onshore most of the nearly 5,000 sailors from the USS Abraham Lincoln seemed determined to go shopping.

At the Hard Rock Hotel â one of two beachside hotels where they were able to stay off the ship â they hung around clutching their recent purchases. But perhaps, after a record 250 days confined inside a grey steel warship, the normality of a trip to the mall might have been just what they needed.

With their military haircuts, moustaches and navy t-shirts, they stood out against the usual Pattaya crowd in its flip-flops and beachwear.

News.title: Chris Mason: Reform face headwinds as they gather for conference
News.content:
Reform UK begin their annual conference in Birmingham a bigger party than they were a year ago, their numbers swelled at Westminster, at Holyrood, in the Senedd and in local authorities.

But they also gather amid significant political headwinds, much of which revolve around money.

There was that whopping Â£5m gift to Nigel Farage from Christopher Harborne, the Thailand based British billionaire, and the long running row about whether the money should have been declared by Farage once he became an MP.

Then there is, among other things, the Metropolitan Police investigation into donations to the party during the last general election campaign.

Reform insists that it "takes pride in its stringent vetting of donations."

When the party got together in the same West Midlands venue a year ago, they were an insurgency provoking intrigue and attention and demonstrating plenty of momentum.

Indeed that momentum was so significant that it was a major factor, perhaps the major factor, in accelerating the demise of Sir Keir Starmer as prime minister, because the potential prospect of a Reform government frightened the Labour Party to its core.

Would Starmer, its then desperately unpopular leader, help or hinder their attempts to take on Farage? Hinder was the eventually overwhelming view within Labour, and so Starmer was a goner.

But politics can change, and change quickly. With Starmer out and Burnham in, there is early evidence of some support for Labour picking up. No longer are Reform comfortably leading in all the opinion polls - in some they're not leading at all. Add to this a more confident and prominent Kemi Badenoch leading the Conservatives and the recent rise too of Restore Britain, the outfit set up by the former Reform MP Rupert Lowe. And the Scottish National Party and Plaid Cymru won and so beat them in the devolved elections in Scotland and Wales respectively. In other words, collectively Reform's opponents appear more energised and popular.

Make no mistake, no party at a UK wide level is popular at the moment, but the scrap appears more evenly matched than it did.

News.title: B&Q and Five Guys among firms that paid staff below minimum wage
News.content:
DIY store B&Q and the fast food chain Five Guys are among hundreds of UK businesses named by the government for paying staff below the minimum wage.

More than 600 employers were ordered to pay affected workers the outstanding wages, with Â£4m returned to workers, according to the Department for Business and Trade.

The firms have also been issued penalties worth Â£7m.

B&Q said the underpayments were unintentional and the result of calculations involving geographical allowances, while Five Guys blamed "technical differences in how payroll regulations were applied".

The list of 658 businesses includes shops, restaurants, nurseries, social care providers and a handful of NHS trusts. The government did not say over what time period the underpayments spanned.

Minimum wage is Â£12.71 for staff aged 21 and over. For 18 to 20 year olds the rate is Â£10.85, and for under 18s and apprentices it is Â£8.

B&Q underpaid 4,530 workers a total of more than Â£456,000, according to the government.

B&Q said in response: "The shortfalls in payments were unintentional. They relate to calculations involving geographical allowances which are paid in addition to minimum hourly rates. All affected colleagues were quickly paid in full in July 2025."

Five Guys, named in the list as owing over Â£54,000 to 3,699 staff, said "technical differences in how payroll regulations were applied" led to its underpayments, which were identified in a review by the HMRC, the UK's revenue and tax authority.

"We worked closely and transparently with HMRC throughout the process and have made all required payments to affected current and former employees," the company said.

St George's, Epsom and St Helier Hospital Group failed to pay over Â£123,000 to 75 workers, according to the list, which also says St George's University Hospitals in Wandsworth, London, underpaid 55 workers.

A spokesman for the two hospital trusts said that "no colleagues were underpaid".

"This relates to a technical compliance issue where part of their salary for a non tax-deductable 'salary sacrifice' (for example, towards childcare) was not counted towards the national minimum wage, even though their gross salary was above the national minimum wage," he said.

A spokesperson said apprentices at Norfolk Community Health and Care NHS Trust were inadvertently underpaid between 2019 and 2023.

They said while their pay met the requirements for their contracted hours, meetings, handovers and time spent changing into uniform hadn't been accounted for, adding the trust has since changed policies and practices.

The other trust named has been contacted for comment.

There were also several nursing homes on the list, and multiple childcare providers.

Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds said the government was determined to stamp out the practice of "short-changing your staff".

"The best businesses know that looking after your workers isn't just the right thing to do, it's the smart thing to do," he said.

Kate Dearden, minister for the future of work, said: "Underpaying your staff is illegal, and we will not let workers foot the bill for their boss failing to follow the rules."

"Every employer should check their payroll now and reach out to Acas if they need further support," she added.

The first 10 employers on the government's list, which was sorted by the amount of wages not paid, are:

1. B&Q Ltd, failed to pay Â£456,934.72 to 4,530 workers.

2. Elysium Healthcare Holdings 3 Ltd, Borehamwood, failed to pay Â£330,048.81 to 1,095 workers.

3. St George's, Epsom and St Helier Hospital Group, failed to pay Â£123,331.97 to 75 workers.

4. Support Staff Services Limited, Slough, failed to pay Â£119,715.13 to 323 workers.

5. Forest Holidays Ltd, Moira, failed to pay Â£100,308.68 to 598 workers.

6. St George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, London (Wandsworth), failed to pay Â£77,498.91 to 55 workers.

7. Lanes Group Limited, Leeds, failed to pay Â£67,893.34 to 297 workers.

8. UK Care Team Ltd, Leicester, LE19, failed to pay Â£67,082.76 to 99 workers.

9. Five Guys JV Limited, London (Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea), failed to pay Â£54,642.47 to 3,699 workers.

10. Merlin Cinemas Limited, Redruth, failed to pay Â£50,198.75 to 181 workers.

The list marks the first "naming round" since the Fair Work Agency was set up in April under the Employment Rights Act.

As well as enforcing the minimum wage, the agency also will soon tackle practices of denying workers holiday and sick pay.

Chair of the agency's advisory board, Matthew Taylor, said naming employers which underpay staff was an important reminder that "paying the minimum wage is not optional - it is the law".

He said: "Most employers want to do the right thing, and we will support them to comply, but those who fall short should expect robust enforcement to protect workers and maintain a fair playing field for responsible businesses."

News.title: Burnham to tackle 'mega-donors' in UK politics, minister says
News.content:
Reform has been critical of measures contained in the bill and the impact they could have on funding the party receives from donors.

There are currently no restrictions on the amount of money UK-based donors can give to political parties and politicians.

Labour MP Stella Creasy said donations from individuals and companies giving Â£1m or more had "surged" in the last decade and gave examples for different political parties.

Among those she named was British billionaire Christopher Harborne, a Thailand-based businessman, who is one of Reform's biggest backers.

Last year he gave a single donation of Â£9m to Reform - the biggest single donation to a UK political party by a living person.

Creasy was among those who tabled amendments seeking to also impose a cap on UK-based donors.

One of her proposals called for an immediate Â£500,000 limit which would reduce to Â£100,000 in the second calendar year. Minsters would have been able to set a permanent cap.

The amendment, which was not moved to a vote, was signed by more than 60 MPs.

Creasy told the Commons: "Obscene wealth is increasingly dictating who is heard, whether we like it or not, what issues are being prioritised and whose interests shape policy decisions."

The Walthamstow MP added that there was a "need to act now to protect the next general election". Her proposals would have exempted trade unions from the donation cap, with the MP saying this is "already well regulated" and "clean money".

Kruger highlighted the millions of pounds donated by trade unions to the Labour Party as he criticised the proposals and the bill.

The MP for East Wiltshire said: "The claim is made that this bill will defend democracy, but actually it's a flagrantly partisan attempt to kneecap Reform UK."

The former Conservative MP added: "The suggestion is made that this bill will restore trust in politics and that is exactly what is needed.

"But what they all mean is to restore trust in the class of politicians and in the political parties that have got us into the mess that we are in, including the party I'm afraid to say I was part of which is why I left it. We need change."

Responding for the government, Eshalomi said the bill "already contains a package of significant measures designed to strengthen the political finance regime whilst ensuring that legitimate donors can continue to fund election campaigns".

The communities minister added that the prime minister was among those "determined to tackle the UK-based issue of mega-donors in UK politics".

"That is why I'm happy to commit and announce the new cross-government task and finish team will be working at pace to find a solution without unintended consequences," Eshalomi said.

"I can reassure members that once these solutions have been found, we would want them in force as soon as possible."

Full details of the new team's remit have yet to be confirmed by the government.

It last month emerged that Burnham registered accepting Â£345,000 of donations over the past year, including Â£164,347 from businessman Lord Sainsbury.

The Liberal Democrats proposed establishing a royal commission to make recommendations for a cap on political donations and the "effectiveness" of existing campaign expenditure limits.

This proposal was rejected in the Commons by 427 votes to 85, majority 342.

Green Party MP Ellie Chowns said Creasy had made a "clear case" for a cap on all donations, adding she would prefer it to be lower and suggested Â£50,000 a year.

Conservative shadow housing secretary Katie Lam said it was a "noble aim" to protect UK democracy from foreign influence but changes proposed by the government had not always been produced with "proper care and attention".

In March, the government said donations in cryptocurrency to UK political parties would be banned alongside the move to cap donations of British citizens living abroad at Â£100,000 annually.

Ministers later announced overseas voters moving to the UK would be prevented from giving more than Â£100,000 in political donations for a year after their arrival.

This was announced alongside tougher checks on company donations, which they believe will help stop foreign money from influencing UK elections.

The bill also contains measures to change the voting system, including extending the right to vote to 16- and 17-year-olds.

MPs approved the bill at third reading by 411 votes to 102, majority 309, and it will undergo further scrutiny in the House of Lords at a later date.

News.title: Rocky Horror star Tim Curry's cause of death revealed as coronary artery disease
News.content:
British actor Tim Curry died of coronary artery disease, his spokesman has confirmed to the BBC.

The Rocky Horror Picture Show star died in his Los Angeles home on 25 August, aged 80.

In addition to the heart condition, Curry had a history of stroke and kidney cancer, which were significant conditions that contributed to his death, his spokesman said, citing a death certificate filed in Los Angeles County.

Stars of stage and screen paid tribute to the actor, who shot to fame as the lingerie-clad Dr Frank-N-Furter in the cult 1975 film The Rocky Horror Show.

After having a near-fatal stroke in 2012, the actor used a wheelchair. He shifted his focus to voice acting exclusively, expressing gratitude that the stroke resulted in paralysis rather than taking away his ability to speak.

He continued to appear at film conventions and published his memoir, Vagabond, last year in which he opened up about the medical incident and his prolonged recovery.

"If there was anything impressed upon me in the aftermath, it was just how remarkable it was that I was still alive," Curry said, according to People, external.

News.title: How Victoria Beckham turned her fashion firm around and made it profitable
News.content:
It has taken Lady Beckham 18 years to shift her business - where she is creative director - into the black.

The former popstar admitted in a Netflix documentary that the company had once been "tens of millions into the red", with "mind-blowing" waste including a flower budget of Â£70,000 a year.

Lady Beckham spoke of her "panic" as the debt piled-up.

"It's been a hell of a journey. I almost lost everything and that was a dark, dark time," she said. "I used to cry before I went to work every day, because I just felt like a firefighter."

David Belhassen, founder of private equity firm Neo Investment Partners, recalled having to deliver some hard truths when he decided in 2017 to get involved with the business.

"I said 'we have to change everything, restructure the business and that's going to be painful'."

Fashion brands can be notoriously slow to turn a profit. Stacia Bedford, a course leader at the London College of Fashion, said establishing a label can take between three and five years.

"Launching a 'typical' fashion brand is enormously expensive," she said.

"Brands that do make money follow the lean startup method and keep their collections minimal. You need a lot of traction to get the attention of an investor."

News.title: ‘I'd be the last to know’: Stars of The Gentlemen react to Meghan reports
News.content:
It has been almost two weeks since reports emerged that the Duchess of Sussex was in talks for a role in The Gentlemen.

At the world premiere for series two of the Netflix show on Wednesday night, stars including Maya Jama, Hugh Bonneville and Theo James remained tight-lipped about the prospect of Meghan joining the cast.

âItâs fascinating to watch, but ultimately itâs a lot of rumour,â James told BBC News, while Jama said: âIâd be the last person to know!â

The showâs executive producer said he didn't want to say yes or no to the reports about Meghan, but added they were looking forward to âmore energy and surprisesâ to come.

The Gentlemen, a comedy action series about a duke turned drug baron, created by Guy Ritchie, was a major hit when it first dropped in 2024.

The show has officially been greenlit for a third series. Talks with Meghan are understood to be in the early stages, but the details of the discussions and any role she might be offered have not yet been revealed.

News.title: Four in court over murder of baby stabbed to death
News.content:
Two men and two women have appeared in court charged with murdering a baby girl who had been repeatedly stabbed at a house in Sheffield.

The newborn - referred to as Baby S in court - was found at a property in Holywell Heights, in the Wincobank area, on Sunday, having suffered 33 wounds from 15 separate stabbings.

Andrea Skopova, 20, formerly of Robey Street, Sheffield, and Peter Horvath, 19, Nina Horvathova, 37, and Peter Horvath, 38, all of Holywell Heights, appeared at Sheffield Magistrates' Court.

The four Slovakian nationals have been charged with murder, causing or allowing the death of a child and perverting the course of justice by taking steps to conceal the killing of an infant.

A fifth person, a 15-year-old girl, who cannot be named for legal reasons, also appeared in the same court charged with perverting the course of justice.

All five defendants were remanded into custody to appear at Sheffield Crown Court on Thursday.

News.title: Letby 'boyfriend' doctor named as court order lifted
News.content:
Letby - who has always maintained her innocence - is serving 15 whole life prison terms. The Criminal Cases Review Commission (CCRC) is conducting a review of Letby's convictions.

At her criminal trial - the longest murder trial in UK history - Deakin gave evidence in relation to several babies. He was granted special measures as well as anonymity. These allowed him to give evidence from behind a screen so that Letby, the public gallery, and the media were prevented from seeing him.

Deakin's evidence provided detail of some of the emergency calls and resuscitations which he and Letby were jointly involved in. Their long nights of text messaging were laid bare and many of the messages shown to the jury.

When he was sworn in, on the first occasion he testified, Letby burst into tears, in what was the first display of emotion from her during the trial.

During her cross-examination, Letby was forced to deny that Deakin was her boyfriend, though she did accept that they had gone on a trip to London together.

The prosecuting barrister, Nick Johnson KC, said Letby "tried to get out the back of the dock" when the doctor first came to the witness box.

Letby said: "Yes, because I felt unwell."

Johnson said: "No, it's because you didn't like hearing your boyfriend giving evidence, did you?"

Letby said: "That's unfair."

Prosecutors also went through a WhatsApp message exchange between Letby and a friend who had teased her for being "flirty" with Deakin.

Johnson said: "She knew you were sweet on Mark, didn't she?"

Letby said: "What do you mean, sweet?"

Johnson said: "That you had a crush on him."

"No," said Letby.

"There was nothing between me and that Mark."

Johnson told the court that Letby told her friend she had received a "strange message" from the doctor.

Her colleague responded: "Did you? Saying what? Go Commando [laughing face emoji]."

While some media reports have described him as "a key witness", Deakin was one of many former colleagues of Letby's whose joint testimony helped to build the prosecution case against her, and none of the convictions rested solely on his evidence.
