News.title: About 700 prisoners to be freed on 1 October under revised early release plans
News.content:
About 700 eligible offenders will leave jails in England and Wales on the morning of 1 October and some 2,550 will have been released by the end of the year, the government's revised early prison release plan shows.

The new plan, signed into law and published online, shows Andy Burnham's government kept the promised original schedule of how and when offenders will leave jail, aside from delaying the start date by a month and excluding specific offences from the programme.

Under the original plan, offenders serving sentences of up to 19 months would have been eligible from 2 September to walk out of jail after serving a third of that time.

In the Commons on Wednesday, Burnham said he understood the "anguish" of victims and "listened to what they were saying".

"I came in and asked for changes to the early release scheme, and we excluded rape, grooming, and child sex offences," the prime minister added.

Prisoners will now qualify for their earlier release from 1 October and officials estimate that around 700 will walk out of the prison gates that day.

From 13 October, governors will release a second tranche of 650 prisoners who have been serving sentences of between 19 months and two years and five months.

Prisons in England and Wales are running at 97% capacity, with the latest Ministry of Justice figures showing the number of available spaces across the male prison estate at its lowest this year, with about 1,500 free spaces.

Under the original plan, prisons and probation services had almost six weeks to prepare this second group following the first releases, but they now have less than a fortnight.

The rest of the estimated 4,500 releases will then be phased in following the dates below. Some 1,400 more offenders were due to be released under the original plans before revisions made after certain offences were excluded.

The estimated numbers are Ministry of Justice calculations:

From 10 November, 650 offenders serving up to three years and two months

From 8 December, 550 offenders serving up to four years and three months

From 12 January 2027, 600 offenders serving up to five years and nine months

From 9 February, 500 offenders serving up to seven years and six months

From 9 March, 200 offenders serving up to nine years

From 13 April, 200 offenders serving up to 10 years

From 11 May, 250 offenders serving up to 12 years

From 9 June, 250 offenders serving more than 12 years.

The offenders serving the longer sentences, which do not become part of the scheme until next year, include more dangerous criminals who would have previously expected to spend two-thirds of their sentence behind bars.

News.title: Four arrested over woman's murder 32 years ago
News.content:
Four people have been arrested on suspicion of perverting the course of justice in the case of a woman who was murdered 32 years ago.

Doreen Morris, 64, was stabbed to death with a fork after disturbing a burglary at her home, Penrhyn Uchaf, on Anglesey, in 1994, according to a 2023 inquest.

Joseph Carl Westbury denied breaking into Doreen's bungalow and was found not guilty of her murder in 1995. He took his life in May 2016.

North Wales Police said a man and three women, all from north Wales, were arrested on Wednesday morning.

The force said advances in forensic science and a review of evidence had led to the development and the Morris family had been told.

Mark Pierce, senior review officer, said: "Forensic results, combined with a detailed review of witness evidence, have provided grounds to interview four people on suspicion of perverting the course of justice."

He appealed for anyone with information about the case to get in touch.

Russia has said it will close German cultural spots across the country in response to being blamed for an attempted attack on an airport.

Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov announced the move on Thursday after Berlin blamed Moscow for an attempted attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport last month. He announced the closure of both the Russian Consulate in Bonn and the Russian House cultural center in the German capital.

Lavrov said that cultural centers belonging to Germany's Goethe-Institut would be closed in Moscow, St. Petersburg and Yekaterinburg, adding that any other response would show a lack of "self-respect" on Russia's part.

Speaking at the Eastern Economic Forum in Vladivostok, Lavrov said that Germany "could not have failed to understand" that the closure of Russian House would "signify the end of their cultural presence in Russia."

A drone laden with explosives was found near a Ukrainian plane at Leipzig/Halle Airport on Aug. 4 and later defused. The airport is a major international freight hub used for providing support to Ukraine.

Moscow has been widely accused by Western officials of running a campaign of sabotage and disruption with the aim of undermining support for Ukraine and destabilizing European nations.

open image in gallery In this pool photograph distributed by the Russian state agency Sputnik, Russia's President Vladimir Putin, accompanied by Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov, attends a meeting with Indonesian President on the sidelines of the Eastern Economic Forum in Vladivostok on September 3, 2026. (Photo by Vyacheslav PROKOFYEV / POOL / AFP via Getty Images) ( AFP/Getty )

Putin has dismissed the allegations, saying Berlin wants to distract from its own failings and dissatisfaction among voters. Any proof being offered "has been planted," Putin said.

European Union ministers on Wednesday weighed how best to respond to the attempted drone attack but struggled to find new ways to meet the challenge without resorting to military means.

"It is clear that it has all the hallmarks of state-sponsored terrorism. The question is: what do we do about this," EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas told reporters before chairing a meeting of the bloc's foreign ministers in Ireland. They discussed sanctions, visa restrictions and shutting Russian consulates, among other measures.

The EU has slapped almost two dozen packages of sanctions on Russia over the war in Ukraine, hitting more than 3,000 officials, oligarchs and entities including banks, energy companies and drone makers. The EU was already preparing to impose more travel bans and asset freezes on another 1,600 people, Kallas said.

Germany insisted it was "not at war" but had become a "daily target" of the Kremlin's hybrid campaign. Putin dismissed the allegations, saying Berlin wants to distract from its own failings and dissatisfaction among voters. Any proof being offered "has been planted," Putin said.

But German Foreign Minister Johan Wadephul said Berlin had carefully prepared its response "and now Russia must live with these consequences." He called on Russia "to show that it is also ready for reasonable talks and negotiations, particularly regarding the situation in Ukraine."

SeaDream Yacht Club has unveiled plans for its first new luxury vessel in 25 years, catering for passengers who want to travel further.

Launching in July 2029, SeaDream III will start with sailings in Asia as well as a world cruise that will end in the UK.

The family-owned brand, which markets itself as "yachting, not cruising,” said the 495ft ship will welcome around 200 guests, with an almost one-to-one crew-to-passenger ratio.

Guest cabins will span five decks and include a greater selection of suites, Commodore staterooms and connecting configurations, with private balconies across four guest decks.

The yacht’s design will place open-air living at its centre with expansive upper decks, a dedicated pool deck and multiple spaces for dining, gathering and relaxing.

There will also be three dedicated watersports marinas to provide direct access to the sea.

SeaDream III will also feature an expanded spa, fitness and wellness offerings, the luxury line said.

In contrast, SeaDream I and II measure 344 feet long and have space for 112 guests.

The first two ships focus on the Mediterranean and the Caribbean but SeaDream III will also operate a wider range of itineraries.

During her first 24 months, SeaDream III will sail to six continents, 73 countries, and 364 ports.

The maiden voyage is scheduled to depart from Hong Kong on 10 July 2029, sailing through the Ryukyu Islands and along Japan’s Pacific coast before arriving in Tokyo for her official christening on 21 July.

The 10-night sailing will feature extended stays in Ishigaki and Yakushima, along with calls in Okinawa, Amami Oshima, Kochi and Shimizu.

Her inaugural season will continue with a collection of voyages exploring Japan and South Korea. Four 14-night round-trip voyages from Tokyo will combine northern and western Japan with South Korea, followed by a 15-night voyage from Tokyo to Hong Kong through Japan’s southern islands.

open image in gallery SeaDream II made a rare call in Tower Bridge, London in May 2025 ( Marc Shoffman )

In 2030, the yacht will sail west from Asia to India, the Arabian Peninsula and the Mediterranean before arriving in London for northern Europe sailings.

On 5 January 2031, SeaDream III will depart West Palm Beach on a 180-night World Voyage to London.

Atle Brynestad, founder and owner of SeaDream Yacht Club, said: "SeaDream III represents the next chapter for SeaDream.

“She will carry forward the same DNA as SeaDream I and SeaDream II: personalised service, exceptional cuisine, a relaxed and friendly atmosphere, and the genuine feeling of being on your own yacht. With SeaDream III, the whole world becomes our destination.”

News.title: Muddy waterfall cascades down cliffside at Zion National Park
News.content:
A fast-moving, muddy waterfall cascaded down a cliffside in Utah's Zion National Park, dramatic video shows.

Vehicles drove past as heavy rainfall triggered flooding in the park. Authorities issued a flash flood warning.

On Saturday (29 August), a flash flood killed two people in Grand Canyon National Park in the neighbouring state of Arizona.

Officials stated on Monday that at least 80 people had been rescued from Grand Canyon National Park and one person was unaccounted for.

Kevin Sorbo does not regret leaving California.

After the Hercules: The Legendary Journeys actor, 67, traded Hollywood for the Sunshine State seven years ago, the MAGA supporter told Fox News in an interview Sunday that part of the reason he left California was that he was “canceled” due to his political beliefs as a conservative Christian — but he had other complaints too.

Sorbo told the right-wing outlet that although he misses the weather, his old house and his local golf course, three factors keep him from returning to the Golden State.

“I mean, here in Florida, yeah, we get five months of pretty high humidity,” the Andromeda star acknowledged. “It’s pretty hot, but the winters here are really quite amazing. But yeah, there are things I miss, but they can keep their taxes, they can keep their traffic, and they can keep their negativity, I’m done.”

He went on to say that Florida has given him more “acceptance” since he relocated with his family.

open image in gallery Kevin Sorbo has spoken out about why he left California ( Getty )

Sorbo is known as a vocal critic of Hollywood, and he often claims that the entertainment industry is biased against people who have conservative or Christian views.

“It's just ridiculous and childish to me,” he said. “We all have different opinions. There's nothing wrong with that.”

He went on to say that people in Hollywood dismissed him after he became outspoken about his support for President Donald Trump.

“It’s the conservatives that are in the closet now because they saw me get canceled,” he explained. “But I’m still working.”

open image in gallery Kevin Sorbo and his wife Sam Sorbo have lived in Florida for seven years ( Getty )

Sorbo is best known for his lead role as the ancient Greek demigod Hercules in the Nineties TV series Hercules: The Legendary Journey, which followed a series of five television films. After Hercules ended in 1999, Sorbo played Captain Dylan Hunt in the sci-fi drama Andromeda from 2005 to 2006. He also appeared on the final season of The O.C.

In recent years, he has focused largely on producing, directing and acting in faith-based films, with his latest project being a Christian movie about a rockstar titled Elijah Peel.

He also has worked on several family-oriented movies. Sorbo and his wife, conservative activist and actor Sam Sorbo, have three children together whom they homeschooled, including their son Braeden Sorbo, who is an actor and the author of a pro-masculinity book.

Braeden made headlines last year when he said on a podcast appearance that he thinks only married couples with property should have the right to vote.

A police chief in a northern Mississippi city has been fired following a fresh wave of controversy, months after officers shot and killed a one-year-old Black child named Kohen Wiley during a shoplifting call.

Harold Vanderford, the police chief of Senatobia, tendered his resignation on Tuesday. However, the city’s board of aldermen rejected his departure and opted to unanimously vote to sack him instead, the city clerk confirmed without offering further detail.

The dismissal comes after joint reporting by The New York Times, Mississippi Today and Verite News alleged Vanderford used racial slurs in private text exchanges with a colleague, alongside ongoing fallout from the fatal shooting.

Young Kohen died and a woman was wounded on 14 June when an officer fired into a vehicle outside a Walmart. The boy’s mother, Vellesiya Wiley, denied that she or a friend had stolen anything, and no charges have been filed.

The officer who shot Wiley and the driver has been placed on administrative leave while the Mississippi Bureau of Investigation conducts an enquiry.

open image in gallery In this photo provided by Marquell Bridges, a group of mourners attend a makeshift memorial for 1-year old Kohen Wiley, outside the Walmart where the boy was shot by police in Senatobia, Miss., on Wednesday, June 17, 2026. (Courtesy Marquell Bridges via AP)

Kohen Wiley was Black, as is his mother. The death ignited anger in a small city where tensions between Black residents and the police have boiled over in recent years. Senatobia, with a population of more than 8,000, is about 40 miles (65 kilometers) south of Memphis.

"I believe the Board has a responsibility to protect the integrity and trust of the Senatobia Police Department," Alderman Demetrius Garrett wrote in a Facebook post. "I still believe in unity. But unity does not mean ignoring serious issues it means standing together for what is right."

The city had previously addressed the reporting about Vanderford's texts, saying in a statement on Aug. 25 that he had appeared before the mayor and board to answer questions and that he would continue to serve as police chief.

Senatobia Alderman Chris McConnell called for an independent investigation of the police department.

"We need answers about departmental leadership, internal culture, the handling of complaints and misconduct, financial practices, and whether the Board has been receiving the information necessary to provide proper oversight," McConnell said in a statement. "Our citizens deserve a police department they can trust."

National civil rights attorney Ben Crump, representing Kohen Wiley's family, called the chief's firing the "right decision."

"The racist language that cost Chief Vanderford his job is exactly why this family cannot simply be told to trust the process," Crump said in a statement calling for the Mississippi Bureau of Investigations to release body-camera footage of the shooting. "Give this family the facts they have been owed since the day Kohen died."

The Senatobia Police Department declined to comment on the firing, and Vanderford could not be immediately located for a response Wednesday.

Kohen Wiley's shooting death was one controversy among others

Vanderford was appointed police chief on Sept. 29, 2025, after the board of aldermen declined to reappoint the previous chief, Richard Chandler, in July of that year.

open image in gallery Harold Vanderford ( Senatobia Police Department/Facebook )

Chandler led the police department through several controversies. They included the 2023 arrest of a 10-year-old Black boy for urinating in public and an incident in which an officer threatened a woman with a Taser and pulled her from her car during a dispute over a handicapped parking space outside the same Walmart where the child was shot.

"You removed Richard Chandler," said Senatobia community activist Patrick Lumumba. "But you did not remove the culture of racism, and that's what Vanderford harbors."

Following the child's death, Lumumba formed the Senatobia Committee for Accountability and Transparency, a community watchdog group that is demanding answers about the June shooting and advocating for better policing.

He voiced confidence in Lt. Angelica Maze, who will serve as the department's interim police chief, calling her a"good person."

In a civil defense shelter hewn into rock, behind doors designed to withstand a nuclear or biological attack, two Finnish conscripts wearing hazmat suits and breathing masks are measuring radiation levels as they take part in an exercise to turn a cave into a place of safety for thousands of people.

Inside, in what is normally a sports hall, hundreds of people are sleeping overnight on trestle beds.

More than 2,000 people including volunteers and students are taking part in the biggest civil defense exercise in Europe since the end of World War II. In the scenario, critical infrastructure in the central Finnish city of Kuopio, including power and water, has been disrupted by cyberattacks and there’s the threat of missile strikes from Finland’s neighbor, Russia.

The goal is for local authorities and ordinary people to rehearse what they would do if they came under attack for real.

But while underground bunkers and shelters may offer some protection from missiles, they are no defense against the campaign of sabotage and disruption that Western officials say Russia is carrying out across Europe. That has involved setting fires, attacking water facilities and power stations, and sending drones for sabotage into European Union airspace.

Finland's border with Russia stretches more than 830 miles (1,300 kilometers) from the Baltic Sea up to the Arctic Circle. In 2024, along with Sweden, Finland joined NATO, following Russian President Vladimir Putin's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Until then, Finns were prepared to defend themselves against Russia largely alone.

Finland looks to Ukraine for lessons

Finland’s defense, said retired Army Colonel Asko Muhonen, relies not only on the military but on the “mindset” of ordinary Finns who are ready to take responsibility for their country’s security.

Muhonen, who organized the exercise in Kuopio, said that comes partly from the system of conscription which continued in Finland, even after the collapse of the Soviet Union.

Not everyone is happy about doing national service but “it’s our duty to serve and protect this country like people have before us. That’s why we have our independence,” said Jyry Pietikainen, 23, a conscript who was taught how to run the Kuopio shelter overnight.

Finland also needs to learn lessons from Ukraine, Muhonen said.

While the biggest shelter in Kuopio can fit 7,000 people, Ukrainians sometimes only have a few minutes to run to a subway station or underground parking lot. That means people need a shelter they can reach easily that offers some form of protection — not necessarily one that can withstand a nuclear attack, he said.

Dmytro Untila, 20, a Ukrainian student at the university in Kuopio, was at home in Odesa when Russian missiles struck his city on Feb. 24, 2022, the first day of the war. He sheltered in the entrance hall of his building because he didn’t have anywhere else to go, he said.

Training for such a situation would have definitely helped in Ukraine, he said, “because nobody knew this could happen.”

The biggest threat to energy infrastructure in the Kuopio region is heavy snowfall, storms and bad weather, said Juha Räsänen, CEO at the Savon Voima electricity company.

But since the invasion of Ukraine, and the company’s decision to stop buying Russian biofuel, the number of cyberattacks against the network has significantly increased, Räsänen said.

Last year, engineers also found at least 10 stickers placed on particularly vulnerable parts of the energy network infrastructure. Other energy companies in Finland have also found them and don’t know where they came from, he said.

“If there was an explosion at that point, it could destroy a whole dam,” Räsänen said. Drones have also been spotted over power lines but those responsible have not been identified, he said.

It is not possible to guard against all threats, Räsänen said, which is why it’s important people are prepared to look after themselves without help for at least 72 hours — if the power supply goes out, or if water becomes undrinkable.

The Finnish Security and Intelligence Service said it investigated “a wide range of observations” and found nothing of concern.

Since 2022, people have been more vigilant because of the security situation and therefore have reported things like reflective stickers related to land survey works, it said in a statement. Drone sightings, it said, have “largely been explained by everyday occurrences.”

“Small things are happening all the time,” including Russian jamming of GPS signals, said Vuokko Lahtinen, 32, who was visiting a sauna in Kuopio.

For that reason, “the best defense of Finland is to make it not worth attacking,” she said.

That relies on the country’s military and defense forces but also Finnish people who feel like “we have something we want to fight for,” she said.

In Finland, she said, there is a “general feeling of responsibility,” which has grown out of local community groups and even initiatives such as recycling.

“On a very simple daily level, if you do things that matter, then it has a butterfly-wing effect,” Lahtinen said.

Finland fought several wars with the Soviet Union

In its wars with the Soviet Union, Finland lost around 11% of its territory, and more than 400,000 people, around 12% of the population, fled their homes from an area that is now in western Russia.

At Kuopio's veterans’ museum, Risto Mönkkönen, 95, showed AP a piece of paper on which he had written down the dates the city was bombed and who died.

“I cannot forget it,” he said explaining how, as a child, he and his father ran into a shelter just as a bomb hit, killing five of his father’s friends.

Pirkko Naukkarinen, 102, recalled how, aged 16, she worked in a field kitchen by the front lines, sometimes sharing dugouts with soldiers and diving for cover in ditches as the Soviet air force attacked the retreating Finnish army.

Aili Toivanen, 92, told AP she was forced to leave her home twice over the various wars. Both times, her family was told by Finnish soldiers that they had one hour to pack their belongings.

The first time, she looked back and saw her home burning — set on fire by Finnish soldiers who did not want to leave anything behind, she said. The second time, she said, the Soviet air force bombed the family’s departing train and they jumped out, hiding in ditches before they took refuge in Kuopio.

When Putin invaded Ukraine in 2022, she said, with tears in her eyes, that she worried she would have to leave her home for a third time.

Finns feel their country is worth fighting for

At the shelter in Kuopio, thousands of people filed in, including schoolchildren and university students.

“Kids would need to know this, because they might have to do something alone. The adults can’t always help,” said Amanda Hill, 11, whose school studied in the shelter for the day.

Sitting on the floor of the shelter with his fellow conscripts, Pietikainen explained why it’s not crazy to practice what happens in a crisis.

“We’re Finns, so we’re kind of pessimistic about life in a way,” but history shows what can happen with Russia, he said.

When it comes to the threats from Moscow, Muhonen said, “don’t believe what they say but observe what they do.”

President Donald Trump has said that the US is prepared to launch another attack on Iran at “any time”.

"We took out all of the new equipment that they tried to build along the Strait of Hormuz - some defensive, some offensive,” he told reporters in the Oval Office on Wednesday.

“It was a very heavy attack last night, and we're prepared to do another one any time we want.” He added that a renewed campaign would not last “too long”.

It came as Iranians and others in the region feared a return of the conflict in earnest after the biggest exchange of fire between Tehran and Washington since July.

US attacks hit the southern coast of Iran while Tehran hit back at US assets in Bahrain, Jordan, Kuwait and Iraq.

Iran accused Washington of hitting a wedding party, killing four people and wounding dozens, while its health minister later said 18 people in total had been killed and 108 injured in the latest wave of US strikes.

The US military said the targets of its attacks were air defences, radar systems, maritime assets, mine-laying capabilities and communications sites on Tuesday.

Kelly Osbourne has shared an update on her mental and physical health following the death of her father and intense public scrutiny over her appearance.

Osbourne has admitted that she was struggling following the death of her father, rocker Ozzy Osbourne, in July 2025.

“I didn’t navigate it – I wasn’t well,” Osbourne told Hello!. “How can you navigate something so cruel when you're so sick? I'm getting a lot better. I've got all the help I need and I’m grateful for the support I have in my life.”

The 41-year-old said she’s doing better now, over a year later, but added that healing isn’t linear and her physical and mental health are “not going to be fixed in a day.”

“It’s one foot in front of the other,” she told the publication. “You've got to fix the head before you can fix the body. It's a slow process. It's going to take me a minute. I'm not going to be fixed in a day. I'm not going to be fixed on one therapy session. This is a lifetime of work I've got to do and continue to do for the rest of my life.

open image in gallery Kelly Osbourne, pictured here with her mother Sharon in February 2026, has been on the receiving end of criticism over her appearance following the death of her father Ozzy ( Getty )

“It's great discovering things about yourself [in therapy], and the reasons why I do certain things that stem from my childhood. You go all the way back and you're like: ‘Oh my god, that's why I do that. That's crazy.’ I'm getting to know myself in a whole new way, but it's a lot more healthy, I can tell you that.”

Osbourne addressed fans and critics on her Instagram earlier this year after she made an appearance at the Brit Awards to honor her late father. Instead of focusing on the tribute to the late Black Sabbath rocker, many on social media focused on his daughter’s appearance.

After the show, Osbourne wrote on her Instagram Stories: “There is a special kind of cruelty in harming someone who is clearly going through something.

open image in gallery Kelly Osbourne has spoken out about struggling with her health after the death of her father, Ozzy ( PA Wire )

“Kicking me while I’m down, doubting my pain, spreading my struggles as gossip, and turning your back when I need support and love most.

“None of it proves strength; it only reveals a profound absence of compassion and character. I’m currently going through the hardest time in my life. I should not even have to defend myself. But I won’t sit here and allow myself to be dehumanized in such a way!”

Last December, she posted a since-deleted Instagram video in which she addressed those who criticized her weight loss and said: “all those people, f*** off.”

The former co-host of The View said: “To the people who keep thinking they're being funny and mean by writing comments like ‘Are you ill,’ or ‘Get off Ozempic, you don't look right,’ my dad just died, and I’m doing the best that I can, and the only thing I have to live for right now is my family.”

News.title: Burnham risks Truss moment, warn bond traders
News.content:
Andy Burnham risks a Liz Truss-style market meltdown unless he presents a credible plan to pay for his agenda, bond traders have warned.

Investors said the Prime Minister faces further spikes in borrowing costs unless he outlines tax rises or spending cuts to fund his major policies.

UK borrowing costs have surged to multi-decade highs this week amid a global bond market sell-off. However, investors are particularly concerned about Mr Burnham’s fiscal agenda before his first Budget next month.

Al Cattermole, a portfolio manager at Swiss private bank Mirabaud, said investors were “unclear” about the Prime Minister’s plans and how he would pay for them.

He said: “If you have a lack of credibility about your spending plan and how that will be funded, then you would get spikes in yields similar to [what] we saw during the Liz Truss episode.

“That was about unfunded fiscal spending. And if you get that again, then there is concern about that.”

Mr Burnham refused to rule out increasing borrowing during his first Prime Minister’s Questions on Wednesday despite recent market turmoil.

Jim Athey, a portfolio manager at Marlborough Investment, said: “Spending cuts are the thing the market wants to hear.

“It would go a long way if this Government were to recognise that it is a challenge that needs addressing – that the path we are on in terms of welfare spending is completely unsustainable.”

He added: “The market knows that, and the market wants to hear that the Government understands that.”

Lord Jim O’Neill said earlier that the Prime Minister must “get real” and cut public spending in order to ease pressure in the bond market.

The cost of long-term government borrowing hit its highest level since 1998 on Wednesday, increasing the strain on the public finances as John Healey, the new Chancellor, prepares for the Budget.

The 10-year gilt yield – a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money – has risen to its highest point since 2007.

News.title: H5N1 hits US mink farms, sparking calls for an urgent cull
News.content:
H5N1 has been detected on a US mink farm for the first time, igniting fears the infected animals could present a human pandemic risk.

The bird flu virus, which has “jumped” from birds to numerous mammal species and infected hundreds of people in recent years, was detected in at least six mink on a farm in Utah in mid-August, according to a notification from the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) released over the weekend.

Mink in captivity have previously been described as pandemic “time bombs”. The size and density of the farms gives invading viruses a perfect environment in which to mutate. Mink also have strikingly similar respiratory systems to humans, which greatly increases the human risk.

The animals are farmed for their fur, which is then typically exported to fashion manufacturers in China, Hong Kong, and Russia and used in items like coats and scarves.

Scientists have long warned that if H5N1 acquires the ability to spread efficiently between people, it could trigger a human pandemic.

“Avian influenza viruses tend to replicate pretty poorly in humans and don’t really have the right sort of properties that allow them to transmit from person to person.

“If H5N1 were to cause a pandemic, it would need to make quite a lot of changes, and there’s a real concern that mink, particularly farmed mink, have a lot of the features that could drive the evolution of H5N1,” Dr Tom Peacock, a virologist at The Pirbright Institute, told The Telegraph.

News.title: Collapsing child vaccination in South Africa ‘a public health emergency’
News.content:
Plummeting child immunisation rates are now a public health emergency in South Africa and risk causing outbreaks of preventable but potentially deadly childhood diseases, the government has said.

The proportion of children under one who have received no vaccinations has trebled in the past decade to nearly a third of infants in South Africa.

Mistrust of vaccines and growing ignorance about the benefits of childhood immunisations risk undoing years of progress made by one of the continent’s most effective health systems.

Outbreaks of measles, diphtheria and whooping cough this year have all been linked to poor immunisation rates and are evidence that herd immunity is breaking down, officials warned.

An alert from the department for health said the proportion of unvaccinated infants had hit 36.3 per cent in the first four months of 2026, up from 12.1 per cent in 2017.

The department warned the jump was “effectively tripling the number of completely unvaccinated children and leaving hundreds of thousands of infants at risk of life-threatening illnesses”.

Coverage of the six-in-one hexavalent infant vaccine that protects against diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough, polio, meningitis, and hepatitis B declined from 87 per cent to 60.5 per cent over the same period.

Officials said the shortfall was caused by a lack of people coming forward to bring their children for jabs and was not due to any shortage of vaccines.

Dr Nonhlanhla Ndlovu, deputy director general of South Africa’s health department, told the state broadcaster that parents had a poor understanding of the public health benefits of childhood jabs.

She said: “The second one that comes out is the issue of public trust, in terms of the safety of the vaccines, but also the trust in terms of our systems.”

“Theses vaccines are very safe and we have seen the gains that we have had in our years before and now that is changing.

“The benefit of vaccines far outweigh anything we can talk about in public health. We need them to come back and bring the children for immunisation.”

News.title: Man City sign Enzo Fernandez for £125m to end transfer saga of the summer
News.content:
It is expected to be another busy deadline day in the Premier League, with many clubs still hoping to finalise deals before the transfer window shuts at 11pm. Here, Telegraph Sport identifies 10 potential high-profile moves that could yet go through.

Julian Alvarez to Barcelona… or Arsenal

This has been the most dramatic and relentless saga of the European transfer window. The situation, as far as we understand it, is as follows: Barcelona want Alvarez and Alvarez wants Barcelona, but Atletico Madrid refuse to sell him to Barcelona. Arsenal want Alvarez, and Atletico are more open to selling him to Arsenal, but Alvarez only wants Barcelona. For a move to happen, it will require one party to change their mind. Either Atletico decides to sell to Barcelona, or Alvarez decides he will join Arsenal.

Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City

Another long-running saga. Chelsea are well aware of City’s interest in Fernandez but want a massive fee for the Argentina international, having initially valued him at £120m. City have the cash and the space in the squad after saying goodbye to Rodri, Tijani Reijnders, Nico Gonzalez and Bernardo Silva this summer. Fernandez has not featured in Chelsea’s last two games.

Lamine Camara to Chelsea

As reported by Telegraph Sport last week, Chelsea have identified Monaco midfielder Camara as a target amid the uncertainty over Fernandez’s future. French reports on Monday suggested the move may have stalled, however. The clock is ticking.

Iliman Ndiaye to Manchester City

Spurs had been working on a deal to sign Ndiaye from Everton but they now appear to have fallen behind City in the race for the winger, as a consequence of City failing in their attempt to sign Cody Gakpo from Liverpool. City are ready to complete the hijack on deadline day.

Ismaila Sarr to Liverpool

A deal that, as of Monday night, is regarded as unlikely to happen. As with their interest in Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh, Liverpool have so far been unable to strike a deal with Crystal Palace for Sarr, who scored 21 goals in 45 games last season. Liverpool would only allow Gakpo to leave if a replacement, such as Sarr, can be signed.

News.title: Borrowing cost surge leaves Healey with £10bn headache
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs have surged at one of the fastest paces in the world in a move that threatens to blow a near £10bn hole in Chancellor John Healey’s fiscal plans.

Interest rates on 10-year gilts, a benchmark for Treasury borrowing costs, rose to the highest level since 2008 on Tuesday amid a global bond market rout.

Britain’s cost to borrow over 20 years rose to its highest level since 1998, signalling growing stress in the market.

Government borrowing costs around the world have climbed sharply in recent weeks, amid concerns about unsustainable debts and persistent inflation.

However, Britain suffered the biggest increase in bond yields in the G7 on Tuesday as economists warned that investors were particularly nervous ahead of Mr Healey’s first Budget.

News.title: Arsenal maintain perfect start but lack firepower of rivals
News.content:
Bukayo Saka maintained Arsenal’s perfect start to the season, but Mikel Arteta appeared to acknowledge that the Premier League champions are in danger of leaving themselves short in attack.

There is still time for Arteta to add another forward to his squad and whether he does so or not could be important, with the transfer window closing on Tuesday night.

Having sold Leandro Trossard and with Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus on the verge of moves away, Arsenal appear light of forward options.

Lyon winger Malick Fofana has been offered to the club, but he is an underwhelming target given Morgan Rogers and Vinícius Júnior were pursued earlier in the summer.

“We are trying to improve the squad,” Arteta, the Arsenal head coach, said. “Until Tuesday night, we’re going to try to do that. I’ve been disconnected from the world for 24 hours because I think my energy and focus has to be on the match. I will give it [my energy] now.”

Asked if he currently has enough depth in forward positions, Arteta added: “It depends if everybody is fit or not. We know that the depth has to be really big when you are fighting for four competitions. So we’re going to try to do that.”

News.title: Manchester United’s attack may be their best form of defence this season
News.content:
Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick in what was another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

In the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “new signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

Sports.title: Arsenal ‘made approach to sign Inter Milan captain Lautaro Martinez as Julian Alvarez and Victor Osimhen alternative’
Sports.content:
ARSENAL reportedly made a play for Lautaro Martinez after realising they wouldn’t be able to land Julian Alvarez.

The Gunners were hopeful of convincing the wantaway Atletico Madrid ace to join them this summer in a blockbuster transfer.



But the former Manchester City striker ended up staying in the Spanish capital, where he faces an uncertain future.

And it’s claimed that Gunners boss Mikel Arteta, who was also linked with a swoop for Galatasaray‘s Victor Osimhen, explored the possibility of bringing Martinez to the Emirates after it became clear Alvarez would be going nowhere.



That’s according to The Daily Mail, who claim Gunners assistant coach Gabriel Heinze reached out to his fellow Argentine to gauge his interest in coming to the Premier League.

The north Londoners’ reported aspirations of a late swoop for Martinez are said to have been emphatically shot down by Italian champions Inter Milan.



Arsenal would’ve been hard-pressed to convince the striker, who broke England fans’ hearts in the World Cup semi-final, to jump ship as he’d previously snubbed a potential move to Barcelona.

In May, he said of his future: “No doubt I would like to retire at this club.

“It’s hard for me to imagine myself anywhere else these days.

“You never know in football but if they don’t kick me out, I’m staying here.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

When pressed on Barca’s pursuit of his services, Martinez told Sky Italia: “The rumours were true.

“But in the end, I wanted to stay here with my teammates, with these people, with these fans who have always been magnificent to me.

“It’s definitely a great pleasure, a great honour, and a huge satisfaction because you’re always working to improve, to move forward, to become better.



“When these offers or calls from these huge clubs arrive, they’re always welcome. It’s a very important thing.

“Now I’m in a city that has supported me incredibly since day one.

“I have a restaurant, my kids go to school. I’ll always be here because I feel good, because I’m happy.

Arsenal will be back in action on Sunday afternoon, welcoming big-spending Chelsea to the Emirates.

Martinez and his Inter team-mates, meanwhile, will face Napoli at the San Siro on Saturday evening.

Sports.title: Ollie Watkins’ wife Ellie chokes up as she bids Aston Villa farewell before England star scores on Al-Hilal debut
Sports.content:
OLLIE WATKINS’ wife Ellie fought back tears as she issued an emotional farewell to Aston Villa after moving to Saudi Arabia.

Watkins, 30, moved to Al-Hilal after six glittering years at Villa that saw him registering 108 goals and 47 assists in 278 appearances that included Champions League outings and a Europa League triumph.



The striker’s exit from Villa Park included a short period of acrimony as he refused to play in the Premier League opener at Brighton that saw Unai Emery’s side getting thrashed 4-0 in a disastrous start .

But the England international returned to apologise to Villa manager Emery before his switch to the Middle East was confirmed and later issued a touching farewell video to the fans.



Ellie, 30, followed suit after she, her husband and their children Amara, 4, and Marley, 3 arrived in Riyadh.

The content creator shared a clip on TikTok where she choked up as she discussed how hard it’s been leaving their lives in the UK.

Ellie said: “Okay, well that wasn’t on my bingo card for 2026.

“We are in Riyadh, we arrived in Saudi last night and I think I’m still in shock to be honest like how life can change so quickly but that is the joys of football.

“I’ve always actually said how lucky I think we are because we’ve been at Villa for six years which in football terms is actually quite a long time.

“We’ve had our children there, we’ve had quite big life events so it feels bittersweet to me. I loved my life there, I settled so well and made the most amazing friends.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“So I am feeling quite emotional about leaving that behind. But I am excited for a change of scenery, I think it’s going to be amazing for the kids and I think they are going to have the best time ever.

“Once we are settled and we know what we are doing, it will all be good. Getting on with our new life in Saudi, so exciting times.

“I’m also feeling a little nervous but I remember feeling like that when we moved to Birmingham so hopefully you can follow my journey in Saudi.”

Watkins enjoyed a glittering start to life at Al-Hilal as he scored on his debut on Tuesday that led to a 3-0 victory over Al-Ahli.



The centre-forward has linked up with a number of notable names, such as Kalidou Koulibaly, Theo Hernandez, Yassine Bounou, Ruben Neves, Sergej Milinkovic-Savic and Crysencio Summerville.

They are also expected to be joined by Gabriel Martinelli, who is heading out of Arsenal.

Sports.title: Man Utd fans call for Jason Wilcox to QUIT after Red Devils failed to sign new left back in poor end to transfer window
Sports.content:
DISGRUNTLED Manchester United fans have called for Jason Wilcox to RESIGN after the club’s underwhelming transfer window.

The Red Devils revamped their midfield by bringing in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba for a combined £149million.



However, issues in defence and attack, including the need for a new striker and a very pressing need for a new left-back, failed to be addressed by club transfer chiefs.

Fans were left disappointed with this reality in a window where many felt more was needed to cope with the rigours of also playing Champions League football.



SunSport’s Man Utd correspondent Samuel Luckhurst rated the window as a 6/10, arguing this term “could be a season of consolidation” in maintaining a place in the top four, rather than a title challenge.

But Man Utd technical director Jason Wilcox has been called out online.

Meanwhile, sensational reports have also claimed the club’s director of recruitment Christopher Vivell could also be on his way out.

Such a suggestion sparked an increase in ire from sections of the fanbase, with one saying: “We’re all wearing this same face after seeing this transfer market. #Berradaout. #WilcoxOut.”

A second said: “I don’t care what happens anymore. This clown (Wilcox) needs to be sacked. NOW!!!”

A third added: “Vivell will 100 per cent leave. He can’t work with the absolute clowns he is surrounded by. Why is it never the dummies that leave?!”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Another said: “Sack the f***ing lot of them, clown show FC.”

A fifth fumed: “Don’t fall for it either… Net spend of £85m this summer and they want you to believe they will spend £500m next year? Disgusting c***s they really are. Every bit of failure is on Ineos this season.”

Bayern Munich were linked with Vivell last month as they seek a replacement for chief scout Nils Schmadtke, who could be on his way out of the Bavarian club.

Though Bayern chief Max Eberl played down those rumours, at least for the time being, as he said: “Nils has one year left on his contract, just like I do.

“We shouldn’t be defaming people. That’s a touch too much for me right now.”



Vivell, 39, joined Man Utd in 2024 – the same year as Wilcox – having previously been the technical director at Chelsea between 2022 and 2023.

The German was also the technical director at RB Leipzig between 2020 and 2022, and was a scout for the Bundesliga side for five years before that, having started scouting at Hoffenheim in 2010.

Man Utd beat Ipswich 5-2 at Old Trafford last weekend but lost away to Hull in their opening game of the season.

They visit Everton next before hosting Azerbaijani side, Sabah, in the Champions League, followed by the Manchester City, also at home.

Sports.title: Chelsea and Tottenham leave Arsenal and Man Utd in their wake as winners and losers of summer transfer window revealed
Sports.content:
IT was the maddest, biggest, most astonishing summer transfer window of all time.

Record-breaking sums and huge squad overhauls, with the drama extending to two hours after the deadline as Everton’s big striker signing changed his mind after the last minute.



As the dust settles, the debates on who were the Prem winners and losers will intensify.

SunSport sifts through the chaos to identify those with something to smile about. And those left with scowls.



WINNERS

Chelsea:

Even by Stamford Bridge standards, this has been a stunning summer of shifting sands.

But while midfield depth may be an issue – given the injury records of Moises Caicedo, Romeo Lavia and Reece James and the collapse of the deal for Monaco’s Lamine Camara – new boss Xabi Alonso seems to have all his other ducks in a row.

Morgan Rogers’ £117m arrival has already paid off alongside Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer, Maxence Lacroix is utterly at home at centre-halves, while Blues fans like the look of full-backs Marco Palestra and Pep Chavarria.

Even the signing Chelsea did not want to make, before Robert Sanchez’ failings made the move for Emi Martinez a no-brainer, has boosted the squad.

Hull:

The Tigers had two options after their unexpected promotion.

They could have taken the easy way out, spent a few bob, accepted their fate, used the guaranteed £220m over the next three years to give them a platform to come back stronger.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Instead, it’s a copy of the playbook that saw Sunderland exceed all expectations last summer – and then some.

In total, 18 new players and the third-highest net spend in the Prem. They even let the bloke who scored their winner at Coventry on Saturday go out on loan on deadline day. Full marks for ambition.

Liverpool:

Bradley Barcola’s £123m arrival was the landmark deal of the Anfield summer – but Andoni Iraola putting his foot down to keep Cody Gakpo might be equally important.

Spaniard Victor Munoz has already made a good impression, winning the penalty that earned a point at Newcastle on the opening weekend before scoring the leveller against Forest on Saturday.

Young Frenchman Jeremy Jacquet could be the partner to keep Virgil van Dijk fresh for the fight at the back, while there are doubts about both full-backs.



Yet if Alexander Isak can profit from the men on either flank, Liverpool could be back in the title mix.

Manchester City:

Life after Pep was always going to be different, yet few could have imagined quite how different.

Overhauling the entire midfield – at a cost of just £327m – was a signal of City’s laser focus on giving Enzo Maresca the chance to get off to a trophy-winning start.

But while City have lost the experience of Rodri, they look to have plenty of goals in them – as long as Erling Haaland stays fit.



Enzo Fernandez will add midfield goals, Iliman Ndiaye something different to the mix, while Rayan Cherki already looks in the mood to make this a launchpad season.

Tottenham:

Well, they should be, anyway, after an unprecedented summer splurge in North London.

This is “Roberto De Zerbi’s Tottenham”, in every sense, all 10 new recruits bearing the manager’s mark.

Now the onus is on the Italian manager to turn the ingredients he put in the pot into something tasty – although there has been a distinct lack of seasoning so far.

Spurs fans have reason to be demanding and that will put pressure on Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Savio and Omar Marmoush in particular.



De Zerbi must make sure they aren’t “N17th” again.

LOSERS

Arsenal:

The expectation was that the champions would improve from a position of strength.

Instead, while Ezri Konsa and Bruno Guimaraes add to the previous strong points of Mikel Arteta’s side, his forward options look weaker.

For all the efforts to land Vinicius Jr, Arsenal look like they were played by the Brazilian and his representatives, leaving Greek winger Christos Solis as the only attacking reinforcement.

Meanwhile, Arsenal allowed Gabriel Jesus, Leandro Trossard and Reiss Nelson to leave, with Gabriel Martinelli Saudi-bound as well.



Fans are asking big questions of sporting director Andrea Berta. It is hard to argue Arteta has a better squad than he ended last term with.

Aston Villa:

It might look very different in May but for now Unai Emery appears to have been asked to undertake a massive job in building almost an entirely new side from scratch.

Losing six of the 11 players who started the Europa League final feels like a seismic change, even if Emery loves a challenge.

Villa have been slow starters in the past, only to pick up the pace quickly and end up as a potent force in both the Prem and Europe.

This time, though, they need all the new recruits to get up to speed quickly, in the most competitive league in the world.

Crystal Palace:

You’ve got to feel sorry for Pierre Sage, whose spirits are unlikely to be lifted by parsley, rosemary or thyme.

The new Palace boss inherited a side that had lost two of its three star assets last term, with Eberechi Eze leaving for Arsenal and Marc Guehi at Manchester City.

While he did keep Adam Wharton – surely a January target for someone – Sage saw wing-back Daniel Munoz join predecessor Oliver Glasner at Forest and Lacroix’s switch to Chelsea, while Jean-Philippe Mateta unsuccessfully asked Fifa to rip up his contract and Ismaila Sarr is in a right old huff.

Even the Holmesdale Massive are hacked off. Nobody looks to be “glad all over” at Selhurst.

The joke was biting, but fair.

Everton – the only team with more stadiums than strikers. And left-backs. And right-backs.

Over the space of three days, the Toffees moved for Richarlison, Joshua Zirkzee, and Folarin Balogun but were rejected by all of them.

And while few Evertonians will mourn the departure of Beto, selling Iliman Ndiaye to take a punt on Jack Grealish’s second loan spell is hardly a bet you’d put more than a fiver on.

Fans are in uproar – even after making the club backtrack over the proposed sale of Harrison Armstrong – and the mood is beyond dark.



You wonder how much longer David Moyes will put up with being ordered to fight with both hands tied behind his back?

Manchester United:

Yes, a new-look midfield – although Carlos Baleba is still injured and Andrey Santos was dropped after one game.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But other than that, United are pretty much exactly the same as they were, which has left Old Trafford fans wondering what the club is playing at.

Deadline day efforts to find a back-up – or replacement – for Luke Shaw were too little and too late, Diogo Dalot is hardly the ideal choice on the right, while they looked vulnerable to pace through the middle even while beating Ipswich on Sunday.

Sports.title: Tottenham misfit Richarlison lined up for sensational Mo Salah strike partnership as Trabzonspor target late transfer
Sports.content:
TOTTENHAM striker Richarlison has emerged as a shock target for Turkish side Trabzonspor.

The Brazilian has been left in limbo after turning down the chance to join Everton before Tuesday’s transfer deadline.

Richarlison hinted he wanted to stay at Spurs via a bombshell statement that said “no one will ever again decide my future”.



But Tottenham are now braced for a formal approach from Trabzonspor, who want to sign a striker this week.



The Turkish transfer window does not close until on Friday and West Ham striker Pablo is another player on their radar.

Richarlison is thought to be open to the idea of moving to Trabzonspor, but agreeing a fee with Spurs may prove tricky.

Tottenham were set to bank £35million by selling the Brazil forward to Everton before the deal collapsed.

Trabzonspor would be able to offer hefty wages, as shown by the contract that Salah penned with them.

The Egyptian signed a two-year deal in August that is worth £363,000 a week – AFTER TAX.

Club president Ertugrul Dogan was behind Trabzonspor’s push to sign Salah and is expected to play a leading role in the pitch to Richarlison.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

If Richarlison were to depart, he’d join Luka Vuskovic, Cristian Romero and Djed Spence among the big name departures.



Should he remain, he has a fight on his hands to find a role in the team with Spurs signing Savio, Omar Marmoush and Mykhalo Mudryk in attacking positions.

Sports.title: Chelsea transfer window ranked as Xabi Alonso strikes gold with Morgan Rogers but could be left short in key area
Sports.content:
CHELSEA fans were one decision away from a seemingly perfect transfer window.

And that decision was not one of their own but one made by AS Monaco, after pulling out of a deal for midfielder Lamine Camara at the final hour, who was supposed to replace Enzo Fernandez.



Still, the Blues’ first window with Xabi Alonso at the helm is something to be marveled at in terms of incomings, but especially in terms of outgoings.

The signing of Morgan Rogers looks to have given them one of the most dangerous forward lines in the Premier League, with Maxence Lacroix enforcing their defence, and Emiliano Martinez replacing the inconsistent Robert Sanchez in goal.



Those three were joined by the incomings of Marco Palestra, Danny Welbeck, Jordan Henderson, Pep Chavarria, Valentin Barco, Honest Anahor, Geovany Quenda, and Dastan Satpayev.

If they had have replaced the outgoing Fernandez with Camara they would total 12 new players who all bring vastly different qualities.



MORGAN ROGERS – 9

£117m from Aston Villa

Rogers’ signing from Aston Villa has started very brightly, and got everyone talking about Chelsea‘s ‘JP Morgan’ or ‘CPR’ front three.

He has a great relationship with Cole Palmer, who also seems to be back on track and boosted by Rogers’ signing, and has scored and assisted in the Prem already.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

It’s a hefty fee, which makes him the most expensive English player of all time, but so far he looks to be proving his worth.

So far, signing him looks a very smart move from The Blues, and one that could even propel them to the title if things work out.



EMILIANO MARTINEZ – 8

£7.5m from Aston Villa

For such a cheap fee, it’s hard to argue that this will be a bad signing for Chelsea.

Robert Sanchez was incredibly error prone, and Martinez is a proven top-level goalkeeper who has won numerous trophies and individual awards, as well as being a leader and adding experience to the side.

However, he is just as, if not more mistake-prone than Sanchez – and it will be a waiting game to see how much that impacts Chelsea and the value of his signing.

MAXENCE LACROIX – 8

£52m from Crystal Palace

Perhaps a little pricey, but undoubtedly what Chelsea needed at the back.



A Premier League proven defender who is comfortable in a back three system, with recovery pace to burn and of a good age profile for what this Chelsea team need.

The Frenchman has been exceptional so far, and especially strong against Fulham where he bagged an assist.

Admittedly, the Blues defence still looks particularly shaky even with him in it, but the missing Moises Caicedo won’t be helping that one bit.

MARCO PALESTRA – 7

£43m from Bologna

The Italian wingback has already been dubbed the ‘next Marcos Alonso‘ at Stamford Bridge.



Problem with that being, he was great going forward, but had obvious shortcomings in defence – something Palestra seems to share with him,

For £43m, the upside to his signing certainly outweights the potential downside, and he looks a promising signing from pre-season despite picking up an injury that has seen him miss the opening two matches of the Premier League.

DANNY WELBECK – 7

£5m from Brighton

What Welbeck brings to this team is obvious, experience and goals.

He will be a good, much-needed leader for Alonso, and has already bagged his first goal in blue in the Carabao Cup.



JORDAN HENDERSON – 7

Free from Brentford

The midfielder is yet to really do anything since joining Chelsea, given his overhanging injury from the World Cup.

That said, he has been taking up something of a coaching role under Alonso and will have a good impact on the dressing room.

Having signed on a free it’s hard to give him a bad mark, and he might even get some minutes in the absence of Fernandez.

VALENTIN BARCO – 8

£33.6m from Strasbourg

Wasn’t given much of a chance by fans when he first signed, but actually already looks a very astute signing.

He’s versatile, and can play as a full-back or a midfielder, shining in the Carabao Cup arguably more than any other player – dubbed a mix of Kevin De Bruyne and N’Golo Kante.



If he turns out to be anywhere near as good as either of those, he will be a success.

PEP CHAVARRIA – 7

£16.3m from Rayo Vallecano

Compared mostly to Cesar Azpilicueta, Chavarria has been solid when he has played for Chelsea so far.

He seems like largely a backup option on the left to the likes of Jorrel Hato and Marco Palestra, but a solid one nonetheless when he has played, and again is the right age profile for what Chelsea needed in this window.

GEOVANY QUENDA – 7

£44m from Sporting

A very, very exciting winger who can also play wingback under Xabi Alonso.



He is versatile and looks fresh in the same way Estevao did when he was breaking onto the scene at Stamford Bridge last season.

When he has played he looks direct and willing to take on his man, and you would imagine he is someone that if Chelsea do ever need to offload that they will profit on.

DASTAN SATPAYEV – 8

£3.5m from Kairat Almaty

Is spending the season on loan at Burnley, but it’s hard to imagine the Blues’ ‘baby Aguero’ not at least turning them a profit in the future.

He has also looked promising when he has actually played under Alonso, scoring a goal in pre-season.



HONEST ANAHOR – ?

£40m from Atalanta

Is supposedly the next best defender to come out of Serie A, and will spend this season at Crystal Palace before joining Chelsea in 2027.

£40m is a lot of money for a centre-back who will need to impress at Palace this season.

OVERALL RATING: 8/10

Xabi Alonso has been given the ‘manager’ title at Stamford Bridge, and it shows.

He has addressed almost every problem area in the squad, apart from the central midfield position where the late departure of Enzo Fernandez has left a hole.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

A new goalkeeper in Emi Martinez and the additions of Maxence Lacroix and Morgan Rogers address issues from qualitative depth to a lack of experience from last season, and seem to suit Alonso’s system nicely.

Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson should provide experience and squad depth, while Chelsea have also sold brilliantly and still brought promising youth in the form of Anahor, Quenda and Satpayev, who will likely make them a profit or become superstars themselves.

Sports.title: Why Man Utd struggle to sell players – one legend departed for ‘peanuts’ and serial winners have left for cut-price fees
Sports.content:
THIRTY-ONE years ago, Manchester United sold three first-teamers and did not make a single signing.

If social media existed in the summer of 1995, the internet might have crashed. Paul Ince, Andrei Kanchelskis and Mark Hughes, integral to Alex Ferguson’s first great side, each had a unique bond with the fanbase.



United banked £14million for the trio, an enormous sum three years after the Premier League’s inception. They have not had many summers like it since.

Ideally, United would have jettisoned a midfielder, a winger and a forward this summer, too. Manuel Ugarte, Marcus Rashford and Joshua Zirkzee were unshiftable.



For a club that received a world record fee for Cristiano Ronaldo in 2009, United are historically bad sellers.

They gave David Beckham away for “peanuts” to Real Madrid at the height of the Galactico era. Anthony Martial, Paul Pogba and Jadon Sancho signed for deals worth a combined £219.9m within a six-year period and were released.



There is no short answer to why United are bad at selling. You could write a hefty tome or record a podcast series on their poor record and why they struggle to fetch fees for senior players.

It was not even 18 months ago that United suffered their worst season in 51 years. So their current squad is not teeming with sellable assets and hardly anyone is capable of raking in a profit.

Altay Bayindir, loaned to Celta Vigo, is renowned for letting in goals. Joshua Zirkzee, the subject of a desperate loan enquiry from Everton on Tuesday evening, is renowned for not scoring goals.

Of all Everton’s window missteps, selling Beto and moving for Zirkzee should spark sackings. Beto scored five times as many goals as Zirkzee last season.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The extravagant salaries United have put players on made them no-goes. Marcus Rashford is only still at the club as no elite European side was prepared to foot his wage bill of £325,000-a-week.

Casemiro saw out his contract as he was immovable. United are bound to encounter the same issue with Mason Mount, into the final two years of his deal and on £250,000 a week.

Jaap Stam, Cristiano Ronaldo, Daley Blind, Chris Smalling and Daniel James would be an obscure five-a-side team. They are also the only players United bought and sold at an eight-figure profit.

Ronaldo, James, Beckham, Angel di Maria, Romelu Lukaku, Scott McTominay, Mason Greenwood, Alejandro Garnacho and Rasmus Hojlund are the only United players to leave for £25m or more.

Of those nine players, four came through the club’s academy. That was the only source of United’s transfer income negotiated this summer, via Toby Collyer and Radek Vitek.



Garnacho, valued north of £85m in 2024, left for £40m in 2025. The most senior sale in the window that just closed was Collyer, starter of three games against Barnsley, Rangers and Steaua Bucharest. The last of those was in January 2025.

United trumpeted the overall £7.6m fee West Brom agreed to pay, with £3m up front. A source said it is “unlikely” the add-ons will be triggered.

The academy sells as United have produced talented professionals for the best part of a century. Andreas Pereira (£10m), James Garner (£15m), Dean Henderson (£20m), Anthony Elanga (£15m) and Garnacho all moved to Premier League clubs before Collyer and Vitek dropped down to the Championship.



In the summer of 2022, United’s only sales were Pereira and Garner. They had been out on loan, so were not damaged by the cataclysmic season with Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and then Ralf Rangnick in the dugout.

Although Ferguson rarely drove a hard bargain, he did not struggle for willing takers. In 2007, Ferguson’s friend Sam Allardyce, had just been installed at Newcastle, who signed Alan Smith for £6m

Roy Keane could barely stomach sharing the same oxygen as Ferguson after United sacked him but still signed five players from his former club during his two-and-a-half years as Sunderland manager.

Steve Bruce, also at Sunderland, gave Wes Brown and John O’Shea a new home in 2011. David Moyes was a sucker for a United reject at Everton.

There were no domestic or Uefa financial rules to comply with back then, either. That was largely the case when Ed Woodward regularly misread a player’s market value.



The die was cast in the summer of 2014. New manager Louis van Gaal was decisive in identifying which players’ faces did not fit, so Woodward sanctioned several sales with little or no negotiating.

Shinji Kagawa left for roughly half the price United paid for him in 2012. Michael Keane and Wilfried Zaha were both flogged for £3m with no sell-on clauses inserted. £16m for Danny Welbeck was, in hindsight, low.

The squad purge continued in Van Gaal’s second summer: £4.25m for Nani, £6m for Jonny Evans and £7.3m for Javier Hernandez. Serial winners sold at a cut price amid mismanagement.



So a precedent was set: United sold on the cheap. Keane moved from Burnley to Everton for £30m in 2017. West Ham bought Hernandez in the same summer for more than double the £7.3m Bayer Leverkusen paid United. Evans was wanted by Manchester City at one stage.

Morgan Schneiderlin (£24m) and Memphis Depay (£21m) left for impressive fees in January 2017. The difference then was United were a resurgent force under Jose Mourinho and the players were cut loose after 18 months, so had suffered little reputational damage.

United banked good fees for Blind (£18.5m) and Sam Johnstone (£10m) in July 2018. Their reputations were enhanced by association with Mourinho and, in Johnstone’s case, emerging from the United academy.

But United regressed in the seller’s market after finishing sixth in 2018-19. Ander Herrera ran down his contract and Lukaku was sold at a minor loss to Inter Milan.



United had a decent 2024 as the majority of their outgoings were academy talents as part of Ineos’s attempts to use it as a cash cow.

There was an obvious market for Aaron Wan-Bissaka, a right back with six-and-a-half years of Premier League experience.

Coming 15th and trophyless in 2025 demanded outgoings. Ruben Amorim’s ‘bomb squad’ made certain players’ positions untenable, though United sold Antony at a considerable loss and failed to obtain a higher fee for Garnacho.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

There was never going to be a fire sale this summer and Michael Carrick’s nature meant anyone ‘for sale’ had a squad role if they stayed.



Ugarte is no Ince and Zirkzee is no Hughes. Rashford has trumped Kanchelskis, though.

Sports.title: Inside Enzo Fernandez’s love life, from brief split with childhood sweetheart to Wanda Nara slipping into his DM’s
Sports.content:
ENZO FERNANDEZ has joined Man City in a joint British record transfer.

The Argentine midfielder, 25, swapped Stamford Bridge for the Etihad on transfer deadline day for £125million.



The move will see Enzo uprooting his family, from London to Manchester, as he settles in to his new club.

Away from the pitch, the World Cup winner is in a longterm relationship with stunning influencer, Valentina Cervantes.



The high school sweethearts share two children, Olivia and Benjamin.

However, there was trouble in paradise when Enzo and Valentina briefly split in late 2024.

They reconciled in 2025, but then he found himself in an alleged love triangle with Wanda Nara.

And Valentina was also said to be charmed by an unnamed Argentina international.

Enzo’s love life has certainly been complicated in the last few years.

Young love

Valentina and Enzo met in 2018 and soon became love struck teenagers in Buenos Aires.



She said: “I met Enzo when he was 16, and at 17 we moved in together. We’re both from San Martín, we have a group of friends in common.

“He used to go on vacation to Mar del Tuyú, and in 2018 I went there with my family, and that’s when I really got to know him.

“We’d see each other on the beach, we talked that summer, and it wasn’t until the end of the year that we actually got together. For our first date, he invited me to the nephew’s country house, which was for his birthday.”



Olivia, their first born, arrived in 2020, and they soon became young parents.

She revealed: “When Olivia was born, we were living in a studio apartment in Urquiza, which Enzo’s agent paid for.

“During the pandemic, the three of us were there, and I was working at a call centre, while he didn’t have a salary yet. At that time, we bought our daughter’s used clothes on Facebook Marketplace.

“We used to take the bus; Enzo would get off at General Paz and catch another one to River, and I’d keep going to the Urquiza station because I worked downtown at an empanada shop, and later at the call centre near the Obelisk.”

In 2022, Enzo moved from River Plate to Benfica. Valentina and Olivia uprooted to Lisbon to start a new life.



But, they weren’t there long. Some five months after he made his debut for the Portuguese giants, Enzo was transferred again.

This time, it was Chelsea calling in a then British record £107million deal.

Valentina and Olivia followed once more, before they could catch their breath in Portugal.

In October 2023, Enzo and Valentina welcomed a son to their brood, when Benjamin was born.



On the surface, they seemed to be the happiest of families. But, underneath the surface, cracks were beginning to show.

A brief split

In November 2024, Enzo and Valentina had parted ways.

Argentine journalist Julieta Argenta claimed that Fernandez told her he wanted to “live alone”.

She added context in a social media post, writing: “They’re still family, but he feels the need to experience the stage he skipped by choosing family early on.”



Valentina admitted she was blindsided by the break-up in an interview with Paparazzi magazine.

She said: “Everything was fine and suddenly one day he told me that he didn’t want to be anymore. There are things that I still have to process, but that’s it, I accepted it.”

Valentina confessed that she cried for five minutes when Fernandez told her about the breakup, but her background of being the daughter of separated parents shaped her perspective.



It got complicated

Barely three months after they went their separate ways, Enzo seemingly had a change of heart.

They were seen walking around London kissing and holding hands, and it seemed their romance was back on

But, reports in Argentina claimed that he moved to repair his relationship, after finding out an unnamed Argentina international team-mate had tried to seduce Valentina.

In an explosive claim about the midfielder’s apparent decision to backtrack on his decision, journalist Daniel Fava revealed it was linked to a move by another member of Argentina’s winning World Cup squad on Enzo’s long-time partner.

Fava said on TV show A la tarde in January 2025: “In the last few hours there’s been a reconciliation with his ex-partner Valentina Cervantes. They’re giving things another go.”



He added: “The information I have is that Enzo Fernandez is desperately trying to win her back because he’s heard that a fellow world champion is sniffing around her.”

The Argentine journalist offered no further clues about the identity of the mystery player he was pointing the finger at, or whether he even knew his name.



After a colleague interrupted to say: “What you’re saying is that he prefers to get back with her than see another man jumping in,” he said of Valentina: “Today she’s prettier than ever.

“Since the separation she has gained a new sex appeal and energy” before making a second bombshell claim “more than one footballer” had contacted her over social media since the shock split.

A fly in the ointment

Not long after Enzo and Valentina had rekindled their romance, it was claimed that blonde beauty Wanda Nara had slipped into his DM’s.

Wanda hosts Celebrity Masterchef in her homeland, and back in October 2025 Valentina was a contestant on the show.

Reports in Argentina said Wanda and Valentina appeared frosty with each other, and apparently for good reason too.



According to La Nacion, Wanda sent Enzo a flirty message that read: “I just saw you around the neighbourhood, write to me if you want.”

It’s claimed that, rather than respond, he immediately showed the message to Valentina.

And this is allegedly what annoyed Wanda.



Valentina blasted reports of alleged messages between her man and Wanda.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

She said: “Yes, I saw it. No, as far as I know, I haven’t seen any messages.

“No, no, Enzo never spoke to me about anything. No, he never spoke to me about any of that.”

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Late Arsenal deal completed, Jadon Sancho bombshell, Man Utd's £150m plan
Sports.content:
The latest transfer news from the Premier League and the football world, including updates on Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester United's plans

The summer transfer window might have already shut in England, but several clubs across the continent are still scrambling to get key deals over the line.

However, in terms of the Premier League, it was another history-making window, as clubs smashed their summer transfer record with over £3.3bn spent.

More than half of the top-flight sides broke their transfer records in a summer window featuring four of the top-flight’s five most expensive ever deals.

The biggest deals saw Manchester City complete the signing of Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea for £125m, while Liverpool paid £120m for Bradley Barcola.

But there still could be more deals to come as Gabriel Martinelli has completed his medical ahead of a £60m move to Al-Hilal.

Manchester United striker Chido Obi is set to join Eredivisie side Willem II on loan, subject to registration, while ambitious Dubai side Arabian Falcons are preparing a pitch for free agent Jadon Sancho to join them.

And looking ahead to next summer, it is already being claimed that Manchester United will look to strengthen their defence next year, and Liverpool could move for Lamine Camara.

Sports.title: Transfer news: Man Utd deal announced, Arsenal double move, Folarin Balogun bombshell
Sports.content:
Latest transfer news from Manchester United, Arsenal, Liverpool and more - as Premier League clubs break summer window record with £3.2billion spend

After a major summer of spending, the Premier League's summer transfer window drew to a close at 11pm on Tuesday evening. It was a record-shattering couple of months across the UK, with a total exceeding £3.2billion exceeded through deals.

Manchester City and Chelsea agreed a £125m deal for Enzo Fernandez, with the wantaway midfielder finally leaving Stamford Bridge after months of speculation regarding his future. The Cityzens also welcomed Iliman Ndiaye to their ranks in a £65m move, further bolstering Enzo Maresca's choice.

Sunderland's approach of Malick Fofana also dominated the headlines on Tuesday, with what should have been a straightforward move turning into quite the saga when Crystal Palace threatened to hijack the Black Cats' move.

With Kyril Louis-Dreyfus flying to Lyon to persuade the 21-year-old winger to join his project at the Stadium of Light, Fofana gave Sunderland the green-light to put the wheels in motion on a move, forced to submit a dealsheet to ensure a transfer due to the last-minute nature of his decision.

In West London, AS Monaco also knocked back Chelsea's £47m move for Lamine Camara in dramatic fashion. Everything had been agreed between the two clubs, when Monaco pulled the plug with just minutes to go until the deadline - with Everton's endeavours of securing Folarin Balogun having a knock-on effect.

Chelsea were reportedly left fuming with the incredibly unprofessional last-minute decision. And Balogun's deal didn't go through anyway, with Monaco's sporting director sensationally claiming it was the striker who walked away from the deal after 'feeling mistreated' during his medical.

Mykhailo Mudryk also joined Tottenham Hotspur on a season-long loan, with both clubs hopeful that the Ukrainian is able to reacclimate to the pace of the Premier League after a two-year lay-off.
