Palace were contacted for comment. Monaco’s sporting director, Thiago Scuro, defended the Ligue 1 side’s actions in a press conference on Wednesday.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

He said: “Around 10pm, in our time here, maybe a bit earlier, Everton realised that OK there is no problem: ‘We are ready to do it. Let’s sign the contract.’ As soon as we got the information, yes, we did come back to Chelsea and told [them]: ‘OK, we have our deal there. There is no deal on Lamine.’ Because it’s also fair to do this. It’s also part of the game.”

He said it was unfair to portray Monaco as “the bad guys in the room”: “Everybody is very fair and nice in the football industry, just Monaco is not. Too much.”

Everton were left with only one recognised striker after Balogun changed his mind over the move to Merseyside and Scuro suggested the US forward was unhappy with how Everton had treated him over his medical.

Sports.title: Premier League transfer talking points: three things we learned from the data
Sports.content:
Premier League clubs have invested more than £3.4bn in players this summer, an increase of 11.9% on last year. There are three aspects of this enormous spending worthy of closer scrutiny.

Priorities on player age have changed

Premier League clubs are spending less on players in the peak 24-27 age band even though those players are increasingly the core of their selections.

As recently as 2021-22, 40% of minutes were taken by players at least 28 years old at the start of the season. That proportion has dropped each year, reaching 26.6% in 2025-26. The reliance on veterans has declined. The bulk of their lost minutes went to players aged between 24 and 27, which is now the dominant age band.

The spend on that key demographic has fallen by 23% since last summer though. Without Manchester City signing the 25-year-old Enzo Fernández for a British transfer record-equalling £125m shortly before the window closed, the drop would have been even greater.

Younger players account for some of the shortfall but a surprisingly high slice of it has gone towards older footballers. The Premier League has invested £323.3m in players aged at least 28, only around £50m shy of the outlay on this age range in the previous three summers combined (£370.5m). Their proportion of the total has not been as high for four years.

How much this increased spending on veterans affects the playing time figures depends in part on the selection decisions of Mikel Arteta. Arsenal signed two 28-year-olds for a combined £126m: Bruno Guimarães (£75m) and Ezri Konsa (£51m). Transfermarkt considers them to be the most expensive central midfielder and centre-back respectively aged over 27 in history.

The three most expensive Premier League signings of the summer before Fernández – Morgan Rogers, Elliot Anderson and Bradley Barcola – were 23 when their deals were completed. With only slightly less spent collectively on footballers who are 22, clubs have gone hard for players on the verge of entering their peak years rather than those in them.

The Premier League is becoming a closed shop

Perhaps the most notable aspect of transfer spending this summer is how much of it has remained within English football. Fourteen of the 19 signings that cost Premier League clubs at least £50m were made from within the division or from relegated West Ham. Where 30.2% of spending remained in the Premier League in summer 2022, the figure hit 39.3% this year.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

With the combined outlay growing by almost £1.5bn in that period, what appears a relatively small percentage shift becomes a significant figure in the accounts. The squad cost ratio rules are unlikely to stem this flow either, because clubs will be happy to sell for inflated fees that can almost only come from within the division.

Barcola was the oldest of the five costliest signings from overseas, with Matias Fernandez-Pardo and Jérémy Jacquet (aged 21), Johan Manzambi (aged 20) and Ayyoub Bouaddi (aged 18) completing the set. The Premier League is able to retain its top stars, its clubs exchanging them among themselves, while having the funds to hoover up the most exciting young talent from elsewhere.

Squad-building trends may be evolving in the Premier League, but the money is here and a significant portion of it is not going anywhere else. English football is starting to become an enclosed ecosystem.

The rest of Europe cannot keep up

Very few clubs across Europe come close to competing financially. The Premier League features a match this weekend between the top two teams in Europe for net spend and it isn’t Arsenal v Chelsea. Liverpool’s trip to Ipswich takes the honour.

The promoted sides have invested enormous sums to try to be competitive. They have all played League One football within the previous eight seasons, yet Real Madrid are the only club from another country with a higher net spend than Hull or Coventry.

The cream of the Premier League crop can probably only move within England. The transfer fee for Rogers (£117m) or Anderson (£116m) was above the net spend of 75 of the 76 top-flight clubs in France, Germany, Italy and Spain. Milan narrowly spent more than the cost of Sandro Tonali (£92.5m) net, but no other side beyond Madrid from mainland Europe did. Most non-English sides would have to have a clearout of talent to raise funds for a single elite player from the Premier League, which isn’t practical.

This financial dominance can be seen in continental competitions. Five English clubs have featured in the past eight Champions League finals, as many teams as the rest of Europe has provided in that time. The Premier League has supplied three of the past four Europa League finalists and three of the past four Conference League winners. This is unlikely to change when relegation favourites in England can outspend all but the very richest clubs overseas.

Sports.title: ‘Get a life’ – Roy Keane’s ‘pet hate’ has Gary Neville, Jamie Carragher and Ian Wright in stitches
Sports.content:
If you are a football fan who gets their phone out at matches to record yourself, well, stay away from Roy Keane.

The Manchester United legend was speaking on the latest edition of The Overlap about his dislike for supporters who do that, leaving his co-hosts in stitches.



4 Keane isn't one for gimmicks, especially excessive use of the phone at football matches Credit: The Overlap

Keane made it very clear that people who record themselves singing songs while walking into games aren't for him.

After acting it out, he said: "Get a life... recording themselves singing about a team."

Keane then grabbed Ian Wright to act as if he and the Arsenal hero were fans walking into a match together.



Wrighty then made it clear he wasn't a fan either, adding the bit that annoys him is when there is a free-kick or a penalty and lots of fans decide to record it.

"Gary [Neville], you know what you do see? You see the camera pan on the crowd if it's a free-kick just outside of the box. Everybody's got their phones out."



Jamie Carragher concluded by bringing up a moment that has been viral since the weekend.

Following Leif Davis' goal to open the scoring at Old Trafford against Manchester United on Sunday.



There is a video of the away fans celebrating with one man looking at his phone, but doesn't begin his celebrations until he hits record on his device.

And on this, Carragher said: "Have you seen the clip of the Ipswich fan? They're all celebrating. Everyone is celebrating, and he's getting his phone out.

"He's not celebrating, then he presses record, and he goes 'Yesssssssssssssssss'".

4 Keane made it clear that phones at football matches are irritating Credit: The Overlap



4 As always, The Overlap was entertaining Credit: The Overlap

4 Carragher also got involved as well Credit: The Overlap

Pet peeve

Given Keane played when there were fewer mobile phones in the stands and there was no social media, so it probably explains why Keane finds it so irritating.

Wright's point about filming free-kicks close to goal and penalties has become a regular thing all across the world.



But it is part of modern football and all supporters can do what they want as long as it isn't banned from the stadium or illegal.

Sports.title: Man United forward Chido Obi set for loan transfer to European club a day after deadline
Sports.content:
Man United forward Chido Obi set for loan transfer to European club a day after deadline

Manchester United youngster Chido Obi will join Dutch side Willem II on a season-long loan, talkSPORT understands.

The 18-year-old forward has made eight first-team appearances for Man United.



2 Obi made his senior debut for United last year Credit: Getty

Obi was also part of the United side that reached the final of last season's FA Youth Cup against Manchester City.

Obi's next step

Having not featured for the first team last term, he's now set to head to the Eredivisie, where he'll hope to get plenty more senior experience under his belt.

Based in the town of Tilburg, Willem II are back in the Dutch top flight after finishing third in the second-tier Eerste Divisie and winning promotion via the play-offs.



The club boast among their former players Man United great Jaap Stam, while current Liverpool and Netherlands captain Virgil van Dijk started out in their youth system.

Willem II are already three games into the new Eredivisie campaign, losing their first two matches 4-1 before picking up their first point with a 2-2 draw against Heerenveen last Sunday.



John Stegeman's men are next in action at home to Excelsior this Saturday coming.

Already making his mark on the international stage

Born in Denmark, Obi has represented the country up to Under-21 level.



However, he has also represented England's Under-17 team, featuring at the 2024 European Under-17 Championship and being named in the Team of the Tournament for his impressive displays.

He's eligible to play for Denmark, England or Nigeria internationally.

Obi joined United from Arsenal later that year, a couple of months before his 17th birthday, with former United defender Phil Jones raving about his talent, describing him as an 'animal' of a player.

2 Obi joined United just under two years ago Credit: Getty



While with the Gunners, he made headlines by racking up ten goals during a 14-3 demolition of Liverpool in an Under-16 match.

He also broke the record for the most goals in an Under-18 Premier League season during the 2023/24 campaign, striking 32 times in 18 outings in total.

Named in the United senior matchday squad for the first time against Tottenham in February last year, he made his first-team debut in that game as a late substitute for Casemiro.

He made six further Premier League appearances in the 2024/25 campaign, becoming United's youngest-ever starter in the competition against Brentford that May.



A player who knows where the net is

Among the goals for United's Under-21s in Premier League 2 last term, finding the net 11 times, Obi came off the bench in the first team's 5-0 pre-season friendly win over Rosenborg in Norway in July.

However, he hasn't been involved in either of United's two Premier League 2 fixtures so far this season.

He's now poised for his first loan spell away from Old Trafford.

Sports.title: Noel Gallagher loves ballsy Enzo Fernandez but thinks Enzo Maresca must build around another diamond
Sports.content:
Noel Gallagher loves ballsy Enzo Fernandez but thinks Enzo Maresca must build around another diamond

Noel Gallagher has hailed Enzo Fernandez's personality and the maverick ability of Rayan Cherki, insisting they are exactly what Manchester City need.

The Oasis megastar joined talkSPORT Drive in the wake of a hugely eventful transfer deadline day, which saw his beloved City pull off the signing of Fernandez from Chelsea at the 11th hour.

6 Fernandez left Chelsea for Man City in a record-equalling Premier League deal on transfer deadline day Credit: PA

After a summer of uncertainty, the midfielder finally joined the Citizens for £125million on deadline day in a record-equalling deal.

It brought an end to an eventful transfer window for Fernandez, who's move to the Etihad looked to be off after Man City missed Chelsea's initial a deadline of 5pm on Friday, August 14 for interested clubs to meet their £120m asking price.

Despite the Blues' stance, the deal accelerated in the final hours of the transfer window and was announced just after the 11pm deadline.

Fernandez wasn't the Citizens' only Deadline Day arrival, with Iliman Ndiaye also signing from Everton in deal worth £65m overall.

The duo join a star-studded Man City side looking to steal back their Premier League crown from Arsenal and once again challenge for silverware on all fronts, with the likes of Erling Haaland and Phil Foden looking to spearhead the charge.

And while Ndiaye and Fernandez only add the new big names in the City dressing room, megafan Gallagher believes another player is the jewel in their crown.

Gallagher: Cherki should be the main man

Gallagher named the dazzling Cherki as Man City's most important player, insisting Enzo Maresca must make him the focal point of his team.

The enigmatic Frenchman has earned a reputation as the Premier League's biggest entertainer after a stunning debut campaign last term, and showcased all of his natural talent in his side's 4-1 win over Crystal Palace.

Cherki netted a mouth-watering brace in the win - with his first goal seeing him dance through the Palace defence before slotting home.

Discussing the 23-year-old's impressive display, Gallagher insisted: “They need to build the team around him.

6 Cherki has proven himself to be box office entertainment over the past year Credit: Getty

6 Gallagher has certainly enjoyed the Frenchman's displays in a Man City shirt Credit: Getty

"That's what I think he needs to be given the licence to, because he can pop up anywhere in the last third of the pitch.

“The [first] goal at Palace - when your team are up there and you can't really see what's going on [from the stands], none of us really knew how he'd managed to get it.

"And even when we came home and watched it back, I was like, ‘How has he done that?'"

Continuing to wax lyrical about Cherki, Gallagher insisted the playmaker's carefree style - which he has previously criticised him for taking too far - makes him the Citizens' biggest weapon.

He added: “He's got that indefinable thing that magicians have. He's gnarly, he says mad stuff, but I mean, he's an absolute diamond.”

Fernandez personality hailed

After naming Cherki as his team's maverick man, Gallagher went on to hail Enzo Fernandez' character as exactly what City need.

6 Fernandez made a pointed celebration after scoring against England in the World Cup semi-finals, and Gallagher is a fan of his personality Credit: Getty

The £125m Argentine has become something of a pantomime villain in English football after he drew the ire of England fans by mocking the Three Lions with a social media post playing their unofficial 'Wonderwall' anthem after Argentina's World Cup semi-final victory.

But with Fernandez's gritty streak also seeing him play a crucial role in Argentina's 2022 World Cup glory, Gallagher insisted his willingness to ruffle feathers makes him perfect for his City team.

The music icon said: “Everybody's now going, ‘Oh, Fernandez, he's this and he's that’. Yeah, he is when you're playing against him.

"But when he's in your team, he's the kind of player that you want.

“I want a Roy Keane-type player. I'm not putting him on the level of Roy Keane, but getting stuck into their midfielders - I want that, and I want that at City because Phil [Foden] ain't gonna do it, Elliot Anderson ain't gonna do it."

Gallagher was also impressed by Fernandez taking the No.17 shirt at Man City - a shirt previously worn by club icon Kevin De Bruyne.

6 Fernandez will wear Kevin De Bruyne's old number at City, who established himself as one of the Premier League's all-time greats in the No.17 shirt Credit: Getty

He added: “This Fernandez kid, I like his vibe, and I'm glad he's here, and I'm glad he took Kevin's shirt because I can guarantee you this, he wouldn't have been offered it.

“I'm glad that he took it because that shows that he's got balls and I like it.”

Future is bright under Man City chairman

Gallagher also shed light on a conversation he had with Man City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak ahead of a summer of transition at the Etihad.

The departure of legendary manager Pep Guardiola was followed by modern-day greats Bernardo Silva and Rodri leaving to join Real Madrid and Barcelona respectively, leaving the Citizens to replace the pillars of their iconic 2023 treble-winning side.

But they have wasted no time in bringing in replacements, with Elliot Anderson first joining in a then British-record £116m move.

His arrival has been followed up by the arrival of Morocco World Cup star Ayyoub Bouaddi in a record Premier League fee for a teenager, before the Deadline Day acquisitions of Ndiaye and Fernandez.

6 Khaldoon Al Mubarak has overseen huge success at Manchester City Credit: Getty

And Gallagher revealed City's summer business has seen chairman Al Mubarak follow up on the succession plan he shared with him at the very start of the summer.

Opening up on their conversation, Gallagher revealed: "I said, ‘How do you see it?’

"And he said, ‘Look, are we going to win 20 trophies in the next ten years? It's highly unlikely. Are we going to win ten trophies in the next ten years? Maybe’

“He said, ‘But all I can promise you is, we are going to build a team that is going to be there. We're going to be there, and we're going to be fighting, and it's not going to fall off, and they're going to do everything they can’.

“He said they were going to spend big in this window, and the players that he outlined to me are - apart from Ndiaye, who nobody saw coming - the exact players he told me he was going to get."

Gallagher continued to hail Al Mubarak as City chairman, who has overseen an era of unprecedented success since assuming his role with Sheikh Mansour's purchase of the club in 2008.

He added: “That guy - he walks it like he talks it. I've had three conversations with him in the last however many years it's been, of how the next five years are going to play out, and he's been true to his word, and he's detailed it almost exactly as it's played out.

“So I can say to City fans, we might not win the league this year, but next year, this team, I mean, even by the end of this year, this team might be flying.

“But next year, with Bouaddi and the team now, the average age is 25 or something. We're ready. We are primed to do it again.”

Sports.title: Noel Gallagher gives surprise review of documentary on Pep Guardiola’s Man City departure
Sports.content:
Noel Gallagher has surprisingly described the documentary about Pep Guardiola's Manchester City exit as an 'uncomfortable watch'.

A lifelong Man City fan, Oasis star Gallagher gave talkSPORT his thoughts on A Beautiful Obsession, the four-part Prime Video series which lifts the lid on Guardiola's final two seasons as manager at the Etihad Stadium.

4 Guardiola said an emotional goodbye to City at the end of last season Credit: Getty

"I haven't seen it all. I've seen a couple of episodes," he told Andy Goldstein and Darren Bent on talkSPORT Drive.

"I went to a screening up here, but it was a very uncomfortable watch for me."

Guardiola 'gave his heart and soul to City'

Reflecting on Guardiola's glittering decade-long association with City, which peaked with an historic treble in the 2023/24 season, Gallagher said: "He gave his heart and soul to the club, and he demands that everybody else around him gives their heart and soul to the club.

"Even fans like me... who are not allowed to say anything, even on the radio.

"But if you're ever in any doubt, his passion for the club is unrivalled. He's full on, 100 per cent, seven days a week, never sleeps...

"He is offended when they lose and he's elated when they win, and he's the real deal.

"But it was a bit of an uncomfortable watch, I've got to say."

Gallagher and Guardiola still in touch

Gallagher revealed that he has spoken to Guardiola since he bid City farewell in May.

"We've had a couple of exchanges," he confirmed.

"He's back in Barcelona. I'll see him next year I would have thought" – perhaps at an Oasis show, after Gallagher hinted at a return to the stage in 2027...

4 Gallagher formed a close friendship with Guardiola Credit: Getty

Gallagher's advice to Foden

One area of the documentary that Gallagher homed in on was Phil Foden's demeanour under Guardiola, noting how he thought the midfielder appeared scared.

"The couple of episodes I've seen, Phil just looks terrified all the way," Gallagher said.

And Gallagher urged Foden to 'relax' and focus on his game, with Enzo Maresca now in the City dugout.

"I didn't feel like he had a good game [in the 4-1 win over Crystal Palace last Friday]," Gallagher continued.

"But when I came back [home] and I watched it back, he actually had a pretty good game.

"But every season now for Phil is massive because the team has been rebuilt [City made two signings on deadline day alone, including Enzo Fernandez for £125m] and he's now got to fight for his place again.

4 Foden played a key part in City's recent victory over Palace Credit: Getty

"But that's a good thing. He's got the world at his feet; he's got the fans behind him; it's up to him.

"You see Nico O'Reilly looks like he's a Rolls-Royce of a player. I think Phil feels [the pressure] a bit more.

"I think Phil needs to relax and just play football.

"We have to remember he's never really played in his preferred position. He's always played out on the wing, but we've got a lot of great players coming through there now and a lot of young players as well.

"We'll see, but it's as important as it was last season. He started off great last season and then fell off a cliff.

"When he comes on or when he starts, he just needs to make an impact and do something and he needs to put the ball in the net, because missing sitters is not going to do him any favours."

4 Foden won six Premier League titles with City under Guardiola Credit: Getty

Foden scored ten goals for City in all competitions last term, his lowest return since the 2019/20 campaign.

But, positively, the 26-year-old started all three games of the Maresca era so far and provided two assists against Palace.

He'll hope to open his goalscoring account for 2026/27 when City entertain Coventry in the Premier League on Saturday.

Sports.title: Steve Bruce reveals ‘lack of respect’ led to managerial exit and left him with regrets
Sports.content:
Steve Bruce reveals ‘lack of respect’ led to managerial exit and left him with regrets

Steve Bruce says he resigned as Hull City manager following a 'lack of respect' from ex-chairman Ehab Allam and regrets not sorting the problems out.

Bruce resigned as the Tigers' boss three weeks prior to the 2016/17 season starting, which ended with the club getting relegated. They did not get back into the Premier League until nine years later.



3 Bruce (right) could only field 13 senior players heading into the 2016/17 campaign Credit: Getty

The 65-year-old has always maintained he left with a heavy heart, but had no choice to leave after his relationship with the owner's son, Ehab Allam, became irretrievable.

Due to Assem Allam falling ill, his son Ehab became keen to sell up and refused the manager a chance to strengthen an injury-ravaged squad with only 13 fit senior players.

His departure was sudden, and after he failed to appear at the training ground, the coaching staff had to inform the players that he had quit the evening prior.



Recalling his fairy tale managerial start at Hull, Bruce said on White and Jordan: "I had a wonderful relationship with his [Ehab Allam] father. Unfortunately, his father took ill. He was a fantastic man, in and around Hull.

"I mean, his first words he said to me was he bought Hull for the community because he didn't want it to go bust, but he doesn't know anything about football.



"He needed somebody experienced. Here you go, Steve, come and run it. And we had a great time. We had four years, two promotions, FA Cup final, 2-0 up in a Cup final, and got into Europe.

"We had a really, really wonderful time. And this was with the Alam family. It's just fair to say, ten years later, I'm disappointed that I couldn't make the relationship work.



"And I do believe that any successful football club, really, you have to have a link between the top and the head coach or the manager.

"There has to be a little bit of respect down the road. And unfortunately, there wasn't any between both of us. And we were both to blame. And I took the decision at the time to say, ‘I can't work like this.’

Hull City remains the club where the former defender enjoyed his longest managerial tenure, sitting in the MKM Stadium dugout for four full years.

3 After taking control of the club in 2010, Allam experienced extreme highs and lows as owner of Hull City



On his departure, Bruce said: "It was after a conversation with Ehab. I said ‘I think it's best I go’, yeah. And he said ‘yes’. He couldn't wait for me to get out the door.

"He couldn't wait. And fair enough, I just regret that I couldn't make it work because it was happy times, we had just gotten the Premier League and we should have been looking to rebuild the team. And we had a nucleus of a very, very decent team.

"I had bit the bullet for the last four or five months. And I suppose, the interference of the scouting network and all the rest of it, after running it, it all of a sudden disappeared.

"And we were successful in the transfer market. We found people like Jarrod Bowen and Andy Robertson and Harry Maguire. But I became not happy with the recruitment part of the club and wanted to go down a different route.



"But it was not healthy for the club in particular. So I made the decision to walk away from it."

Hull's revival under Sergej Jakirovic

After narrowly avoiding relegation to League One in 2025, Hull City staged a remarkable turnaround to crash the Championship play-offs last season.

3 Hull sit third in the Premier League with two wins Credit: Getty

They went on to defeat Middlesbrough in the play-off final at Wembley, securing their return to the top flight for the first time in nine years.



So far, the underdogs have made a perfect start in the Premier League under head coach Sergej Jakirovic, even beating the Red Devils 2-0 on the season's opening day.

Bruce complimented the current atmosphere surrounding the club, as he said: "I have to say the new manager walking through the door, everybody was predicting that last year they would be relegated.

"Not to get to the top end and get them into the play-offs and ultimately get them promoted.

"I was particularly impressed defensively the way they were because they had to from last season. They conceded something like 60-odd goals.



"They conceded and still managed to get up. And yet this year they look rock solid defensively."

Sports.title: Noel Gallagher teases Oasis 2027 tour in biggest hint yet
Sports.content:
Noel Gallagher has dangled the possibility of another Oasis tour next year.

The rock legend and die-hard Manchester City fan will set the pulses racing of Oasis fans with some cryptic comments about what's next for the reunited band after their long-awaited tour last year.

3 Noel initially hinted Liam wasn't sold on doing a tour next summer but then made another telling remark Credit: Getty

The Britpop icons memorably returned to the stage, having not performed together since 2009 amid the long-running feud between Noel and brother Liam.

But fans were treated to a long run of shows around the UK and Ireland and around the world from the band who spawned iconic hits including 'Wonderwall' and 'Don't Look Back in Anger'.

And fans might want to get saving for further performances, if Noel's comments are anything to go by.

Noel Gallagher teases Oasis return

Asked by Andy Goldstein if the rumours were true that Oasis would be gigging again next summer, Gallagher initially appeared to downplay the possibility on Drive: "It's Liam, isn't it? He's not into it. He's not into Oasis anymore."

However, when told his brother had come off social media (Liam posted on X recently: 'I'm out of here'), Gallagher responded: "Well, then there must be something happening.

"Let's put it this way: there's no football tournament on next year, so we've got to do something in the summer, right?"

There has been speculation of Oasis making a return to Knebworth next summer.

The group famously played the storied outdoor venue in Hertfordshire over two dates in August 1996.

Some 250,000 people flocked to see them that weekend, with around 2.5m applying for tickets.

City's perfect start

Gallagher was also speaking about his beloved Manchester City, who made it two Premier League wins from two under new boss Enzo Maresca.

3 Gallagher is regularly spotted in the stands at City games Credit: Getty

Erling Haaland and Ryan Cherki both bagged braces as City thrashed Crystal Palace 4-1 at Selhurst Park last Friday.

They return to action on Saturday with a home clash against newly promoted Coventry.

Maresca then leads his side in Europe for the first time with their Champions League opener away to Porto next Tuesday, live on talkSPORT.

City had an eventful end to the transfer window, signing Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea and Iliman Ndiaye from Everton on deadline day.

In joining for £125m, Fernandez becomes the joint most expensive player in British football history alongside Alexander Isak.

Meanwhile, Jack Grealish has left the Etihad Stadium again, heading back to Everton for a second loan spell.

3 Fernandez was one of two big deadline day signings for City Credit: Getty

Fighting talk from Gallagher as City target Arsenal revenge

Gallagher thinks the Argentina World Cup winner could make all the difference to City's Premier League title chances.

On the subject whether it would be another two-horse race between City and Arsenal, who beat them to glory last term, he said confidently: "Before we got Fernandez, [it was a case of] whoever finishes above us is going to win the league.

"We've got Haaland, [Gianluigi] Donnarumma, Cherki, [Elliot] Anderson, [Nico] O'Reilly... We've got a great team don't you worry about that."

He also insisted Arsenal still haven't entirely 'proven' themselves, addressing the Gunners in continuing: "Let's put it this say: you won the league last season; you never beat us at all.

"We played you three times [in all competitions]; you never beat us. We beat you in the [FA] Cup final, we beat you at our place and we drew at yours [in the league].

"So, for all the talk of Arsenal being this amazing squad and the best team in Europe, you've still got to prove it against us – and we just got better last night [by signing Fernandez]."

Sports.title: Richarlison to get move away from Tottenham and could triple his wages
Sports.content:
Richarlison to get move away from Tottenham and could triple his wages

Richarlison has agreed terms on a lucrative deal to join Trabzonspor ahead of the Turkish transfer window closing, talkSPORT understands.

The Turkish club want to sign the Brazilian and unite him with former Liverpool star Mohamed Salah.



3 Richarlison has asked to leave Tottenham Hotspur Credit: Getty

They have had two offers turned down so far by Tottenham Hotspur.

The first bid was £15million and the second was £20m. However, they are expected to come in with another offer as they look to get the deal tied up.

Fabrizio Romano is reporting that Richarlison will triple his salary if he makes the move.

Roberto De Zerbi told reporters after the 2-0 defeat to Newcastle United at the weekend that the forward had asked to leave the club.



He was one of three, with Kevin Danso and Pape Matar Sarr the other two. Danso joined Sunderland and Sarr is with Juventus, both on loan.

However, Richarlison stayed put. He had looked to be returning to Everton in a deal that was meant to see Iliman Ndiaye go the other way.



They were billed as separate deals, but a series of events unfolded that ensured neither transfer happened.

What happened with Richarlison?

Spurs agreed a fee with Everton to take Ndiaye from them. In return, Richarlison was set to head back to Merseyside, but he failed to agree terms with Everton.



In the time Tottenham were waiting, Manchester City saw a deal for Cody Gakpo collapse. Gakpo chose a switch to the Etihad Stadium over Spurs, but the two clubs couldn't agree a deal.

The reason they couldn't agree a deal is because Liverpool didn't have time to find a replacement. That saw City switch attention to Ndiaye, and he picked Man City over Tottenham.

3 Ndiaye has left Everton for Man City in a £65million deal

And at the same time, Richarlison took to Instagram and emotionally revealed that he felt disrespected by Tottenham.



He made it clear he would only move on his terms as well.

It was in Portuguese, but translated as follows: "After everything I've been through in recent years, I decided that they would never again decide my future for me.

"I've been through a lot of bad things these days and almost all of them happened because of decisions made by other people.

"Pressure, threats, retaliations, none of this scares me. I've been through worse things… believe me!

"I have always made it clear, at every opportunity, that an exit of mine to another place would also have to be good for the club.



3 Richarlison might get the move he carves Credit: Getty

"If it wasn't, I would never accept… as I didn't accept when everything here was falling apart and they needed me.

"I stayed and gave my life. So, I hope you treat my situation with the same respect that I always had for Spurs and for all the people who worked with me during this period. Just don't want to decide for me.

"If they enter into an agreement between Spurs and Everton, I go back to my favourite team.



"My intention was to return to the place where I was very happy. But the negotiations were the way people wanted and it won't be like this anymore.

"Despite this riot, I have a contract with Spurs and I will be at the club's disposal."

Turkish transfer window

The Turkish transfer window is still open, and it is when the main European one closes that these sides usually spring into life.

Teams in Turkey have until Friday, September 4 to sign players.

So, they still have plenty of time to get Richarlison wrapped up as long as they agree a fee with Spurs.

Sports.title: Enzo Fernandez lands Premier League icon’s shirt number in Man City move
Sports.content:
Enzo Fernandez will wear the No.17 shirt at Manchester City - previously worn by Premier League icon Kevin De Bruyne.

The midfielder finally joined the Citizens from Chelsea for £125million on transfer deadline day in record-equalling deal.

3 Fernandez left Chelsea for Man City in a record-equalling Premier League deal on transfer deadline day Credit: PA

It spelled the end of a long-running transfer saga involving Fernandez, who flirted with an exit from Stamford Bridge all summer.

Having first had his heart set on a move to Real Madrid, the Argentina star sealed a Premier League switch at the 11th hour after Man City emerged as suitors in recent weeks.

Chelsea previously set a deadline of 5pm on Friday, August 14 for interested clubs to meet their £120m asking price, only for the cut-off point to pass without City making an offer.

Despite the Blues' stance, the deal accelerated in the final hours of the transfer window and was announced just after the 11pm deadline.

Fernandez's departure came in a chaotic end to Deadline Day, which saw Chelsea miss out on signing Monaco's Lamine Camara as a replacement, with the Ligue 1 side turning their back on the £47m deal previously agreed between the two clubs.

Fernandez inherits De Bruyne's shirt

Having sealed a move to the Etihad, Fernandez is now looking to inspire City to glory, and has been handed an iconic shirt number.

Less than 24 hours after his arrival, the Citizens confirmed the 25-year-old will wear the No.17 jersey.

He inherits the number from club legend De Bruyne, who vacated it last summer after a trophy-laden ten years at the club.

During that time, De Bruyne scored 108 goals and provided 177 assists in 422 appearances, as well as winning 17 trophies.

Before the Belgian great, winger Martin Petrov took ownership for three years until 2010, while Jerome Boateng, Michael Johnson and Jack Rodwell have all previously donned the shirt too.

3 De Bruyne established himself as one of the Premier League's all-time greats whilst wearing the No.17 shirt for Man City Credit: Getty

But with De Bruyne becoming synonymous with the jersey during his time at City, Fernandez has some way to go to live up to his legacy in Manchester.

The Argentine revealed the number carries personal significance when explaining his picking of the No.17 shirt.

He told Man City's official website: “It’s a number I like.

“It embodies me. It was my first number in the national team, so I’m very happy to choose this number.”

While Fernandez cannot yet touch any of De Bruyne's achievements in a City shirt, he heads to the Etihad as a proven winner.

The ex-Benfica star boasts 2022 World Cup glory with Argentina on his CV, while lifted the Conference League and Club World Cup trophies at Chelsea - winning both under new City boss Enzo Maresca.

3 Fernandez has now reunited with his former boss at Chelsea, Enzo Maresca Credit: Getty

And Fernandez shared his delight at joining the Citizens and sealing a reunion with Maresca.

He said upon arrival: “Every player wants to be part of a club like this because everyone knows how well-run City are.

“I could not be happier to be here, and I am ready for the challenge of helping City continue winning trophies. This is a club built for success.

“If you look across the squad, City have quality in every area. I want to learn from my new teammates and become a better player.

“I pride myself on continually improving my game. Anyone who’s worked with me will know how hard I train every single day and how much I put into matches. I give absolutely everything and I can promise Manchester City that will continue now I’m here.”

Sports.title: Clippers stripped of FIVE first-round picks and slapped with $30m fine as NBA rules on Kawhi Leonard secret payment scandal
Sports.content:
The NBA is stripping the Los Angeles Clippers of five first-round picks, issuing a $30 million fine to billionaire owner Steve Ballmer and suspending the former Microsoft CEO for one year following an investigation into improper payments to All-Star Kawhi Leonard, the league announced Wednesday.

The NBA has been investigating allegations that the Clippers circumvented the salary cap by funneling money to Leonard through an endorsement deal with companies including Aspiration, a green banking firm that has since gone bankrupt as its co-founder Joseph Sandberg admitted to defrauding investors out of $248 million.

'The investigation found a pattern of misconduct and multiple significant rules violations by the Clippers organization, a prior offender of the salary cap circumvention rules,' read the league statement.

Although he was not suspended, Leonard was ordered to pay $700,000 in restitution for improper benefits he and his uncle/representative Dennis Robertson received from the Clippers and other organizations. However, the 35-year-old Leonard will not have any contracts voided by the league as a result of the NBA investigation.

Robertson, meanwhile, has been banned from any business dealings with the NBA.

Additionally, Clippers president of basketball operations Lawrence Frank has been suspened without pay for six months while president of business operations Gillian Zucker got a one-year ban.

The NBA is stripping the Los Angeles Clippers of five first-round picks, issuing a $30 million fine to billionaire owner Steve Ballmer

Kawhi Leonard came out of the year-long investigation with his earnings nearly intact

All punishments are binding, according to the league and players' union.

Despite this, the Clippers are not done fighting this ruling, the team explained in a statement.

'We vehemently reject the NBA's findings, which are the result of a heavily biased investigation seeking to justify a predetermined narrative rather than facts and evidence,' read the team statement.

'What the league told us privately differs from what it announced today publicly, and they have not held themselves close to the standard Commissioner Silver set at the start of this investigation to ensure it's fairness and accuracy.

'For the past year, we cooperated fully and in good faith and we will now fight just as hard to demonstrate our innocence. We intend to vigorously challenge these findings and penalties through every avenue available to us and look forward to an ethical and impartial arbitration process.'

According to the a summary report prepared by law firm Wachtell Lipton, the Clippers violated NBA rules by 'initiating off-court income opportunities between Mr. Leonard and four companies doing business with the team.'

Those companies include Aspiration Partners, Boingo Wireless, Daktronics, and Lockton Insurance.

Additionally, the Clippers are accused of facilitating endorsement deals, inducing companies to enter into these agreements by offering other business with the team, and paying personal expenses on behalf of Leonard and his representatives.

Lastly, the team failed to report improper solicitations made on Leonard's behalf by Robertson.

The Clippers should have been aware of the rules, according to the Wachtell Lipton report, because they had previously been found in violation of these same mandates.

'In 2015, in circumstances similar to the matter at hand, the Clippers engaged in efforts to facilitate an endorsement agreement between DeAndre Jordan—a player the Clippers were then seeking to sign in free agency—and an incoming team sponsor,' read the report. 'The League investigated this matter, determined that the rules had been broken, and fined the Clippers $250,000.'

NBA commissioner Adam Silver did follow some precedent with his punishment for LA

Meanwhile, Leonard and Robertson were found to have pressured 'the Clippers to assist [Leonard] in obtaining off-court income opportunities, successfully obtaining those opportunities, and failing to reimburse payments by the Clippers for personal expenses,' according to the statement.

The Clippers recently agreed to trade Leonard back to Toronto, where he won an NBA title in 2019 before signing with LA. The deal was placed on hold as the league investigation continued over the summer, but as Leonard revealed in his statement, it appears he is now headed back to the shores of Lake Ontario.

'Integrity and respect for this game are fundamental to who I am,' Leonard said in a statement issued by his agent. 'I accept full responsibility for lapses in judgment by people within my inner circle and regret the distraction this situation has caused the fans and my family.

'I entered into my contract with the Clippers as well as the agreements in question in good faith, fully committed to fulfilling my obligations and with no knowledge of any intent on anyone's part to circumvent the salary cap.

'For 15 years, my priority has been giving everything to my family, the game, and those I share the court with. As I return to Toronto, I am focused on what I can control, closing this chapter, and moving forward with a clean slate.'

There is precedent for at least a portion of the NBA's punishment for the Clippers.

NBA commissioner Adam Silver's predecessor, the late David Stern, similarly stripped the Minnesota Timberwolves of five first-round picks after discovering the team had circumvented the salary cap to improperly pay star forward Joe Smith in 2000.

However, the Wolves were fined only $3.5 million at the time, and because the team cooperated with the league, some of the picks were ultimately returned to Minnesota.

Silver explained his ruling in the league statement.

'The NBA's collectively bargained system for determining player compensation is a fundamental component of the basketball competition that the league oversees for the benefit of the teams and players and ultimately the fans,' Silver said in a statement. 'I am deeply disappointed by the flagrant violations of our rules and by the Clippers' institutional and leadership failures that led to this misconduct. The severity of the penalties reflects the seriousness of the violations.'

NBA commissioner Adam Silver's predecessor, the late David Stern (pictured), similarly stripped the Timberwolves of five first-round picks for an improper deal with Joe Smith

The Timberwolves allegedly circumvented the cap to pay Joe Smith additional salary in 2000

Leonard's arrival in his native Southern California was supposed to usher in a new era for the traditional NBA cellar-dwelling Clippers.

But in trying to lure Leonard, the Clippers traded for veteran All-Star Paul George from Oklahoma City in exchange for budding guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, who would go on to win an NBA championship and league MVP honors with the Thunder.

In total, the Clippers officially paid Leonard $291 million over seven seasons, not to mention the millions funneled through other businesses and the $30 million fine the team has incurred for those violations.

Regrettably, the Clippers don't have much to show for the Leonard era. After reaching the Western Conference Semis and Finals in 2020 and 2021, respectively, the team has failed to win a playoff series since.

Leonard (seen here with Ballmer in 2019) initially signed a three-year deal with LA for $103m

The allegations against the Clippers first surfaced on Pablo Torre's podcast nearly one year ago.

Since then, NBA has been investigating the Clippers and Ballmer for allegedly facilitating an under-the-table side deal for Leonard that allowed the team to add other stars, such as Paul George. The team repeatedly denied the accusations, while Ballmer stated he had no knowledge of Leonard's alleged $28 million 'no-show' endorsement deal with the doomed financial services firm, Aspiration.

Torre made the claim against the Clippers by citing a 2025 bankruptcy filing that names the team and a company owned by Leonard under the list of creditors for Aspiration QFZ, LLC, a subsidiary of fintech and sustainability brand Aspiration Partners Inc.

Torre claimed to have contracts showing Aspiration QFZ, LLC entered into a $28 million 'no-show' agreement with Leonard's company, KL2 Aspire LLC, and later claimed - following a report from the Boston Sports Journal - that Leonard also received a separate $20million 'side deal' from Aspiration.

Ballmer invested $50 million in Aspiration through an LLC in 2021 as the team was also embarking on a $300 million deal with the green bank. Then, in April of 2022, Aspiration signed Leonard to a $28 million endorsement deal, which has been characterized as a 'no-show' job. Leonard did not publicly endorse Aspiration at any point.

Leonard joined the Clippers in 2019 and went on to sign two extensions with LA

Daily Mail obtained a federal bankruptcy filing showing unsecured claims of $30 million and $7 million for the LA Clippers and Leonard's company, KL2 Aspire LLC, respectively

The bankruptcy filing from federal court in Delaware, obtained by the Daily Mail, also shows unsecured claims of $30 million and $7 million for the Clippers and Leonard's company, KL2 Aspire LLC, respectively.

And while Ballmer said last year he was 'embarrassed' that he didn't pick up on any financial trouble from Aspiration, he defended his and the Clippers actions and said they 'weren't involved' in the company's deal with Leonard.

The team, as it pointed out in a statement, 'ended its relationship with Aspiration years ago, during the 2022-23 season, when Aspiration defaulted on its obligation.'

Furthermore, as reported by Torre, Aspiration QFZ's alleged payments to KL2 Aspire were sent to Robertson, Leonard's uncle and advisor, who was previously investigated by the NBA in 2019 for allegedly requesting impermissible benefits for his nephew and himself.

That 2019 investigation did not find any impermissible benefits going from the Clippers to Leonard or anyone working on his behalf.

A year later, a self-described acquaintance of Leonard and Robertson named Johnny Wilkes sued the Clippers, claiming he was still owed $2.5 million from the team for helping them to sign the former Spurs and Raptors star.

Wilkes, a self-described acquaintance of Robertson, claimed in the lawsuit that Ballmer would 'fund a $100,000,000.00 marketing campaign for Kawhi Leonard' and the uncle would get his own Southern California home if the All-Star forward agreed to sign with the Clippers.

That lawsuit was ultimately dismissed and neither the Clippers nor Robertson admitted to any wrongdoing.

Sports.title: NFL rocked by tragedy as former star dies by suicide at 40... shortly after troubling final social media post
Sports.content:
NFL rocked by tragedy as former star dies by suicide at 40... shortly after troubling final social media post

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Former NFL star Alphonso Smith Jr. has reportedly died by suicide at the age of 40.

The former Detroit Lions cornerback passed away at a housing community in Florida on Wednesday, according to TMZ.

A chilling final Facebook post that appeared on Smith Jr.'s account earlier in the day referenced 'demons' and concluded by saying: 'THIS IS IT!'

‘I tried everything in my power to fight the demons behind the ones that someone put into ME!’ he wrote.

‘To my family, BABY, my MOM, my siblings, things happened to your boy, your brother while I was little that an older lady did onto me,’ he wrote. ‘As a result guys, I did the same onto others!’

Smith did not go into further detail about what happened to him or what he did to others, but did describe himself as someone who ‘needed help & did not get it.’

Former NFL star Alphonso Smith Jr. has reportedly died by suicide at the age of 40

A chilling Facebook post appeared on Smith Jr.'s account on Wednesday referencing 'demons'

Smith Jr. played college football at Wake Forest before being drafted by the Denver Broncos

He went on to blast himself as a ‘coward’ while apologizing to his children, parents, and friends.

'I am the WORST & I pray my soul rest in heaven for my heart is pure, but my BRAIN & experience is MESSED UP,' he added.

A Florida native, Smith Jr. played college football at Wake Forest from 2004 to 2008 before being selected by the Denver Broncos with the 37th overall pick in the 2009 NFL Draft.

During his college career at Wake Forest, Smith amassed 188 total tackles over four seasons to go with 21 total interceptions.

The Broncos traded him to the Lions in 2010 and he went on to play three seasons in Detroit before his NFL career ended after the 2012 season.

In total, Smith Jr. played in 42 NFL games and recorded 88 tackles and eight interceptions.

His death comes just over a month after Super Bowl champion Jordan Devey also died by suicide at the age of 38.

Devey's wife, Lindsey, shared the news in an emotional Instagram tribute posted on what would have been the couple's 15th wedding anniversary.

Former NFL star and Super Bowl champion Jordan Devey has died by suicide at 38 in July

'We have filled the walls of our homes and hearts with countless memories, joys, struggles, and triumphs,' Lindsey wrote alongside photos of the couple.

'We brought 4 beautiful children into this world that have your eyes, freckles, and compassion. You were our hero and our hearts ache in your absence. We love you. We miss you. And as you said in your last words to me, "we'll talk soon."'

A GoFundMe campaign launched on behalf of the family confirmed Devey died by suicide, leaving behind his wife and four young children.

'Tragically, Jordan took his own life, leaving his family to navigate an incredibly difficult and heartbreaking time,' the page reads.

'As they face overwhelming emotional and financial challenges, including mounting medical expenses, the community is coming together to support Lindsey and their children.'

Devey, who went undrafted out of Memphis in 2013, spent eight seasons in the NFL, playing for the Baltimore Ravens, New England Patriots, San Francisco 49ers, Kansas City Chiefs, Oakland Raiders and Buffalo Bills before retiring in 2021.

Over the course of his professional career, he appeared in 44 regular-season games and made 21 starts across stints with the Patriots, 49ers, Chiefs and Raiders.

If you or someone you know needs help, please call or text the confidential 24/7 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline in the US on 988. There is also an online chat available at 988lifeline.org.

Sports.title: Inside Crystal Palace's transfer window: How Eagles held on to star duo, why they were happy to let Daniel Munoz go, how Brennan Johnson failure hurt business and what Dario Osorio and Quinten Timber bring to the table
Sports.content:
What was all the panic about? Crystal Palace may have left significant transfer business until after the window had officially closed but they can be content with their summer’s work.

Losing Daniel Munoz and Maxence Lacroix appeared a tricky inheritance for Pierre Sage, who already had the daunting task of succeeding Oliver Glasner, yet Palace – with recruitment led by Matt Hobbs, Iain Moody and chairman Steve Parish – eventually bolstered their squad after a late rush to Tuesday’s 11pm deadline.

Most importantly, Palace have kept Jean-Philippe Mateta and Ismaila Sarr, much to the latter’s dismay. The talismanic pair – who scored 37 goals between them last term – both wanted to leave.

Sarr sulked while his agent kicked up a fuss. That was unsurprising, given one source told Daily Mail Sport over breakfast in June that his agent was keen to move him on. Palace remained resolute, though, refusing to sell the attacker with three years remaining on his contract.

Once the window closed, Sarr’s agent had his say, criticising the club for not executing the ‘will of the player’ – a strange comment given Sarr signed a five-year contract without a release clause just two years ago. The club had no obligation to sell him, particularly as he did not submit a transfer request.

But the question remains: how will he return? If Sarr wants to leave in January or next summer, the best way to make that happen is to apply himself and demonstrate why he deserves an upward move rather than continuing to sulk. After all, Palace have Europa League football and fancy their chances of a deep run in the competition.

Crystal Palace have managed to hang onto Ismaila Sarr (right) and Jean-Philippe Mateta

Pierre Sage has the daunting task of succeeding Oliver Glasner as Palace boss

There are no concerns about Mateta’s response. He will do what he did when his move to AC Milan collapsed in January: knuckle down and let the football do the talking once he has recovered from injury.

Holding on to attackers of their class is a triumph and Palace consolidated by adding depth, too. Dario Osorio, signed from Danish club Midtjylland, has plenty of upside as a winger who drifts inside, making him well suited to Sage’s 3-4-2-1 formation. The 22-year-old offers end product, talented ball delivery and averaged a goal or assist every 180 minutes last term.

Dwight McNeil is a curious addition, given he arrived in a straight swap for Brennan Johnson, whom Palace paid £30million for in January. Decision-makers accepted that they had got the Johnson transfer wrong, something a club with Palace's financial constraints cannot afford to do.

The swap did at least remove substantial money from the wage bill. But the Johnson overspend in January limited what Palace could do this summer, with the club finishing the window with a positive net spend as they sought to recoup some of the capital lost on their former record signing.

Evann Guessand has returned on loan following his stint at the club during the second half of last season. Before injury, he was a menace starting from the left and provided adequate back-up to Yeremy Pino.

Zavier Gozo was also signed in attack from Real Salt Lake, with the teenager viewed as one for the future. He came on against Manchester City last week and showed some exuberance. That is the type of business Palace should be doing: signing replacements for players years before their departure, providing them with the chance to learn from established players and adapt to the league before they are asked to fill in for them full time.

Last season, Palace ended the summer window with just four No 10s and wingers, with midfielders Daichi Kamada and Justin Devenny often required to fill in. This term, they have eight players to call upon for those spots. There is competition, alternatives and potential.

Replacing Lacroix with Axel Disasi is, admittedly, a downgrade. Lacroix started for France at the World Cup and is now Chelsea’s first-choice centre back. Disasi, meanwhile, is a Chelsea cast-off and nowhere near the France squad.

Decision-makers at Palace accept they had got the Brennan Johnson transfer wrong and he has been moved on to Everton

Axel Disasi has been brought in to beef up the Palace defence and adds experience

Lacroix held the Palace backline together with his recovery pace and immense physicality, qualities Palace will inevitably miss this season. Most importantly, though, he made Jaydee Canvot and Chris Richards better, guiding them through games.

Disasi may not have the same pace but he is experienced and a solid defender, though he can have his blips in possession. His arrival on loan at West Ham in January markedly improved their defence, helping them keep six clean sheets in 14 games.

Centre back remains the most concerning area. Canvot and Honest Ahanor, a deadline-day arrival from Atalanta, are promising but lack know-how. Ahanor is impressively imposing for his age, although it is a shame Palace are developing a player who will join Chelsea next summer – even if they have procured a skilled defender.

Richards is proven at right centre back but if Disasi becomes unavailable, he would have to move into the middle, where he has looked suspect. Oscar Mingueza, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Jefferson Lerma, who can all play in multiple positions, are viewed as understudies. Not adding another central centre back could be a costly omission as the backline appears fragile without Disasi.

Number-wise, though, it is an improvement. At one point last season, Palace had only four centre backs for three positions. They may lack a sprinkling of quality at the back but they have brought in enough depth to compete in Europe and domestically.

Losing Munoz to Glasner’s Nottingham Forest was emotionally tough for Palace, given the rivalry between the clubs and his role in winning three trophies in two years. But, from a business perspective, it was the right move.

Munoz, now 30, has reached his peak transfer value, leaving for £22m, and the data suggests he will start to decline. In two years, Palace have made a £16m profit and replaced him with Anan Khalaili, whom they believe is a younger version with a higher ceiling. On his debut against Manchester City, the similarities were striking, with the Israeli wing-back relentless from start to finish. Those two transfers were net zero, too.

Quinten Timber, an athletic ball-winner, adds a desperately required profile to Palace’s midfield options, replacing bit-part player Devenny, who moved to Stoke City on a permanent deal.

Losing Daniel Munoz to Nottingham Forest was emotionally tough for Palace. But, from a business perspective, it was the right move

Quinten Timber, an athletic ball-winner, adds a desperately required profile to Palace’s midfield

Adam Wharton and Kamada is a strong pairing but against superior opposition, the two-man midfield has lacked athleticism and bite at times. Timber gives Sage a plan B.

Some sources have suggested Timber’s physical profile should suit the Premier League, given his brother Jurrien’s success at Arsenal. His arrival also helps solve the problem of losing Kamada to the Asia Cup in the new year.

Ben Chilwell – if he can stay fit – is an upgrade on Borna Sosa, who failed to make an impact last season. Chilwell, signed for free from Strasbourg, was at the club on loan from Chelsea when Palace won the FA Cup. He is a leader, homegrown and offensively talented.

His injury record is alarming but he did manage 34 games at Strasbourg last season. Sosa, who has joined Cologne on loan, played a third of the minutes Chilwell did last season because he was not at the level required.

What Palace have successfully done this window is build a complete squad, with multiple options in every position. That was the bugbear last season.

They have a 28-man group, six of whom will need to be cut from the European squad, giving Sage the ability to rotate with at least two players for every position.

Of course, the window could have been improved if moves for Joel Ordonez and Malick Fofana had gone through. But Ordonez’s medical showed his broken metatarsal injury was more serious than initially expected, meaning he would not have been an option until later in the season.

It could be a deal Palace revisit in January. The highly-rated centre back should be available by then and has long been admired by the club.

Ben Chilwell (left) signed for free from Strasbourg and was at Palace on loan from Chelsea when they won the FA Cup

Fofana’s move from Lyon was ultimately hijacked by Sunderland after Palace thought they had beaten the North East club to his signature. Palace sources were frustrated on Tuesday afternoon, as Sunderland offered the player’s family money they could not match. Sage desperately wanted to sign him after working together at Lyon.

There has been significant player turnover at Palace and it will take time for the squad to gel – 11 players have arrived with six first-teamers making way.

On the whole, they are in a stronger position than last year, with a proficient starting XI and solid back-up in every position. That gives them plenty of reason to be optimistic. The proof will be on the pitch but the signs are promising.

Sports.title: Emotional Eddie Hearn reveals why he was in 'floods of tears' in build-up to Katie Taylor's retirement fight - and predicts event could be the biggest of ALL time
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn has admitted he was reduced to 'floods of tears' watching the promo video for Katie Taylor's retirement fight, before predicting her final ring walk at Croke Park could become 'one of the greatest moments sport has ever seen'.

Taylor will call time on her glittering career on Saturday night when she faces unbeaten Frenchwoman Flora Pili in front of an expected 80,000 fans in Dublin.

The 40-year-old will bid to become a three-time undisputed world champion in the 27th and final fight of her professional career, with the vacant WBC title also on the line alongside her WBO, WBA and IBF belts.

And Hearn, who has promoted Taylor throughout her professional career, is already struggling to contain his emotions ahead of the occasion.

'I've got my daughter with me, and we came through the airport, and it's like every other person knows about Saturday,' he said. 'Everyone knows about Saturday. It sounds like everyone's going. So I just can't wait. I just can't wait to feel it, and it'll be unbelievably emotional.

'I mean, that promo video… I'm not afraid to say it. When I say I cried, I am not exaggerating. This is a bit embarrassing but I bawled my eyes out. Not like, 'Oh, a tear came out', literally floods of tears.

Eddie Hearn (pictured above) has admitted he was reduced to 'floods of tears' watching the promo video for Katie Taylor's retirement fight

Taylor will call time on her glittering career on Saturday night when she faces unbeaten Frenchwoman Flora Pili (pictured on the right) in front of an expected 80,000 fans in Dublin

The 40-year-old (pictured above) will bid to become a three-time undisputed world champion in the 27th and final fight of her professional career

'I can't stop thinking about the ring walk. I truly believe it will be one of the greatest moments sport has ever seen.

'Yes, it's going to be one of the biggest events Irish sport has ever seen, one of the biggest female boxing events ever seen, but honestly I think it could be the biggest sporting event of all time. It's going to be one of those events where everyone's going to go, 'Wow. I can't believe it's happening.'

For Hearn, the scale of the occasion is all the more remarkable given that he once doubted whether Taylor would ever get the chance to fight at Croke Park.

The Matchroom promoter admitted he is disappointed with himself for allowing those doubts to creep in, particularly after previous attempts to Taylor's dream location had failed to materialise.

'I'm disappointed in myself, actually, that I allowed that to happen, because maybe we could have done it earlier,' Hearn said. 'But I probably didn't have the confidence that I had going into it this time, with Peter, with the Serrano three-fight deal and all that.

'If Croke Park had originally gone, 'Yes, this is going to be massive,' I would have gone, 'Wow you're right' and we would have done it. But I was like, 'I don't know' and I was thinking blimey, if they're not sure, do we really want to be gambling with these costs?

'But, they listened, they helped out as well. They were fantastic in the end.

'Saying all of that though, I never thought we'd do 40,000 on a pre-sale. It's honestly blown my mind how passionate the fans are for Katie and how much they support her and show up for her.'

For Hearn, the scale of the occasion is all the more remarkable given that he once doubted whether Taylor would ever get the chance to fight at Croke Park

Taylor pictured inspiring the next generation during her open working in Dublin on Wednesday

The demand has left Hearn wondering just how many more fans could have packed into Ireland's national stadium.

'We're getting hundreds of messages every day from people saying, 'Please, I want to bring my daughter. It's heartbreaking in a way because we'd love for everyone to get a ticket and be there to watch it live but that's just the way it is.'

Hearn is delighted that DAZN will broadcast the fight, while also praising the decision to allow Irish broadcaster RTE to show the event.

'I'm so happy that DAZN are broadcasting the fight,' he said. 'But I think the RTE thing is incredible as well. I was shocked, but very grateful that DAZN allowed that to happen because I think it's very important for Ireland.'

And while her journey to the Olympics and gold medal at London 2012 remains the defining chapter of her amateur career, Hearn believes it is what Taylor has achieved as a professional that will shape her legacy for generations to come.

Taylor won Olympic gold before turning professional, but went on to conquer the sport at the highest level, headlining at Madison Square Garden, fighting on Netflix and beating virtually every major opponent put in front of her.

Hearn believes her battle with Chantelle Cameron, including the rematch in which she avenged the first defeat of her professional career, are particularly underappreciated.

'She won that gold medal, but I think when you look back on everything that she's done, from starting out fighting on the AJ cards to headlining MSG, fighting on Netflix, you know, and she's beaten everybody,' he said.

Taylor won Olympic gold before turning professional, but went on to conquer the sport at the highest level, headlining at Madison Square Garden and fighting on Netflix

She has beaten virtually every major opponent put in front of her - including Amanda Serrano

'By the way, when you look back, you see Chantelle Cameron beat Mikaela Mayer last Saturday. She's a strong, big, big, big girl. And Katie's rematch victory over Chantelle Cameron, I think, is so underrated, especially at the stage in her career that Katie was at.

'There are so many things. I think the Olympics will always be the Olympics, but there are a lot of people that don't remember the Olympics or weren't around in 2012. The younger generation now that are following Katie, I don't think they're necessarily reminiscing about the Olympics.

'These are girls that are eight, 10, 12, 16. They weren't even born when she won the Olympics. So I think what she's done in the pro ranks will be remembered forever. Honestly, it's just everything that she's done across the board. We are so lucky to have had a fighter like her.'

Hearn also believes Taylor has fundamentally transformed women's boxing.

'She changed women's boxing forever,' he said. 'Whether I did it or not, she was going to convince probably someone to do it, right?

'Now, whether they would have done it the same way as us, I doubt it. But this wasn't me going, 'I'm going to try and change women's boxing.' This was me going, 'I believe in you, and I want to come along for the journey.'

'So what led from there is the doors opening and watching…'

Hearn remembers just how different the landscape was when Taylor turned professional.

Serrano and Taylor fighting in their IBF, WBA, WBC, WBO, and Ring super lightweight title bout during Netflix's Katie Taylor vs Amanda Serrano 3 at Madison Square Garden on July 11, 2025

'When she turned pro, there were some weight classes in women's boxing that had four fighters at a professional level,' he said. 'You could fight for the world title in your second or third fight. And now it's really hard to win a world title. There are some brilliant fighters.'

Perhaps most tellingly, Hearn says Taylor has achieved something that goes beyond titles, records and money: she has earned the respect of virtually every fighter in the sport.

'There isn't one female fighter you could find that wouldn't go, 'She's incredible,' he said. 'She's just so loved. And there's no airs or graces. She's not there for the fame. She's not there for the money. It's just pure - purely a faith, the love of the sport, and trying to set an example.'

Yet amid all the emotion and celebration, Hearn knows Taylor cannot afford to lose sight of the woman standing opposite her on Saturday night.

Pili is unbeaten at 12-0 and, while she does not possess Taylor's experience or pedigree, she is younger, strong and willing to trade.

With Taylor fighting for her third undisputed crown and Pili seeking to pull off the biggest upset of her career, Hearn insists the retirement celebrations must wait.

'You know, today really the switch has got to focus on the fight because this girl's decent,' he said. 'She's big. She's 12-0.

'I'm not saying she's got the pedigree of Katie Taylor, but Katie's 40 years old, right? She's fighting a young, strong girl who likes to trade.

Pili (pictured above) is unbeaten at 12-0 and, while she does not possess Taylor's experience or pedigree, she is younger, strong and willing to trade

While Taylor's final fight will inevitably dominate the night, Hearn insists the rest of the card has been designed to make the occasion worthy of Croke Park

'And so does Katie.'

'She's IBO world champion, European champion, decent amateur, who, by the way, can become undisputed herself on Saturday,' Hearn said. 'So I think today there needs to be a little bit of a switch from this whole, 'Oh, euphoric, this is going to be amazing.'

'I just walked into her BBC interview there, and she was saying, 'I need to prepare myself for war here.' Because she can't walk out and get caught up in the emotion. She can't get in the ring and the start of the fight just passes you by.

'She's got to go in there, and prepare for it to be a war from the opening bell.

'And it will be an all-out war because it's the only way she knows how to fight. She's not going to try and box a moon because she'll want to leave it all in the ring.'

And while Taylor's final fight will inevitably dominate the night, Hearn insists the rest of the card has been designed to make the occasion worthy of Croke Park.

There will be major music acts, a host of Irish talent and a series of intriguing fights before Taylor takes her final walk to the ring.

'I'm not going to give too much away… I want you all to see it unfold on the night,' Hearn said. 'But there's definitely people everybody's heard of in this country who are going to be performing on Saturday night, and a number of different things going on during the night.'

Sports.title: 'This could put people's lives at risk': The 'deeply worrying' dangers of Olympian boxer Anthony Fowler's Supreme Peptides selling unlicensed 'DIY Ozempic', a mystery London lab and how regulators are cracking down on 'repeat offender'
Sports.content:
'This could put people's lives at risk': The 'deeply worrying' dangers of Olympian boxer Anthony Fowler's Supreme Peptides selling unlicensed 'DIY Ozempic', a mystery London lab and how regulators are cracking down on 'repeat offender'

Unlock more of the best of our journalism with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

Former Olympic boxer turned influencer Anthony Fowler has joined the booming market in cheap 'DIY Ozempic' in a way which scientists have told us could be putting lives at risk, a Daily Mail Sport investigation has found.

Fowler, who we exposed last year for making potentially dangerous claims about his cannabis oil products, has now expanded into peptides, by spinning a new business out of his Supreme CBD firm. The company was willing to sell weight-loss products to a would-be buyer while not disclosing the contents of the product and simply instructing them to inject themselves over several weeks to lose weight and ‘see what results you get’.

After approaching Fowler, 35, who won Commonwealth Games gold in 2014 and boxed for Team GB at Rio 2016, as part of our undercover investigation into his activities, Daily Mail Sport was offered a 40mg dose of a weight loss peptide for £120 by his new Supreme Peptides business and told it had reduced Fowler’s brother’s weight by two stones. We were told the product was ‘similar’ to the licensed weight-loss drug Mounjaro but had ‘no side effects’.

Under UK law, any companies using medical claims to sell products – including those pushing obesity treatments – must have the appropriate authorisation from the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) before selling or supplying it. Daily Mail Sport has found no evidence that Supreme Peptides has any products registered with the MHRA.

The MHRA told us it did not comment on potential or ongoing investigations. It told us: 'If a product is classified as a medicine and is not appropriately authorised, we take regulatory compliance action.'

One of the products pictured on Fowler’s Supreme Peptides website – Tesamorelin, used in the US by HIV patients and people looking to shed abdominal fat – is not an MHRA-authorised medicine and selling or supplying it in the UK is illegal. Fowler is offering it for sale at a price of £89.99 for 10mg.

Former Olympic boxer turned internet influencer Anthony Fowler has joined the booming market in cheap 'DIY Ozempic' in a way which scientists have told us could put lives at risk

Fowler, who we exposed last year for making potentially dangerous claims about his cannabis oil products, has now expanded into peptides

Fowler, 35, won Commonwealth Games gold in 2014 and boxed for Team GB at Rio 2016

Channa Jayasena, a professor of medicine at Imperial College London, told us that it was ‘deeply worrying’ to see people, desperate to lose weight but unable to access prescription-only drugs, being offered unlicensed products.

Jayasena, a professor of reproductive endocrinology which deals with hormone and fertility issues, said: ‘This could put people's lives at risk. You have to make peptides using very strong chemicals and then purify them using more strong chemicals.

'These chemicals are highly toxic and they are purified under incredibly rigorous conditions and standards, that need to be kept. My concern is that these are black market synthesised peptides, which have potential impurity and no guarantee of what is inside them.’

A major investigation by the Daily Mail into ‘DIY Ozempic’ sellers earlier this year found that peptides – the active ingredient in licensed weight-loss drugs – were being sold to people to make cheap home-use kits without the legally required medical checks or monitoring. Scientists told us that customers didn’t know what they were buying or whether the advised dosage was safe.

Potential harms include increased cancer risk and damage to organs. Huge demand for weight-loss injections – now believed to be used by around 2.5 million Britons – has fuelled a booming black market.

Liverpool-based Fowler, who continues to use retired professional footballers Paul Merson, Chris Kirkland, Matt Le Tissier, John Aldridge and Emile Heskey to promote his cannabis oil products, is openly claiming on his social media channels that his peptides should be taken for weight loss. In a post last month he claimed to have 'a lab I use in London’ which tested them. Aldridge and Heskey have been promoting his weight-loss claims.

One of Fowler’s Instagram posts depicts a chiselled man bearing a six pack beside a fat man scoffing food, and declares of the health safety authorities: ‘They don’t want you having whats good for you (sic).’

Since setting up his peptides business, which he registered at Companies House in June, Fowler has fallen foul of Instagram rules and the platform suspended his account last month, depriving him of a key way of getting orders and issuing payment instructions to customers. He told his followers that Instagram had ‘grassed' and ‘banned’ him and that he was ‘absolutely fuming’.

Former professional footballer Emile Heskey has been promoting Fowler's Supreme CBD products

One product pictured on Fowler’s Supreme Peptides website – Tesamorelin, used in the US by HIV patients and people looking to shed abdominal fat – is not an MHRA-authorised medicine

The ex-boxer set up an alternative account but Instagram has continued to prevent him from responding to customers’ direct messages. From his sun lounger on holiday, Fowler told his followers on August 27 that his DMs were working, only to state in a later post that he was being ‘harassed’ because they were blocked ‘yet again’.

Amid his Instagram difficulties, Fowler directed followers to the account of an ‘Anthony Lloyd’ whose WhatsApp profile picture is the Supreme Peptides brand, telling them this person would ‘look after you if you want to LOSE WE*IGHT or get in shape’.
