World.title: Another beluga whale sent from Marineland to Chicago's Shedd Aquarium has died
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Shedd Aquarium in Chicago says two whales have died after it took in 10 beluga whales from Marineland in Niagara Falls, Ont.

Shedd says one whale, Rain, came from Marineland in mid-August while the other, Beethoven, was already a resident.

Marineland, along with Shedd and several other aquariums, recently completed an unprecedented relocation of captive whales after shipping 30 belugas and four dolphins to five destinations.

Another Marineland beluga, Peekachu, died last week after it became severely dehydrated.

Shedd says the deaths occurred Wednesday afternoon despite immediately trying to save the whales.

The aquarium says it does not know if the deaths are related, but they are performing tests and necropsies.

World.title: Canadian missing after Nepal flooding found safe, Anand says
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand says one of the 30 Canadian citizens and permanent residents missing after catastrophic flooding in Nepal's border region with China has been found safe.

She says the individual was unreachable due to communication outages and was able to establish contact Tuesday.

The flash flooding struck one week ago after a glacier collapsed in the Himalayan border region between Nepal and China.

WATCH | A glimpse of flood devastation: Drone video reveals flood devastation in Devighat, Nepal | Duration 0:54 Drone footage from Wednesday shows skeletal remains of homes and mud-caked debris in the Nepalese town of Devighat, which sits on the banks of the Trishuli river, after deadly flash floods tore through the region last week.

More than 1,100 people were killed and more than 3,900 are missing.

Nepal's Foreign Ministry says about 590 foreign nationals from 39 countries remain unaccounted for.

Anand says Canada will be sending more than 18,000 emergency items from Canadian Red Cross stockpiles to the area in addition to the $5 million Ottawa has already pledged in humanitarian aid.

World.title: 'My students should be here': Tumbler Ridge teacher shares toll of deadly B.C. school shooting
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

One of the teachers caught in the deadly school shooting at Tumbler Ridge Secondary has shared her story publicly for the first time, describing a "dark cloud" lingering over her hometown in the weeks and months following the tragedy.

Deidre Rushlow is one of the plaintiffs in a series of lawsuits filed this week in California against OpenAI, alleging the company's ChatGPT platform was used to help plan the shooting, which left eight victims, including five students and an educator at the school, dead.

Along with the lawsuit, Rushlow issued a written statement through the Canadian lawyers representing her in the case. In it, she says she is "haunted by the memory" of the day, calling it "a wound that sears with unending pain for my entire community."

Her letter is a rare insight into what people who were at Tumbler Ridge Secondary experienced, with the town's leaders asking for privacy as they recover from the tragedy.

"My name is Deidre Rushlow. Up until February 10, 2026, I was the English and Humanities teacher at Tumbler Ridge Secondary School. My students were in the library when the shooting happened. I did not know, nor could I know, that when I sent them to the library with my educational assistant, they were living their final moments," the statement begins.

Youth in Tumbler Ridge memorialize the victims of February's mass shooting, writing names and messages on a wall in the community's downtown. (Tom Summer/CBC)

Rushlow says she was in her first year of full-time teaching, having previously attended and graduated from the school before becoming a substitute.

"When I finally got the keys to my very own classroom last summer, I scrubbed each corner clean, added personal touches to brighten it up, and spent days organizing it until every last detail was perfect for my students," she writes.

"That same classroom has now been reduced to a pile of dust, all of my supplies and decorations packed into boxes and stored somewhere unknown to me. The career that once brought me such joy now terrifies me in ways I never imagined possible. How can I ever be responsible for another parent’s child again?"

WATCH | Remembering the victims of the Tumbler Ridge shooting: RCMP identify all 8 victims of shooting in Tumbler Ridge, B.C. | Duration 4:37





"My students should be here getting ready for the next school year," she says. "Instead, their families, friends and classmates are left behind to suffocate in limitless grief and trauma."

Investigation ongoing as new school year begins

As the school year begins, students at Tumbler Ridge Secondary will be back in portable classrooms that were set up in the wake of the shooting.

The school itself, which housed students from grades 7 to 12, is being demolished and replaced by a new facility funded by the provincial and federal governments.

The first wing of the former Tumbler Ridge Secondary School is seen here being dismantled on Monday, Aug. 17. (Tom Summer/CBC)

The municipality is also working with those higher levels of government to develop a recovery plan and to continue offering supports to those who need it.

The police investigation into the deadly day is also ongoing, RCMP say, with a coroner's inquest planned once that is complete.

'We will not forgive, we will not forget,' teacher says

Recent scrutiny has been centred on OpenAI after it was revealed that the shooter's ChatGPT account had been flagged internally, without warning Canadian officials or law enforcement.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has since apologized and says new policies are in place to offer better protections.

WATCH | Edelson explains what's in the new lawsuits: Lawyer for Tumbler Ridge victims says OpenAI should be held accountable | Duration 9:00 Jay Edelson is the CEO of Edelson PC, the law firm representing victims and survivors of the Tumbler Ridge, B.C., shooting in a lawsuit against ChatGPT. He says one of his chief aims is to have chat-logs between the shooter and ChatGPT released.



But as part of the lawsuits filed this week though U.S. class-action firm Edelson PC, it is claimed OpenAI's leadership "ignored its own safety staff and refused to alert police," instead "choosing profit over the lives of the children of Tumbler Ridge" as it prepares to become a publicly-traded company. "

Jason Kwon, chief strategy officer at OpenAI, said in a response posted on X that those claims are false and that his team works " hard to define standards and processes for when to report cases to law enforcement and to apply those standards to really difficult and complex situations."

The lawsuits and their claims will be tested in court in California, where OpenAI is headquartered.

In her statement, Rushlow writes she wants accountability for the company.

"We will not forgive, we will not forget, and we certainly will not rest until every last individual at OpenAI who was complicit in the Tumbler Ridge shooting has been brought to justice," she says.

World.title: Dancing With The Stars announces Season 35 cast: Julia Stiles, Jenna Dewan and more to hit the ballroom floor
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

The stars have been picked. Now they just need to learn the steps.

The cast of Season 35 of Dancing With The Stars was officially announced on Wednesday, with a fresh lineup of familiar faces trading their famous day jobs for sequins, choreography and a shot at the mirror-ball trophy.

Before Wednesday's announcement on Good Morning America, Maura Higgins, Ciara Miller, Jackson Olson and Guillermo Rodriguez had already been confirmed as part of the cast.

Twelve more stars were then named to the roster on the ABC morning show — including Julia Stiles, trading in her Save The Last Dance flats and 10 Things I Hate About You acting chops for the cha-cha-cha, and The Rookie star Jenna Dewan.

With Hollywood heavyweights, social-media personalities, an Olympian, a Paralympian and even a banana stepping onto the dance floor (Savannah Bananas exhibition baseball player Jackson Olson), it's shaping up to be one very busy ballroom.

The show, which airs in Canada on Disney+, will have a double premiere on Sept. 15 and 16.

Here's the full cast and the professional dancers they've been paired with:

Tatyana Ali (Fresh Prince of Bel Air) and Jan Ravnik

Jan Ravnik and Tatyana Ali. (Disney/Andrew Eccles)

Fans have thoughts

Fans on social media have voiced mixed opinions of the lineup.

That includes casting Dewan, who, unlike many others in the lineup, has an extensive dance background. Before starring in the 2006 dance film Step Up, Dewan worked as a backup dancer for stars including Janet Jackson, Missy Elliott and Christina Aguilera.

Harry Shum Jr., also brings a ton of dance experience to the cast. He's performed alongside major artists like Beyoncé, Mariah Carey, Jennifer Lopez and Madonna, before going on to star in several films in the Step Up franchise.

"That advantage is crazy," one user wrote on X .

"DIABOLICAL. Give someone else a chance 😭," another said.

But other fans were quick to praise the choice of incoming ballroom competitors, particularly Julia Stiles.

"That’s literally MOTHER. This partnership is going to change lives," one user declared on X. "yeah so this is my team," said another.

A new pro and a family connection

The upcoming season will be the first to feature the winner of Dancing With The Stars: The Next Pro, Adele Zaikman. The competition was hosted by last season's mirror-ball champion and wildlife conservationist Robert Irwin.

This season also marks a big moment for Hailey Bills and the start of a potential fun family feud.

After spending Season 34 as a troupe member on the show, Bills has been promoted to pro and will be part of the third same-sex pairing in Dancing With the Stars history.

Bills is also no stranger to the show’s ballroom — she’s the niece of pro Jenna Johnson, who is married to fellow pro Val Chmerkovskiy.

World.title: Air Canada Express flight attendants vote on strike mandate as contract talks stall
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Flight attendants who work on Air Canada Express flights are voting on whether to authorize strike action as their union says bargaining talks have stalled.

The Canadian Flight Attendant Union, which represents around 1,000 flight attendants, says it's seeking a strike mandate after being unable to reach an agreement with Jazz Aviation on "the most critical issues" despite nine months of negotiations and enlisting the services of a mediator.

"The CFAU believes a strong strike mandate from its membership is necessary to ensure Jazz Aviation understands the seriousness of the outstanding issues and the resolve of its members," the news release said.

A spokesperson for Jazz Aviation said the company remains committed to reaching an agreement at the bargaining table "without disruption to its operations."

The company is seeking out the appointment of a conciliation officer as negotiations with the Canadian Flight Attendant Union have reached an impasse, the spokesperson said in an email.

Jazz Aviation serves as the primary operator for Air Canada Express flights. It is not owned by Air Canada but by a holding company called Chorus.

Union says pay among key issues

Chris Schliep, the union's vice-president, said the parties have made progress on some items over the past few months but that significant issues remain unresolved.

The main outstanding issues for the union include wages, compensation for work performed on the ground and "improvements that recognize the impact this job has on our members' lives," Schliep said in an email.

"Jazz flight attendants have not kept pace with comparable flight attendants at other Canadian airlines, particularly in light of the recent agreements reached across the industry.

"We believe these are reasonable issues that need to be addressed. Our members are asking for an agreement that properly recognizes the work they actually do and the responsibility they carry."

The union also wants its members recognized as safety professionals for the work they perform completing checks, attending briefings and boarding passengers, he said.

The importance of safety was highlighted in March after the fatal accident involving Air Canada Express Flight AC8646 at LaGuardia Airport, which killed both pilots, the news release says.

"Safety does not begin at takeoff, nor does it end at landing," said Marsha Walters, president of the Canadian Flight Attendant Union, in the news release.

"It begins with fair working conditions, proper rest, and respect for the flight attendants who are responsible for the safety and care of passengers every day."

WATCH | Former WestJet flight attendant on why she left industry: Former flight attendant on why she quit the industry | Duration 5:10 Calleigh Gingras is a former flight attendant who has been a vocal critic on social media about issues within the airline industry. She says she is not shocked by news of a possible strike by WestJet flight attendants and that despite loving the job, the pay for the working conditions, including many hours of unpaid work, was 'not sustainable' for her.

Voting closes on Friday at noon. The vote comes just weeks after WestJet flight attendants went on strike and a little over a year after more than 10,000 Air Canada flight attendants did the same.

It's unclear when Air Canada Express flight attendants could walk off the job if they vote in favour of a strike mandate.

World.title: Pentagon makes testosterone screening mandatory for U.S. service members effective immediately
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

The ​U.S. Pentagon issued detailed guidance on Wednesday for a new, mandatory testosterone deficiency screening policy for active-duty and reserve service members age 30 and older, ‌a follow-up to a July announcement from U.S. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth.

The guidance, which is effective immediately, establishes standardized screening and treatment pathways for men and women that ​the Pentagon says are aimed at ​improving military readiness by identifying and managing hormonal and energy-availability issues.

Hegseth, who has promoted the use of ​testosterone, announced the mandate last month, raising questions ⁠among experts about whether ⁠there was a ‌scientific basis for such a policy. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration plans to hold a meeting of experts to discuss medical use of testosterone in ⁠mid-September.

According to the guidance, men age 30 and older will receive mandatory testosterone blood tests, while younger men will be tested ‌only on request or if clinicians identify warning signs.

For women, the guidance does not mandate routine testosterone blood tests, but it calls for screening for ​fatigue and disrupted menstrual cycles that can be associated with hormonal dysregulation and ⁠conditions called low-energy availability and relative energy deficiency in sport.

The ⁠document lays out guidelines for when it is appropriate to ⁠prescribe ⁠off-label testosterone in ​women, namely for postmenopausal women with unusually low sexual desire.

Doctors have ​raised concerns ⁠that broad testosterone testing could lead to unnecessary, or potentially harmful, treatment, saying there is little evidence that universal screening for low testosterone among military personnel would improve U.S. combat readiness.

World.title: De la Espriella claims Colombia’s military killed 23, arrested 6 EMC guerrillas
World.content:
President Abelardo de la Espriella claimed Wednesday that Colombia’s armed forces killed at least 23 members of FARC dissident group EMC and captured another six.

In a video, De la Espriella said that “Operation Azarias,” targeted the EMC’s Carolina Ramirez Front and killed one of its commanders, a man called “Tigre” or “Pintado,” in the south of the Guaviare province.

A second guerrilla commander, “Victor,” was among the six alleged EMC members who were arrested during the operation, which included air strikes.

The president claimed that Victor carried out attacks against the military “during the elections, as part of the ‘gunpoint vote’ strategy launched by the previous regime to skew the popular verdict.”

That narcoterrorist, whom we have now taken out of circulation, carried out attacks against members of the National Army and the Navy. During the elections, as part of the “gunpoint vote” strategy launched by the previous regime to skew the popular verdict, this criminal ambushed a unit that was on the move precisely to protect citizens’ right to vote freely. President Abelardo de la Espriella

There is no evidence to suggest that De la Espriella’s predecessor, former President Gustavo Petro, employed illegal armed groups to coerce voters into voting against his would-be successor.

One minor allegedly survived the attack and was surrendered to family welfare agency ICBF. The Medical Examiner’s Office is expected to investigate how many minors were among the alleged “narcoterrorists.”

At least three minors were killed in a previous operation in Guaviare that killed at least nine alleged members of the EMC’s main rival, FARC dissident group EMBF, the Medical Examiner’s Office said earlier this week.

Air strikes against illegal armed groups are controversial as they could imply the blanket killing of victims of child recruitment, a war crime according to international humanitarian law.

The government has long insisted that those recruiting children and minors are responsible for the deaths of their victims.

World.title: 1 killed, 15 injured in northeast Colombia car bomb attack on police station
World.content:
At least one person was killed and another 15 injured in a car bomb attack on a police station on the outskirts of Cucuta, the capital of Norte de Santander.

According to the National Police, the bomb exploded on Monday evening outside of the police station in Los Patios, a municipality that is part of Cucuta’s metropolitan area.

Apart from the casualties, the blast also damaged buildings and vehicles that were parked near the police station, police told local media.

In an initial response, President Abelardo de la Espriella said on social media platform X that he had convened a security council meeting “with the entire top brass of the security forces.”

“Wherever the terrorists try to sow fear, that is where the State will be with all is might,” said De la Espriella.

We will pursue with an iron fist those who threaten Colombians, until we capture them, dismantle their networks, and restore peace to our communities. Abelardo de la Espriella

In the region around Cucuta, guerrilla organizations ELN and EMBF have been fighting each other. Organized crime groups operate mainly inside the urban area of the capital of the Norte de Santander province.

No group immediately claimed responsibility for the attack.

World.title: Vote to move Uribe’s massacre probe to Congress triggers infighting among Colombia’s left
World.content:
Internal fractures within Colombia’s leftist opposition burst into the open following a vote by five representatives of the Historic Pact (PH) party to transfer a criminal investigation against former President Alvaro Uribe to Congress’ Accusations Commission.

The controversy erupted after the five PH members of the committee backed a motion of Uribe’s Democratic Center (CD) party to assert legislative jurisdiction over long-standing criminal cases against Uribe, including investigations into the massacres of El Aro (1997) and La Granja (1996), and the 1998 assassination of human rights defender Jesus Maria Valle.

PH members

David Alejandro Toro

María del Mar Pizarro

Heráclito Landínez

Jorge Bastidas

Gabriel Becerra

As the former governor of Antioquia, Uribe would have been in on the massacres carried out by the Bloque Metro and AUC paramilitary groups, according to the Prosecutor General’s Office, which refused to turn over the investigations.

The commission claimed jurisdiction over the Uribe file because the paramilitaries didn’t demobilize until after 2002, when he became president.

Critics of the decision, including the prosecution and PH Senate chief Ivan Cepeda, argued that Uribe’s alleged involvement in the crimes happened years before he was granted presidential immunity.

Cepeda spent much of his career fighting Uribe in court over his alleged ties to the AUC.

Because of the committee vote, the Constitutional Court will have to rule on who gets to investigate Uribe’s alleged crimes against humanity, which could delay the investigation.

Journalists who reported on the PH support for the fabricated conflict suggested that this may be part of a political deal between congressmen political deal between Uribistas and Petristas, supporters of former President Gustavo Petro.

Becerra, who is close to Cepeda, said in a statement that there “existed nor will there exist any political deal that would compromise justice, truth or the rights of victims.

According to the house representative, the PH lawmakers “initially considered it reasonable and legally appropriate to clarify the jurisdiction of the authority responsible for conducting the investigation,” but changed their mind in response to the controversy and calls for their resignation.

Lawyer Miguel Angel del Rio, the victims representative in the Uribe case, told Tercer Canal that “the ethic committee of the Historic Pact should investigate these five congressman,” adding that “what we have here is solidarity with impunity and this cannot be allowed.”

The Historic Pact became Colombia’s largest political party after congressional elections in March, but has seen an increase in internal tensions after Cepeda’s failure to win the presidential election in June.

World.title: Finance minister presents Colombia’s $203B budget proposal
World.content:
Colombia’s Finance Minister Miguel Gomez presented a budget proposal of COP634.9 trillion ($203 billion) for the coming year, a 14% increase compared to last year.

Much of the increase is due to the government’s debt obligations, which went up 55% to 155.4 trillion ($49.8 billion), almost a quarter of the entire budget.

At a presentation, Gomez told press that an earthquake that left tens of thousands homeless in western Colombia earlier this month also forced the administration of Abelardo de la Espriella to increase spending.

In a video, the finance minister also said that the government “has taken deci

The budget bill, a revision of the one that was presented by the former government of former President Gustavo Petro, will have to be approved by Congress before October 20 or be issued as a decree.

The government will also present a Finance Bill, which determines how the government plans to pay for its spending, before December.

World.title: Colombia claims killing eight suspected EMBF guerrillas
World.content:
President Abelardo de la Espriella said Thursday that Colombia’s armed forces killed eight guerrillas of FARC dissident group EMBF in a joint operation.

In a post on social media platform X, De la Espriella said that the military offensive targeted “camps used by structures of the Jorge Suarez Briceño Block,” a unit of the EMBF, in a rural part of El Retorno in the Guaviare province.

In a precision airstrike followed by an operation carried out by our commandos, the preliminary tally shows that 8 terrorists have been killed so far, 11 rifles and 5 machine guns have been seized, along with a large amount of logistical supplies. President Abelardo de la Espriella

De la Espriella said that “Colombia must know we are going on the offensive” against organized crime and illegal armed groups that are all deemed “narco-terrorist” organizations by the government.

“Major ringleaders and their criminal organizations will find no hiding place or sanctuary anywhere in the country,” the president added.

De la Espriella took office earlier this month, vowing to end peace negotiations with illegal armed groups and go on a military offensive with the help of the US military instead.

One of the groups that was negotiating peace with the administration of former President Gustavo Petro was the EMBF, led by former FARC commander “Calarca.”

The group, together with FARC dissident group EMC, controls large swathe of territory in southern Colombia and along the border with Venezuela.

World.title: De la Espriella calls for “iron fist” against crime in Colombia
World.content:
Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella called on the security forces to impose the law “like a giant with an iron fist, the iron fist of the State.”

During a meeting with commanders of the security forces, De la Espriella stressed that security “is the cornerstone of our government and the most forceful government policy.”

The president urged the security forces to confront crime with an iron fist and stressed that “our soldiers and police officers have the full and unconditional support of this government. Never again will they be mistreated or forced to bow down to crime.”

Here we must act like a giant with an iron fist—the iron fist of the state. And that ability to convey a sense of unity is what has a psychological impact on crime and sends a clear message to citizens: we are here to protect you, to look out for you, but also to enforce the law. President Abelardo de la Espriella

De la Espriella called to erase the distinction between organized crime and illegal armed groups, and “treat them all under a single designation, which is that of terrorist groups,” claiming they are interconnected.

We have to stop treating these criminals differently. We must treat them all under a single designation, which is that of terrorist groups, because the criminal pyramid we have in Colombia—whose base is drug trafficking, followed by illegal mining, extortion, and smuggling—is all perfectly interconnected. The foundation of all crime and the primary source of all forms of violence is drug trafficking. President Abelardo de la Espriella

“When it comes to fighting crime, there are no differences—neither in the state’s actions nor in its response and certainly not in the categorization” that allowed peace talks with groups like the FARC and ELN, according to the president.

“That is over in this administration. They are all terrorists, and we are going to treat them as such, no matter what happens,” said De la Espriella.

World.title: De la Espriella claims 123,700 barrels stolen monthly from Colombia’s state oil company
World.content:
Oil thieves from north Colombia would be stealing at least 123,700 barrel of gasoline, diesel and naphtha, a month, claimed President Abelardo de la Espriella.

According to De la Espriella, the theft of the refined oil products that wee imported or produced by state-owned oil company Ecopetrol “is utterly alarming, and demands an immediate and forceful response from the State.”

Every month, approximately 123,700 barrels of refined products—gasoline, diesel, and naphtha—imported or produced by Ecopetrol would be stolen. This would occur solely on a 14-inch pipeline that connects Pozos Colorados, in Santa Marta, to the interior of the country, and the losses are concentrated mainly in Cesar and Magdalena. President Abelardo de la Espriella

“We would be talking about more than 1.5 million barrels a year, with losses exceeding $500,000 million for Ecopetrol and, therefore, for the nation,” the president said in a post on social media platform X.

De la Espriella added that “these fuels are used as raw materials in the illicit processing of cocaine” by illegal armed groups that operate in the country’s periphery.

If we confirm that a large portion of this fuel is being used to power cocaine production facilities, then we are not only dealing with a massive theft from Ecopetrol: we are dealing with a criminal network that may be linking the theft of hydrocarbons to drug trafficking and the financing of armed terrorist organizations. President Abelardo de la Espriella

The president ordered a “joint operation” of the military, police, prosecution and administrative authorities “to comprehensively combat this criminal economy” led by Defense Minister Jorge Eduardo Mora.

“I want results and periodic report on progress,” said De la Espriella.

Organized crime and illegal armed groups have been involved in fuel theft for decades.

World.title: Media concentration in Colombia
World.content:
Listen to this episode on Spotify

Colombia’s corporate media have played a dubious role in the history of the country and have concentrated an immense power for their owners.
